News.title: Bizarre moment half-naked woman in underwear & flip flops snatches milk bottles from family’s doorstep
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a woman snatches milk from her neighbour’s doorstep – wearing only her underwear.

CCTV footage shows the semi-naked thief sneaking up to the property and swiping two bottles of milk in a 5am dawn dash on July 17.



Wearing only flip-flops, black knickers and a crop top, the brazen milk snatcher then makes a getaway.

The neighbour was shocked to find her milk delivery had vanished that morning – and even more startled when she checked her doorbell footage.



The homeowner said: “We were very frustrated to see it on our doorbell as have two young children, but you hope it’s someone in such desperate need they resort to stealing.

“Why in her underwear we do not know!



“Makes us think twice about getting milk delivered as it has happened several times in our area recently.”

The baffled mum from Bearwood, in the West Midlands, uploaded screengrabs of the footage to Facebook.



Similar reports of dairy theft soon flooded in.

One user wrote: “What’s thong with people!”

Another said: “It’s Maggie Thatcher’s relative.”

One joked: “No milk left and wanted her Weetabix!”

West Midlands Police said it received a report of milk being stolen at 5.10am on Friday, July 17.



The suspect has yet to be identified.

Its statement said: “Anyone with any information is asked to contact 101 or use the Live Chat option on our website quoting crime number 20/328342/26.”

It follows a fierce feud in April between two neighbours who were battling over a household bin in South London.

News.title: Trainee pilot dies after celebrating first solo flight with oil drenching ritual that sparked fatal allergic reaction
News.content:
A PILOT died after a bizarre ‘oil bath’ ritual celebrating his first solo flight triggered a fatal anaphylactic shock.

Gustavo Henrique Lara, 27, suffered the fatal reaction at an event held to mark the end of his eight-year-long aviation training in southern Brazil.



Lara was covered in aircraft engine oil from the neck down at the Ponta Grossa flight school in the southern state of Parana on July 16.

He died after suffering a seizure and three cardiac arrests.



Just an hour before the tragedy, Lara had posted a photo of the plane he flew in and chillingly wrote: “Today could be the best day of my pilot training so far.”

A man has been arrested for manslaughter after turning himself in to the cops.

He has been identified locally as a flight instructor at the school and was subsequently released on bail.

There is no evidence to suggest the instructor, who had insisted Lara was only covered from the neck down, had any intention of killing him.

Lara began complaining of dizziness following the wild ritual and soon after it became clear that something was seriously wrong, a witness said.

They continued: “He was having a lot of difficulty breathing.



“Then we rushed over to try to do something, started shouting to call the ambulance, to call for help from the helicopter crew as well, who were right there nearby.”

Lara’s friends and family have paid tribute to him as a “beautiful boy” who will be deeply missed.

His cousin Barbara Giacomitti said: “Gustavo was a dreamer and, above all, a hard worker.

“He achieved everything through his own merit. His greatest dream was always aviation.

“He dedicated years and years to it.



“In fact, he practically lived in the sky.”

“It is an irreparable loss. There will never be another like him.

“But how fortunate we were to have been among the lucky ones. He left too soon, but God needs the best by His side, and he was the best.”

An investigation has been launched into his shock death.

The oil bath is a traditional baptism ritual at many flight schools in Brazil.



It is performed on student pilots to celebrate a major milestone in their careers, such as their first solo flight, and marks their entry into the community of pilots.

Police chief Lucas Petry said: “Gustavo’s close friends have said he had been very excited about that day, that he had been talking about it for a month and had invited everyone to be part of that moment.”

Brazil’s National Civil Aviation Agency (ANAC) have said they condemn the use of oil and lubricants in celebration rituals.

ANAC said: ““ANAC warns that aviation chemicals, such as aviation oils and lubricants, should under no circumstances come into contact with the skin, as indicated on the labels of these materials.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It is essential to rethink rituals marking the completion of training stages and ensure that any celebration is conducted responsibly, without exposing students, instructors, or third parties to risk.”



The Agency extended their sympathies to his family, friends, and everyone who knew him.

News.title: Brit attempted murder suspect ‘who tried to slit tourist’s throat’ is arrested after reaching Tenerife on flight from UK
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

IN CUFFS Brit attempted murder suspect ‘who tried to slit tourist’s throat’ is arrested after reaching Tenerife on flight from UK

A BRITISH murder suspect who allegedly tried to slit a man’s throat has been arrested in Tenerife moments after landing from Liverpool.

An arrest warrant for the 46-year-old man had previously been issued before Spanish cops cuffed him on suspicion of the December attack.



The man was detained after landing in the holiday hotspot for allegedly slitting another Brit’s throat at a tourist complex in Adeje, Tenerife.

The victim suffered serious injuries to his body and neck but managed to survive.



National Police in Tenerife confirmed today: “Officers have arrested a man at Tenerife South–Reina Sofía Airport following his arrival on a flight from Liverpool for the alleged commission of the crime of attempted homicide.

“The detainee was subject to a warrant for the crime.



“The events took place in December last year at a complex located in the municipality of Adeje.”

They added: “The victim suffered multiple attacks with a large bladed weapon to vital areas, including the neck.

“He survived thanks to the intervention of a witness.

“The person allegedly responsible for these acts managed to flee, so the investigation has remained open ever since.



“In addition, he has several pending cases for reckless driving, assault on law enforcement officers, and causing bodily harm.”

Police did not disclose the nationality of the man arrested in an official statement released, but well-placed sources confirmed both he and his alleged victim are British nationals.

It is still unclear why the near-fatal stabbing late last year took place.

It comes after a cyclist was killed in what was described as a “deliberate” hit-and-run in Tenerife in December.

Police were alerted in the municipality of Arona in the south of the holiday island.



The victim was cycling on the TF-652 road between Las Chafiras and the fishing village of Las Galletas.

News.title: Andy Burnham weighing up bringing back 50p tax rate for wealthy workers in bid to balance budget
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has opened the door to a manifesto-busting tax hike in a bid to shore up the “difficult” state of the public finances.

The new Prime Minister refused to knock back the chance of bringing back the 50p top rate of tax to help ease financial pressures on low earners and pensioners.



His intervention came just after he arrived in Downing Street after vowing to give people some breathing space as they grapple with high bills.

But the Labour manifesto says the party will not raise income tax, VAT or national insurance.



He was pushed over re-introducing the 50p rate as a way of paying for potentially raising the personal allowance which has been frozen at £12,570 for five years.

He said: “Certainly, I heard issues related to the personal allowance more than anything on doorsteps in Makerfield.



“I think it’s been frozen now, hasn’t it for a number of years, so it has dragged more people in – pensioners, I think – and that particularly I think has become a growing issue.

“So all of this will be looked at though at the budget, and obviously it’s difficult given the financial circumstances in which we find ourselves.

“But I wanted to recognise the point because it’s challenging for people and it’s people on the lowest incomes perhaps who’ve most been affected by that.

“So it’s an issue that I’m just kind of showing I have a visibility of the issue and the impact it’s had on the different groups that I’ve mentioned, but it’s difficult because changing the threshold is not without significant consequences. But I’m looking at it.”



The 50p rate was brought in by Gordon Brown but then cut to 45p under the coalition government in 2013.

It comes after he told Gary Lineker in an interview that his government may have “to ask for a little more” tax.

When quizzed further on whether the 50p rate was one of the things he was looking at, he said: “I think that would be just premature to say that. I’ve barely got my feet under the table.”

Mr Burnham also stopped short of giving firm details on using the National Wealth Fund to fund cash going into infrastructure projects.

The fund is financed through taxation and borrowing which could lead to jitters in the money markets.



When asked whether doing more within the existing fiscal rules set out by Chancellor Rachel Reeves, he said he would use the “flexibility” within them.

He added: “But we will stick to the existing rules and I’ve made that very clear in Downing Street. So none of this is about taking risks with the economy. I’ve never done that in any role that I’ve had.

Mr Burnham added that he has always taken a “prudent approach”. He added: “We will show how it will be funded and that will be clearly set out in our budget.”

Speaking on the steps of Downing Street, he spoke of helping out more Brits in an effort to beat the cost of living squeeze.

He could bring down energy bills, reduce bus fares to £2 or even help workers ease the pain with rent controls.



He said: “We are looking at measures that could make a difference this year. So we are looking at all of those things but we will make more announcements tomorrow.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We’re just finalising the details. It’s premature to say it will be any one of those particular things. We just want to do some things that people will feel and feel quite quickly.

“It won’t solve everything, it won’t take all of the pressure off but it just shows the direction of travel and that we’re serious about helping them out.”

News.title: Hosepipe ban loopholes mean people can still water trees or fill up a pond – as FOUR new regions hit by restrictions
News.content:
HOSEPIPE ban loopholes could mean Brits can still water their trees or fill up a pond despite strict restrictions being put in place.

It comes as four regions are set to be hit with new rules this week in a move that will affect millions of households.

South East Water has said 2.4million customers will be affected by temporary restrictions in Sussex, Surrey, Hampshire and Berkshire from Saturday.



The ban had already been in place just for its customers in parts of Kent.



On Friday, Affinity Water and Cambridge Water announced similar measures.

The move affects residents living in Central region, covering Bedfordshire, Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, Essex, Hertfordshire, Surrey and parts of London.

Water suppliers are asking customers to cut back water use straight away, telling them not to use hosepipes for their gardens, cars, patios, boats or swimming pools.

Under the Temporary Use Ban put in place, however, you can use a hosepipe to water trees, saplings, whips, and hedging planted within the last three years.

This exemption applies only if using a watering can is not a practical alternative.

Under a hosepipe ban, given the “very high level” of demand for drinking water, residents cannot use hosepipes or sprinklers to water gardens, wash cars, or fill up swimming and paddling pools.

Breaking these rules can see homeowners fined for £1,000, which is enforced by the water company.



Similarly, if you have a pool or pond with any fish or aquatic life living in it, you can use a hosepipe to make sure it is topped up.

This rule is the same for ornamental fountains if they are used to oxygenate a fish pond – however, this is not the case if it is purely decorational.

However, the ban does not limit essential uses, including watering lawns for specific reasons, and filling up ponds.

Individuals who have newly-laid turf in their garden are able to water their lawns for a restricted period of time, typically 28 days, then transitioning to a watering can. This allows the newly-installed lawn to establish roots, preventing the grass from drying out completely.

News.title: Ryanair CEO breaks silence on potential cause of terrifying cabin window smash that saw passenger nearly sucked out
News.content:
RYANAIR’S CEO has broken his silence after a smashed cabin window saw a terrified passenger “sucked up to his shoulders” out of the aircraft.

Michael O’Leary said initial findings suggest that “foreign object damage” caused the incident – not the age or servicing conditions of the aircraft.



The Boeing 737-800 was travelling from Thessaloniki, Greece, to Memmingen, Germany, when passenger Ljubiša Karović, 61, was pulled through the window at 20,000ft.

Ljubiša was hospitalised with severe injuries after instant depressurisation sucked him into the gap, exposing his head and neck to brutal 370mph winds.



His wife, Svetlana, was able to grab hold of Ljubiša just in time, preventing him from being torn out of the aircraft.

In a harrowing admission, she told Serbian outlet Nova: “I reacted immediately and grabbed his legs. I thought: ‘If we die, we die together.’ It was horrible.”

Three brave bystanders then helped to pull back Ljubiša into the aircraft, which left the window exposed.

One witness told Radio Thessaloniki: “A noise was heard as if a tire had burst.



“There was panic with screams and voices because we immediately lost altitude from the decompression.

“For a moment I thought someone had accidentally opened the emergency door.

Another passenger told the outlet: “They grabbed him and held him down, fortunately he hadn’t taken off his seatbelt.

“His head was completely outside the plane. The girls who were next to him were pulling him. Some doctors also went to help him.”

Ljubiša was left wounded following the five-minute nightmare and suffered burns.



O’Leary said: “Initial indication would suggest it looks like a foreign object damage to the engine on takeoff at Thessaloniki, but we don’t have, we can’t say that definitively.”

He told analysts that despite the aircraft being 18 years old, its engine had been refurbished and fully serviced in the last two years.

O’Leary said that a draft report on the incident would be released within 28 days, followed by an in-depth report.



If the damage was caused by an external object, it would reduce Boeing’s and Ryanair‘s responsibility for the incident.

Following the horror incident, the couple’s lawyer, Vasilis Tsiaras, told The Sun how they desperately tried to stuff luggage into the gap.

He said: “There was a big hole that they tried to seal with a suitcase, which was a little bit soft and was sucked from the plane.

“They tried to do the same with more of a tough suitcase and managed to stop the flow of the air.”

Tsiaras also claimed the same aircraft encountered a technical problem only the day before the incident.



The lawyer alleged the plane had been forced to return to Thessaloniki airport shortly after taking off for Sarajevo, Bosnia.

He said: “At this time we cannot claim that the two incidents are connected, however there is a strong suspicion that the problem is related to engine maintenance, as that is where it all seems to have started.”

The airline claimed that the incident was caused by a disruptive passenger, who had to be returned to the airport and removed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The US National Transportation Safety Board is currently investigating the latest incident.

News.title: When is Andy Burnham’s first PMQs? How to watch the new PM face Prime Minister’s Questions
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has entered Downing Street as Britain’s new Prime Minister following the resignation of Sir Keir Starmer.

The former Mayor of Greater Manchester was formally appointed by King Charles III at Buckingham Palace on Monday (July 20), making him the nation’s seventh Prime Minister in a decade.

With a brand-new cabinet to assemble and major policy shifts on the agenda, his first time facing Prime Minister’s Questions (PMQs) is certain to be an interesting one.



When is Andy Burnham’s first PMQs?

Voters will have to wait a little longer to see Burnham at his first PMQs, and he will not be facing a grilling this Wednesday (July 22).



While incoming leaders usually face MPs almost immediately, the timing of this political transition means that’s not possible.

The House of Commons officially rose for its summer recess on Thursday, July 16.

Because Parliament is on holiday, there are no scheduled Commons sittings, debates, or PMQs taking place this week.

Instead, Burnham’s first official PMQs is scheduled for Wednesday, September 2, 2026, at 12pm, when MPs return to Westminster.

This creates a gap of almost seven weeks between a Prime Minister taking office and facing parliamentary scrutiny.

Opposition politicians have called on the government to recall Parliament to hold the new PM to account, but so far no extra sittings have been scheduled.

What to expect

When September 2 rolls around, expect fireworks at the despatch box.



As head of the government, Burnham will face intense grilling from Opposition Leader Kemi Badenoch, as well as backbench MPs and party rivals.

Key topics expected to feature during his maiden appearance range from tax and the economy to domestic policy.

Opposition MPs are set to zero in on how he plans to fund expansive public spending proposals amid tight national finances and high public debt.

He is also likely to face questioning over his domestic agenda, including pledges to scrap mandatory digital IDs, bring energy and water suppliers back into public ownership, and support new North Sea oil and gas extraction.

His ambitious plan for No10 North is also sure to spark debate, alongside questions on how he intends to plug gaps in national defence spending and manage international commitments.



Burnham is a seasoned political operator, having served as Health Secretary, Chief Secretary to the Treasury, and Mayor of Greater Manchester.

Known for a plain-speaking, approachable communication style, he built a strong national profile outside the “Westminster bubble”.

But the House of Commons remains a notoriously hostile arena.

Returning to the rapid-fire pressure of the despatch box after nearly a decade away will be a major test of his political authority.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

How can I watch PMQs?

PMQs takes place every sitting Wednesday at 12pm, and lasts for roughly 30 to 45 minutes.



You can stream it directly from Parliament TV, and the official UK Parliament YouTube channel also streams the full session.

News.title: Disturbing house of horrors floor plans reveal chilling ‘hidden’ space and just one bathroom where 16 ‘feral’ kids found
News.content:
DISTURBING floor plans of the Ohio house of horrors where 16 children were found have revealed a chilling hidden space – and just one bathroom for the family of 20.

Newly uncovered county property records paint a grim picture of the cramped home where prosecutors claim the children endured years of neglect before four relatives were arrested.



According to property records from the Vinton County Auditor’s Office reviewed by Los Angeles Magazine, the century-old Hamden home at 182 Ohmer Street measures just 1,336 square feet and has only a single full bathroom despite allegedly housing 20 people.

The official floor plans also show a 518-square-foot basement beneath part of the property, although investigators have previously said reports that all 16 children lived downstairs are false.



Authorities have alleged the youngsters were instead kept confined upstairs, while neighbors and investigators said the smell of human waste, garbage and animal feces rose from the basement and spread through the house.

The sketch also reveals two first-floor additions, a front porch and a rear wooden deck, with the modest property made up of just five rooms in total, according to county records.

The home was built in 1900 and is listed as a single-family residence, the records show.

It is currently appraised at $68,670, with the building itself valued at just over $42,000.

Annual property taxes are listed at less than $1,000.

The shocking details come after Vinton County investigators entered the property on June 30 while responding to what authorities have said was an unrelated investigation.



According to prosecutors, officers discovered 16 children, aged between 18 months and 18 years, allegedly living in deplorable conditions.

Gary Siders Jr., Elizabeth Siders, Gary Siders Sr. and Christina “Lynn” Siders have each been charged with 16 felony counts of child endangering.

Prosecutors allege the children suffered prolonged neglect and abuse.



The case has since been sent to a grand jury and remains under investigation.

Law enforcement has previously described the conditions inside the home in graphic detail, while alleging the children were confined to a single room. A gag order has since been imposed on several defendants.

It comes as the children’s grandmother, Christina Siders, has filed her own request for a gag order after being charged alongside her husband, son and daughter-in-law over the alleged abuse.



According to WOWK, Christina’s attorney has asked the court to bar further public comments about her role in the case – mirroring a request already granted to her son, Gary Siders Jr.

It is not yet known whether the judge will approve the latest motion.

All four defendants have pleaded not guilty.

Gary Siders Sr. was released on a recognizance bond after suffering a medical emergency, with Vinton County Prosecutor William Archer saying his treatment “could potentially bankrupt Vinton County” if he remained in custody.

Elizabeth Siders has also asked to be released, with her attorney saying her “principal desire” is to be reunited with her children.



The latest court fight comes after records revealed the family had already come to the attention of authorities five years before the children were rescued.

Court documents obtained by NewsNation affiliate WCMH show Gary Siders Jr. and Elizabeth Siders were hit with a truancy complaint in October 2021 after six of their oldest children allegedly failed to attend a single day of school during the 2021-22 school year at Addaville Elementary School.

The case was dismissed in January 2022 after officials were unable to locate the parents, with records stating their whereabouts were unknown.

Authorities have since said the children had no school records, no medical records and no previous Child Protective Services involvement before the June 30 rescue.



Officers stumbled upon the children while executing a search warrant linked to unrelated allegations involving Gary Siders Jr., investigators said.

Authorities alleged the youngsters – aged between 18 months and 18 years old – were living in filthy conditions, with many confined to a 12ft-by-12ft area for years.

Seven children were taken to hospitals in Columbus, including two who were airlifted by helicopter, while one child was initially listed in critical condition.

Investigators also said some of the children were unable to speak, and alleged the oldest, an 18-year-old, could not write her own name.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson described what investigators found as “pure evil”, saying: “This is very, it was terrible. I mean, it looked like almost feral animals. It was terrible.”

He also alleged the children had spent most of the last four years confined to an area no larger than 12ft by 12ft, adding: “Most of our livestock was kept in better conditions than the children. It was just a disgusting scene.”

News.title: Andy Burnham live: Prime Minister's new Cabinet changes with David Lammy, Rachel Reeves and Liz Kendall OUT
News.content:
Andy Burnham's new Cabinet will look significantly different to that of Keir Starmer as high profile names, such as deputy prime minister David Lammy and Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves, have gone

Andy Burnham has already made sweeping changes - and promises - after officially being named as the new Prime Minister.

The ex-Manchester mayor has left deputy prime minister David Lammy and chancellor of the exchequer Rachel Reeves out of his Cabinet, with both politicians confirming their departures on social media this afternoon. Secretary of state for science, innovation and technology Liz Kendall has also gone.

Speaking without a lectern or notes, in a huge move away from tradition, Mr Burnham, 56, spoke for 10 minutes and used the opportunity to outline his vision for the UK. He made several vows, stressing his first action will be to set out a plan to end rough sleeping.

Minutes after this vow though, his Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government - Steve Reed OBE - quit. Mr Lammy and Ms Reeves have since said they are no longer part of Mr Burnham's Cabinet, though no replacements have officially been named.

The new leader said: "I will bring forward a new plan for Britain, a 10-year plan laying out a path from where we are now to where I believe we all want Britain to be, wherever we're coming from, whatever party we support. But I can do something to give people some breathing space now, some help with the cost of living.

"And I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them. And that work starts now. I will soon go through that door behind me and issue my first instruction to end rough sleeping in our country."

The new PM will now appoint his Cabinet throughout the afternoon, with speculation still rife surrounding the next Chancellor of the Exchequer. Peter Kyle and Liz Kendall are favourites to take the spot, but Ed Miliband has been tipped for weeks to be the next Chancellor.

News.title: 'Andy Burnham makes belter of a first impression but must act quickly to change Britain'
News.content:
First impressions matter hugely and Andy Burnham’s was a belter.

Fluent, authentic, confident, optimistic and bold to inject promised hope into many hearts was a storming first hour.

Keir Starmer departed Downing Street quietly for the final time with great dignity and pride, loyal staff and supporters wiping away tears.

Burham arrived with a loud bang, the human circuit breaker instantly showing Labour MPs and voters why faith was put in him.

‌



Watching Nigel Farage and Reform stormtroopers who wanted Starmer gone, mistakenly believing a Hard Right future was in the bag, will now be bowel-movingly nervous about what they wished for.

View Image Andy Burnham entered Downing Street earlier today

Because Burnham does walk his talk, delivering help to ease the cost of living crisis and boost living standards, and flapping Farage may well have more time to spend with other people’s money even if he survives that Clacton circus gig with a bin.

This PM’s arrival was arguably the most impressive of 10 PMs I’ve covered moving into the seat of political power, 11 if you count watching Thatcher in my teenage years. Better even than Blair or Cameron or Johnson and certainly, remember her?, Truss.

‌



Speaking without notes in a man-in-the-pub tone was a calculated risk paying handsome dividends, illustrating he’s a story teller not a script reader.

But content matters most and the balance between continuity and change will be the decider. Yes, we’ve yet to see the beef and if Burnham doesn’t live up to his self-billing jubilant Andy’s Army will stall.

The signs are good though, the recognition families yearn for a breathing space at the beginning of a 10-year plan to undo strangling privatisation and deregulation of the past four decades an attractive prospect.

Electricity, gas and water industries flogged by the Cons mutated into cash-guzzling machines screaming out for renewed public influence and ownership.

‌



Failing to replace sold council houses deprived millions of future folk affordable, secure and decent homes.

Visiting a homeless centre early morning, immediately declaring ending rough sleeping a priority, revealed an endearing compassionate core.

Admitting past personal mistakes, indeed nervousness about the job he grabbed in a bloodless coup, is also a refreshing switch from robo politicians.

Burnham, however, realises he won’t get close to 10 years every PM publicly desires and few enjoy (Blair and Thatcher were the last) if he stumbles instead of hitting the ground running in an unforgiving, febrile and fractured politics.

‌



In news we used to talk about a 24/7 cycle, every hour of every day counting. Burnham will be judged 60/60, every second of every minute, as internet mobs fuelled by poisonous disinformation, lies and X’s Fascistic trillionaire US owner Elon Musk’s divide-and-rule algorithms inciting hate and despair.

Legitimate questions deserve answers about any mandate when Burnham is the 10th of 19 post-war PMs to emerge through the Parliamentary system rather than a General Election.

Particularly when acknowledging he’s the sixth to walk up No 10 in a decade, the seventh PM since 2016 counting Cameron, signalled no early poll is on his agenda.

So that’s potentially three years as PM to transform Britain. His, Labour’s and the country’s fate may be sealed in three weeks or months.

News.title: King Charles praises Europe’s first eco-mosque during visit to Cambridge
News.content:
King Charles praises Europe’s first eco-mosque during visit to Cambridge

King Charles, who has long supported interfaith relations - has spoken with community leaders at the revolutionary mosque, which prioritises a safe place for prayer while also promoting sustainability

View 6 Images The monarch visited Cambridge Central Mosque today (Image: Chris Jackson/PA Wire)

The King has hailed Europe’s first eco-mosque as “a remarkable example of integrated faith activity” on a visit to Cambridge today.

‌



The monarch met members of the diverse community, including the mosque's imams and trustees, and other faith leaders from across the city who have joined forces to support the place of worship.

‌



The award-winning Cambridge building was designed by London-based firm Marks Barfield Architects. Julia Barfield, Director of Marks Barfield, and Timothy Winter, Chair of the Trust, Cambridge Central Mosque, accompanied The King during his visit. The King - who has been credited throughout his life with supporting interfaith relations - toured the Mosque's facilities, showing particular interest in its Community Garden.

‌



View 6 Images King Charles III shakes hands with faith leaders and community members in Cambridge (Image: Chris Jackson/PA Wire)

Charles was shown the sustainability features of the building, which include photovoltaic arrays, air-source heat pumps, a sedum roof, natural ventilation systems, and the use of timber from sustainably-managed forests. The award winning design has resulted in no air conditioning being needed for the building which was cool despite the 25 degree temperatures in the city.

Charles was taken to a side room to remove his shoes before entering the main prayer room, where he met groups from the local community and school children who attend religious classes during the week.

‌



The Mosque considers itself an example of the vital role religious communities can play in the shared human struggle against global heating, and aspects of Muslim teaching on care for the planet were discussed during the visit.

6 View 6 Images Charles took his shoes off as he entered the mosque (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images) 6 View 6 Images The monarch unveiled a plaque to commemorate the visit (Image: Chris Jackson/PA Wire)

‌



The King's longstanding commitment to architectural excellence was visible in his appreciation of the mosque's architectural purpose in developing a specifically British idiom of mosque design. Speaking to the trustees, Charles called the building “magnificent” and architecturally wonderful”.

Award-winning features in the mosque include references to the fan-vaulting of the nearby King's College Chapel, and the crosshatched Victorian brickwork widely used in the local Romsey area of Cambridge.

During his visit, the King was also told of the importance of the mosque and other places of worship in helping Cambridge maintain its role as a magnet for global talent, with many world-leading academics and researchers from around the globe working in the city and playing a key role in strengthening its economy and international reputation.

‌



View 6 Images Charles shaking hands with Cambridge locals as he arrived at the mosque (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

The mosque, which opened in 2019, has been credited with actively promoting interfaith dialogue across Cambridgeshire. The Mosque is also an approved host for the Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme. At the end of his visit The King was thanked by the attendees, who prayed for him and were pleased to note his respect for their contribution to British life.

After unveiling a plaque to commemorate his visit, the King, 77, said: “The care and attention that you have lavished on it, and the fact that you have a purpose built mosque here with a community centre attached, makes a huge contribution I'm sure. Not only to the Muslim community but to Cambridge itself. So, I do congratulate you, and I pray with all my heart that you continue to have every possible success and you continue your work with other faiths in this area and set a remarkable example of integrated faith activity. Thank you for having me here today.”

‌



Abdal Hakim Murad, Chair of the Board of Trustees, said: "For the thriving and diverse Muslim community in Cambridge The King's visit represented a heartening affirmation of our mosque's commitment to Muslim integration into modern Britain, and to strengthening fraternal ties between religions."

View 6 Images Charles visited Europe's first Eco-Mosque (Image: Chris Jackson/PA Wire)

‌



He continued: “We were really delighted to be able to show The King the cutting-edge sustainable technologies which make our mosque a symbol of the shared human fight against climate change.”

Zeynep Coskun Koc, trustee of the mosque, said: "Fourteen years ago, when I first became involved in the Cambridge Mosque Project as a young graduate student at the University of Cambridge, this mosque was just a shared dream on paper.

“Today, it is a global beacon of inclusivity, where we hosted His Majesty The King. Serving as a trustee and helping steward the partnership between the Diyanet Foundation and the Cambridge Mosque Trust has been the honour of a lifetime. This visit celebrates not just a building, but the powerful bridge of faith, collaboration, and community empowerment we built together."

News.title: Argentina in fresh punch shame after World Cup final as new footage emerges
News.content:
Argentina in fresh punch shame after World Cup final as new footage emerges

Spain's World Cup triumph descended into chaos as Argentina players and staff were seen throwing punches following the full-time whistle at MetLife Stadium

View 2 Images Roberto Ayala clashed with Dani Olmo

Argentina coach Roberto Ayala appeared to throw a punch at Spain's Dani Olmo during the chaotic scenes that followed the World Cup final. The defending champions suffered a 1-0 extra-time loss in New Jersey after Ferran Torres struck in the 106th minute.

‌



But the result only told half of the story. Enzo Fernandez was sent off just before the additional period for a second yellow card, while there were unsavoury scenes at full-time involving Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina.

‌



And now Footage has emerged showing Ayala, who is one of Lionel Scaloni's assistant coaches, swinging his right arm towards Olmo as they clashed. To his credit, the Barcelona star didn't react and team-mate Eric Garcia stepped in to play the role of peacekeeper.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Former England goalkeeper Joe Hart labelled Argentina's behaviour 'disgusting'. He said: "There was one man on the pitch who did have class and that was Lionel Messi, who shook hands with every one of those Spanish players.

"The game's done. They could have absolutely no complaints about what happened today. Disgusting behaviour."

‌



Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match READ MORE :

Before he added: "Spain fully deserve it. They have been absolutely superb all tournament. They have dominated all game against a rigid, rugged Argentina. The best team has won this World Cup."

While fellow BBC pundit Wayne Rooney said: "Does it surprise you? It doesn't surprise me.

"We've seen this with Argentina before. It's just not the reaction you want. We've seen some of the reaction after knocking England out in the last round.

‌



"That's just sad. If you lose a game of football, be graceful and get out of there. It's really poor from them."

View 2 Images Paredes was sent off for an angry clash with Eric Garcia (Image: Getty Images)

Paredes was also sent off following the whistle, while Molina also appeared to throw a punch after the match. The latter took a swing at Rodri, while Paredes was spotted kicking Eric Garcia to the floor before pushing him back with a hand around his neck when the Barcelona defender attempted to confront him.

‌



He was also spotted in an exchange with Gavi and former Chelsea midfielder Craig Burley fumed: "Argentina were a complete and utter disgrace today, both with their performance and their antics.

"We expected the antics, we expected the thuggery, we expected the off the ball stuff, but we also expected a lot more on the ball, a lot more purpose... they were an utter shambles, disgusting, disgraceful. I'm so pleased Spain won. It was a disgusting performance [from Argentina]."

News.title: Queen Camilla praises innovative charity as she has emotional conversations with women experiencing rough times
News.content:
Queen Camilla praises innovative charity as she has emotional conversations with women experiencing rough times

The Queen has visited a unique charity that helps people turn their lives around after trauma, as she listened to women tell their stories of their emotional journeys

View 6 Images Queen Camilla in Norfolk today (Image: Chris Radburn/PA Wire)

Queen Camilla today spoke of the ‘brilliant’ work of a charity which helps homeless men and women, many of whom who have experienced deep personal trauma, turn their lives around.

‌



Her Majesty was visiting Emmaus Norfolk and Waveney, which offers accommodation, therapy and practical work experience on the site of a former nunnery, which is now the first in the UK to offer separate accommodation and services for nine women.

‌



In their residential centre, she spoke to three of the current ‘companions’, one of whom shared a heartbreaking tale of how her children were taken into care when she became a victim of domestic violence, leaving her to turn to alcohol abuse.

‌



View 6 Images Camilla visited Emmaus Norfolk and Waveney today (Image: Chris Radburn/PA Wire)

The woman - who cannot be named - has been at the centre for 11 months and told the queen that it had helped her to ‘get sober’ and ‘see my kids as well’. Camilla, who has been patron of Emmaus UK for 20 years, asked her how it had helped her. "Just being part of something, making friends," she said. "Being part of a community?" Camilla offered.

"And having people who understand your situation? So you rely on each other. I don’t think there’s anywhere like it." Another young girl told her she had been the victim of sexual violence growing up and found it difficult to navigate life and hold down a job.

‌



"So I joined the women's project and have really changed as a person," she said. "It was a huge decision to come here. In a lot of ways it saved my life." Camilla responded: "Well, it's lucky to hear that this is working so well. It's lovely to hear these success stories. And it’s nice that you've got every generation here. It’s just brilliant."

She also met with a woman named Melanie, another current companion, who told the queen in a speech: "We know that you are a champion of women’s causes and it was especially heartwarming for us that you were able to spend time talking to women in our women’s project. I was part of that last year, it was life changing.

View 6 Images Queen Camilla meeting companions during a visit to the charity (Image: Chris Radburn/PA Wire)

‌



"For women who have experienced domestic abuse and sexual violence to be seen, heard and empowered means the world and we are so grateful that you could hear our stories. To have your continued support nationally means thar people who have experienced homelessness, insecure housing and significant associated trauma are elevated and validated and I can say that from my own personal experience."

The Queen beamed and told Melanie that she was ‘so impressed’ with the community there - which has shops selling second-hand and recycled goods as well as a café and even its own forge - and hoped it would be rolled out nationally.

She told the shaking woman that she was a ‘perfect example’ of what it can do for people, enabling her to stand up and give a speech with ‘perfect confidence’. Melanie, who curtseyed with a look of utter astonishment on her face at the compliment, said afterwards that she was ‘overwhelmed’ at the queen’s words.

‌



View 6 Images Queen Camilla meeting Terry Waite (Image: Chris Radburn/PA Wire)

On arriving at the centre Her Majesty, wearing a blouse shirt dress with an eye-catching brooch, was greeted by Sir Terry Waite, the human rights activist and former hostage who is president of Emmaus UK. After meeting staff and supporters she toured the women’s centre before visiting a new shop offering stunning handbag and lamps made from recycled fabrics by some of the companions.

"There are bargains everywhere," she smiled. "What beautiful things you have and you are leaning new skills that can take you elsewhere. Brilliant. You could go into design, creative arts, anything."

‌



Before she left she cut a red ribbon to celebrate its opening. In the nun’s old library she visited a new ‘Book Nook’ - the first in conjunction with her own Queen’s Reading Room charity - which has been specially curated by campions with a passion for reading. The cosy spot will enable residents to engage with literature.

Camilla, 79, was given a handpicked posy by a lady who has been involved in setting up the area, peppering her with questions about her favourite books. "It’s a perfect spot," she said.

View 6 Images Camilla meeting companion Pascalle Sweerts in Norfolk (Image: Chris Radburn/PA Wire)

‌



She also gave the woman armfuls of books she had chosen for them to add to their library and said: "It’s got a fantastic feel to it. These are books I’ve read that I thought you might like. There’s a bit of everything, there’s some really good ones here. Handpicked. You’ll be able to add these to the bookshelves.

"I love getting everyone reading and hope it brings them as much enjoyment as it brings me. When you get the bug! There a lot of comfortable chairs to sit on. It’s perfect. You are the first Emmaus to do it. It’s very exciting to have you as the first one. Let me know how you get on with those books. Here’s to many more."

In the forge, she watched as they prepared copper to make bowls out of which will be sold in their on-site charity shop and social enterprise as well as unveiling a plaque marking 20 years of her patronage, as well as attending a celebratory reception.

‌



Afterwards the Norfolk branch’s chef executive, Cecile Roberts, said of the 52-room community: "When I first came into post eight years ago, there were no women in the community. And it didn't take much research to understand that women needed separate facilities. So we created a small women's wing of just a three bed wing, which filled up immediately once we opened it."

View 6 Images The Queen praised the work of the charity (Image: Chris Radburn/PA Wire)

‌



She continued: "Then we came to realise that many of the women who came through our services had experienced domestic abuse, sexual violence, and we wanted to do something really meaningful. So we collaborated with women with lived experience and co designed a project, which has intensive therapeutic intervention over the period of a year. And so we can provide nine women with that opportunity every year."

She said of the queen’s visit: "I think you can probably see from everybody's faces that we're just incredibly proud [of the Queen’s visit]. It just meant the world, it was fantastic for all of us here, and particularly for the women in the women's project. It was lovely to see those women who have been enabled, through that therapeutic intervention, to speak so clearly, and in such an empowered way, with Her Majesty, that was really lovely to see.

"I felt, particularly proud. The women were very open with her as well. She's got such an easy presence, so it was lovely to see. She's been our royal patron for 20 years in the UK. And for her to come here, to mark that occasion has been such an honour."
