News.title: Mum rushed to Canary Islands hospital with 'stomach cramps' told she's pregnant and giving birth
News.content:
Mum rushed to Canary Islands hospital with 'stomach cramps' told she's pregnant and giving birth

Carmen Romero is believed to have experienced a cryptic pregnancy when she gave birth suddenly to her daughter shortly after she was admitted to a hospital in Spain

View 3 Images Carmen Romero was stunned when her baby arrived (Image: Carmen Romero)

A woman was rushed to hospital and was shocked to discover she wasn't just suffering from stomach cramps.

‌



Carmen Romero, now 31, from the Canary Island of Tenerife, reportedly went to A&E when she was 24 complaining of stomach cramps, but was later told she was about to give birth.

‌



Speaking on the television programme Y ahor Sonsoles to presenter Sonsoles Onega, Carmen explained that she originally went to the hospital “with cramps” and ended up giving birth to what would be her second daughter. At the time her first daughter was just one-and-a-half years old.

‌



She explained: “I went to the emergency room because my father insisted. I just had cramps, like the urge to use the bathroom….I gained 45 kilos during my first pregnancy and developed a hiatal hernia.”

Carmen added that when she went to the hospital she discovered she wasn’t just slightly pregnant, that she was in fact in labour and about to deliver the child.

She explained that she hadn’t felt a single kick from the child before the labour began: “I didn’t feel a thing, not a kick, nothing.”

‌



View 3 Images A woman from Tenerife gave birth in mysterious circumstances (stock) (Image: Getty)

It was later reported by 20 Minutos that Carmen said: “They did an ultrasound and told me, 'You’re pregnant.' And I said, 'Excuse me? How far along?' And the doctor replied, 'I’d swear you’re actually giving birth right now,’

"I flatly refused to go into the delivery room; I couldn't believe I was pregnant. But once they calmed me down and I spoke to my mother on the phone, I told them to at least give me an epidural. But the woman said, 'The baby's head is already out.' I was in the delivery room for ten minutes."

‌



Carmen added that she had not suspected anything unusual, partly because she had a condition that caused abdominal bloating. She also said that she explained that her periods were irregular.

Irregular periods in this case meant she might go months without having one and then skip them entirely. She added that after the birth she had a “horrifying” experience when they gave her the child.

She said: “I was alone, they put the baby on top of me and told me: 'It's a girl, she's okay'. I looked at the baby, hallucinating. I felt like they had given me a baby that wasn't mine.

‌



“You have a daughter whom you aren't even able to love at that moment, because you are in such shock that you can't picture yourself as a mother.”

View 3 Images Carmen and her baby (Image: Carmen Romero)

Carmen later admitted that she told the child that she wanted to put the baby up for adoption, before she later decided to change her mind on the matter.

‌



In a subsequent interview, Carmen said that she had a moment when she began to develop a connection with a child that was now hers.

She said: “But twenty days after my daughter was born, she suffered a sleep apnea episode; she turned purple and stopped breathing. That was the moment I said, 'Shit, I love her. I need someone to save my child.'”

It is now believed that Carmen, now 31, experienced what is known as a cryptic pregnancy, when the pregnant individual does not know they are pregnant until the very latter stages of a pregnancy.

Article continues below

The BBC reported in 2024 that, when it comes to the UK at least, that around one in every 2,500 births is cryptic, equating to around 300 births each year. In Spain there are reportedly few figures about cryptic pregnancies.

News.title: Andy Burnham leaves door open to income tax cut for lower earners as he pledges cost of living blitz
News.content:
Andy Burnham leaves door open to income tax cut for lower earners as he pledges cost of living blitz

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham is expected to hit the ground running with a policy blitz in the coming days, including a package of cost of living measures to be unveiled on Tuesday

View 2 Images New PM Andy Burnham has pledged to take urgent action on the cost of living (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham has left the door open to cutting income tax for lower earners as he pledges help for people squeezed by the cost of living.

‌



The new Prime Minister is expected to hit the ground running with a policy blitz in the coming days, including a package of measures to help struggling Brits to be unveiled on Tuesday.

‌



Speaking to reporters shortly after entering No10, he signalled he was looking at increasing the amount people can earn before they have to pay income tax but said a decision would be taken in the Budget. And he refused to rule out introducing a 50p tax rate, saying it was premature to discuss.

‌



Mr Burnham said he would look at issues like rent controls, energy bill support and capping bus fares to help hard-pressed families, but said no final decisions had been taken. He also said he was determined to grip the crisis-hit social care system, saying: "We need to face it and fix it."

The PM spoke to reporters shortly after delivering his first speech to the nation from outside Downing Street, where he promised a "circuit breaker for Britain" with a 10-year plan to fix deep-rooted problems. Flanked by cheering supporters, he stopped to hug his mum Eileen before he made his way in through the famous black door with his wife Marie-France van Heel.

Andy Burnham live: New PM vows to END rough sleeping with biggest changes in 40 years READ MORE :

View 2 Images Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his wife Marie-France van Heel are clapped in as they arrive at 10 Downing Street (Image: Simon Dawson / No 10 Downing Street)

‌



Speaking to reporters in the Downing Street garden, Mr Burnham said the tax-free allowance, which has been frozen at £12,500 since 2022, had come up more than any other issue on the doorstep in his Makerfield constituency.

He said: "It has dragged more people in - pensioners, I think - and that particularly I think has become a growing issue. All of this will be looked at though at the Budget, and obviously it's difficult given the financial circumstances in which we find ourselves.

“But I wanted to recognise the point because it's challenging for people and it's people on the lowest incomes perhaps who've most been affected by that. So it's an issue that I'm just kind of showing I have a visibility of the issue and the impact it's had on the different groups that I've mentioned. But it's difficult because changing the threshold is not without significant consequences. But I'm looking at it.”

‌



Asked if he'd look at a 50p rate of tax to fund it, he said: "I think that would be just premature to say that. I’ve barely got my feet under the table."

It would mark a departure from Labour's manifesto, which committed not to raise the basic, higher, or additional rates of Income Tax, or VAT.

Mr Burnham said he wanted to give families some breathing space through measures that would make a difference this year. Asked if he was thinking about issues like bus fares, energy bills and rent freezes, he said: "We are looking at measures that could make a difference this year. So we are looking at all of those things but we will make more announcements tomorrow.

‌



"We're just finalising the details. It's premature to say it will be any one of those particular things. We just want to do some things that people will feel and feel quite quickly. It won't solve everything, it won't take all of the pressure off but it just shows the direction of travel and that we're serious about helping them out."

The PM also signalled that reforming social care would be a major priority after successive politicians have kicked the issue into the long grass.

He said: "I think the country needs to step back here and say, 'How have we let a situation kind of just roll on, where we know it's a major issue, and yet no one's got the courage to fix it?' I just think that's quite damning really of my generation of politicians."

Article continues below

He went on: "If I look at the National Health Service right now, what I hear from people is that corridor care is becoming the norm all year round, not just in winter time, and the standards in relation to A&E are just not achievable in terms of the 90-plus % of people coming through in four hours. And they say the biggest cause of that is broken social care because if there's no barrier there at the front, how on Earth can the hospital system cope? And I know this from my dad, who has Alzheimer's."

Mr Burnham added: "I am ready to use some of my political capital on this issue. I'll be blunt with you. I would not want to leave office having done what Westminster has done - not just for 15 years actually, I think you're getting close to 30 years - It's not defensible.

"How many people have lost their homes and their savings in that time? We need to face it and fix it."

News.title: Teen killer unmasked after luring man to meet girl, 16, before machete ambush
News.content:
Teen killer unmasked after luring man to meet girl, 16, before machete ambush

Two teenagers have been sentenced after luring 26-year-old Adam Khan to meet a girl, 16, in Luton before he was killed in a machete attack - one was jailed for life

Police release CCTV after 17-year-old convicted for machete attack murder

A teenager has been jailed for life after murdering an accountant in a machete street ambush.

‌



Emmanuel Avogo, then 16, can now be named for the first time after hatching a plan with a 16-year-old girl to “lure” Adam Khan, 26, to a meeting in Humberstone Road, Luton, on August 31 last year.

‌



When Mr Khan turned up to the meeting, Avogo chased him and then pulled a machete from down his trousers which he used to stab Mr Khan to death.

‌



Harrow Crown Court heard Avogo regularly carried a knife and had a string of incidents in his past involving violence and knives. On Monday, he was sentenced by Mr Justice Bennathan to life with a minimum term of 20 years, after being convicted at trial of murder.

View 3 Images Emmanuel Avogo has been named for the first time (Image: Bedfordshire Police)

The girl – who cannot be identified – was sentenced to a two-year detention and training order after she was found guilty at trial of manslaughter.

‌



The judge said Mr Khan had been “pestering” the girl for sex and agreed to provide her with some cannabis, she planned with Avogo to set him up to be attacked, but she did not know he would be armed with the machete.

“By August 31 he had offered to got you some cannabis for some form of sexual favour, and most people would agree this was very wrong”, he said.

“It would have serve him right if you two had taken the drugs and run off, but he had done nothing to deserve the terrible violence done to him that day.”

‌



The killers were dubbed “pure evil” and told to “rot in hell” by Mr Khan’s sister on Monday, as the court heard how the victim had been destined for a successful career as an accountant when he was killed.

View 3 Images Adam Khan, 26 (Image: Bedfordshire Police)

Before passing sentence, the judge stripped Avogo of his anonymity as a youth defendant.

‌



Noting his knife crime past, the judge said Avogo is “still in denial” about the murder, “suggesting any hope of reform and rehabilitation is a very distant prospect”.

“He frequently carried a knife or machete around the time of the offence,” he added.

“The seriousness of the offence of which he was convicted and the widespread publicity and concern surrounding young people and knife crime militate in favour of allowing this case to be examined by the press and discussed by the public.”

‌



Prosecutor Kate Bex KC said Mr Khan fell victim to an “ambush”, after he had exchanged phone messages with the girl in the lead up to the fateful meeting.

View 3 Images CCTV showed Avogo fleeing the scene

“Both defendants had developed a plan to lure Mr Khan to the scene, and following a confrontation he was then attacked by Mr Avogo”, she said.

‌



“He was attacked using a machete Mr Avogo had stored at his home address, and had been concealed down his trousers.”

In CCTV of the incident, Mr Khan is seen approaching a car and talking to the girl through the window, before Avogo appears.

Mr Khan retreated and drove away for a short distance with the boy chasing after him, but then stopped his vehicle, took a tyre wrench from the boot, and went to confront Avogo.

‌



He was stabbed five times – in the face, stomach and arm – in the fight that followed, and died later that evening in hospital. Mr Khan’s mother, who was not named in court, said her son had started working at 15 after the death of his father to support his family, and she called him “bright, strong, resilient and caring”.

She said of the teenage killers: “I hope they meet a fate far worse than what they inflicted on my son.”

Mr Khan’s sister said in her victim impact statement that her brother was murdered a day before he was due to take his final accountancy qualification exam, having got himself a job within a top financial firm.

‌



“He had so much to look forward to, but that was brutally snatched from him,” she said.

She said the teenage killers have “pure evil inside of them”, and said: “My brother’s death will hover over our heads and leave a hole in our hearts for the rest of our lives.”

She added: “I pray the harshest of justice is served to the inhumane people who committed this crime. “May they rot in hell.”

‌



At trial, it emerged that Avogo was a habitual carrier of knives and four months before murdering Mr Khan he had been spared jail after stabbing a man with a machete during a robbery of an e-bike.

In 2023, when he was 14, he received a police caution after attempting to push another boy into the road and punching him in the face, the court heard.

Later the same year, he received a second police caution after attacking two fellow school pupils, punching one repeatedly in the face and punching a second to the ground when he tried to intervene.

‌



Avogo assaulted a police officer in January 2024, and he was caught with a lock knife in August that year, when aged 15.

The e-bike robbery happened in March 2025, when he posed as a buyer in response to a Facebook marketplace advert and tried to ride off with the bike during the arranged meeting in Aylesbury.

When the seller stopped him fleeing, Avogo pulled out a 67cm-long machete from his trousers and left the victim with hand and leg injuries.

‌



He pleaded guilty at Milton Keynes Youth Court to attempted robbery, possession of an offensive weapon, and unlawful wounding, and was sentenced to a youth rehabilitation order with a night-time curfew.

Avogo had been hit over the head with a hammer in October 2023, leaving him in need of brain surgery, and he said during the trial that PTSD contributed to his response to the confrontation with Mr Khan.

Mr Justice Bennathan noted that the boy continues to plead his innocence over Mr Khan’s death, insisting he had not intended to cause him serious harm.

Article continues below

After the stabbing, the girl searched online for “Luton stabbing” and researched how to delete an Instagram account. Both defendants waved to their families as they were led away from the dock.

News.title: Burnham promises help with your money. How could it affect you?
News.content:
In his first speech as prime minister, Andy Burnham has promised to give people more "breathing space" to help with the cost of living.

Policies will be announced on Tuesday - his first full day in the job. Although a few hours after taking office, the new prime minister confirmed he will be "looking at" the tax-free personal allowance ahead of his first Budget in the autumn.

Cost of living is a key issue for Burnham. Many people, he has previously said, can't go out for a pint on a Friday, can't take the kids out and can't go on holiday owing to the pressure on their finances.

The cost of living has dominated people's lives in recent years, and - to some extent - our politics too. Easing that pressure hasn't been easy.

So, if Burnham chooses to support people on issues such as energy bills and the cost of transport, allows people to earn more before being taxed, and makes care and somewhere to live more affordable - he'll face tough choices on funding those moves and managing the trade-offs that come with them.

And his chancellor will often be the one who has to deliver any changes, and outline how to pay for them.

News.title: Burnham's policy choices reveal what kind of PM he wants to be
News.content:
Later this week, he is expected to change the government's stance on oil and gas exploitation, with a new energy secretary in place.

Those Labour MPs worried about the Green Party taking their seats will be concerned about this - but a lot more will be worried about whether this could be seen to be diluting the government's commitment to net zero.

There was also a promise to do something about the cost of living, with more detail tomorrow on the "breathing space" he is offering hard-pressed families.

Extending Manchester's Â£2 bus fare cap would be a tangible step and also different from the Â£3 cap under Keir Starmer and Rachel Reeves.

With energy prices rising again, there may be action there.

The former minister, Miatta Fahnbulleh, has spent the past few weeks working on policy options. She is the former head of the New Economic Foundation think tank and it wants bolder cost of living measures â from rent controls to making bus journeys entirely free for under 25s.

The question though is whether Burnham will go beyond announcing specific policies and outline a broader vision.

He indicated in his speech that he would set out how the cost of living measures will be paid for. So will he make the greater argument - which he believes - that taxes on income are too high, taxes on wealth are too low?

Will he expand on his Times interview and pledge to raise tax thresholds at least for basic rate taxpayers, while pushing up capital gains tax?

Burnham has said he will be "looking at" the tax-free personal allowance ahead of his first Budget in the autumn but stressed that changing it would be "difficult" in the current economic circumstances, and it could have "significant consequences".

But if he wants to address people's priorities more than his predecessor he may have to find a way to fund this as he also said he had "heard issues related to the personal allowance more than anything on the doorsteps in Makerfield" (the seat he represents).

He has pledged to stick to Rachel Reeves's "fiscal rules," which limit debt and borrowing - so it is likely to be "re-prioritisation" of existing spending rather than new money.

But that can still tell its own story about he intends to govern.

Burnham also promised a new kind of politics â re-using his recent catchphrase of "problem solving not point scoring".

This could be making a virtue out of necessity. If he wants to achieve the ambition he set out today - not to leave office without reforming social care â then he will need cross party co-operation.

More widely, Andy Burnham has not exactly managed expectations.

He has promised nothing less than a new economic model, leaving behind an era of centralisation, privatisation and de-industrialisation.

Just as rough sleeping is meant to signal to party members where he stands, he will soon need to set out symbolic policies which reveal - to voters and the markets alike - what the economic reality will be behind the radical rhetoric.

News.title: Key takeaways as Andy Burnham becomes PM
News.content:
In his first speech in Downing Street, Burnham announced he would "end rough sleeping in our country".

This was swiftly followed by a No 10 press release promising an extra Â£340m for the task over the next five years.

He also promised a new 10-year plan for Britain - to be unveiled later this year - and to build a new economy, putting "life's essentials back under public control".

But arguing that people also needed "breathing space now", he said announcements on tackling the cost of living would start on Tuesday.

Other changes he promised included changing the education system to help young people into work, building more council homes, and honouring commitments to fund defence while sticking to the UK's spending and debt rules.

News.title: Watch: Starmer resigns, Burnham becomes PM... the day so far
News.content:
Andy Burnham has become the UK's prime minister today, replacing Keir Starmer.

The day began outside a busy 10 Downing Street where Starmer made his final address as PM, before he and Burnham visited King Charles in Buckingham Palace.

The new prime minister then gave his own speech in Downing Street saying he wants a "circuit-breaker for Britain" and bring some of the biggest changes that country has seen in 40 years.

News.title: Who is Andy Burnham's wife, Marie-France van Heel?
News.content:
She was described as the "coolest girl in college" when she first started dating Andy Burnham.

More than three decades later, Marie-France van Heel has walked into Downing Street alongside her husband to take on one of the most powerful unofficial roles in government - the prime minister's spouse.

Burnham has replaced Sir Keir Starmer in No 10, and he met Dutch-born van Heel, known as Frankie, when she started studying at Fitzwilliam College at the University of Cambridge in 1989.

He was in his second year of an English Literature degree, and Burnham's former lecturer, John Mullan, wrote in the Times that other students thought he had scooped the pools when they began dating.

News.title: Ofcom launches investigation into Married at First Sight UK
News.content:
Married at First Sight UK is facing renewed pressure after the broadcast regulator launched an official investigation into the hit Channel 4 reality TV show.

In a statement on Monday, Ofcom said it was investigating "a fairness and privacy complaint" about the prime-time show.

In May, a BBC Panorama investigation revealed rape allegations from two female cast members on the show - allegations the men involved deny.

An Ofcom fairness or privacy complaint can be lodged by individuals who participated in TV or radio programmes. Complaints like these usually relate to claims of being treated unfairly or having unwarranted infringements of privacy on programmes.

It is understood the watchdog is considering a complaint of unjust or unfair treatment from a cast member of Married at First Sight UK.

At least one other cast member previously complained to Ofcom about their treatment on the show, but the watchdog dismissed their complaint as it found the broadcaster had no case to answer.

An Ofcom spokesperson said such complaints are considered "on a case-by-case basis through a detailed and careful assessment process".

News.title: Lamine Yamal celebrates World Cup win with little brother who charmed fans
News.content:
Spanish footballer Lamine Yamal may have lifted the World Cup but it is his little brother Kenye who appears to have stolen the spotlight.

The three-year-old quickly become an internet sensation after footage of his exuberant celebrations following Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina spread across social media on Sunday.

While the footballer, just 19 himself, continued his rise by helping Spain achieve football's biggest prize, attention swiftly turned to his younger brother's joyful reactions from the sidelines.

From sticking out his tongue on the big screen to wildly cheering on his older brother, Kenye has been hailed by fans as one of the unexpected breakout stars of the 2026 tournament.

News.title: My fitness tracker knew I was pregnant before I did
News.content:
Dr Stuart Lavery, consultant of reproductive medicine at University College Hospital in London, said: "People are understandably using this technology to try to get a greater understanding, and to try and pick up things as early as possible because it has such a profound impact on your life if you're planning a pregnancy."

However, "we might be running before we can walk," he cautioned.

"We probably need a lot more data on the reliability, we need a lot more researchâ¦ otherwise what happens is your levels of anxiety will just skyrocket," he said.

"I have no doubt that more people will be using technology, an app-based approach or a wearable-based approach, to try and pick up these things. But I think it should come with quite a big health warning about how much we can rely on them for accuracy."

When asked about the anxiety women reported feeling early in their pregnancy as a result of checking their ring data, Dr Chris Curry, Oura's clinical director of women's health, told BBC News: "With or without biometric tracking, pregnancy can be an uncertain time where many women, particularly those pregnant for the first time, are in the dark about the range of what's normal."

She added that if women feel overwhelmed, the company "encourages members to take a break from the app experience, whilst Oura Ring continues to collect data and gather insights", adding: "The ring is a support tool, not a replacement for your care team."

Ravika sadly did miscarry. She's hoping to start trying to conceive again soon - and when she does, her experience has made her rethink wearing her tracker again.

"I didn't really see myself as being an anxious person, butâ¦ I think going forward if it came to a point where I had an inkling that I was pregnant and my stats were low, as soon as that positive pregnancy test was there, I do think it would be the best thing for me to take the ring off."

News.title: Prisons minister Lord Timpson quits government
News.content:
The prisons minister has resigned from the government, the BBC has been told.

Lord James Timpson was appointed to the role in July 2024 after leaving his job as CEO of the Timpson group, a business which provides key cutting and shoe repair services and employs hundreds of former prisoners.

His arrival in government was greeted with much fanfare by some in the Labour Party and described as "radical" and "innovative".

But in a departing statement on Monday, seen exclusively by the BBC, Lord Timpson said he was stepping down and it was an "honour" to serve in the post.

His statement did not give a specific reason for resigning, but it is understood he feels he has done as much as he can in the role.

Prisons in England and Wales were at crisis point, reaching almost full capacity, when he first entered Sir Keir Starmer's government.

He oversaw the controversial early release scheme which saw tens of thousands of inmates let out to create more space in jails.

His critics will argue prisons continue to be violent, drug infused and overcrowded, while probation officers still report being overworked and unable to cope.

But figures do show assaults against staff and self-harm in prisons are falling.

Lord Timpson said in his resignation statement that he had left "our prisons and probation service in a much healthier and happier state than two years ago".

He added: "I'm proud to have become the longest-serving minister in this role for 15 years. I'm also proud that 75% of prisons and 90% of probation teams are now performing better than when I started.

"Self-harm, violence and assaults on staff are all down, and fewer people are leaving prison without a home to go to, a measure of dignity I care about deeply."

He also pointed to the Women's Justice Board he established, saying he "believe[s] most women should not be in prison at all" and "diverting them away from custody, helping them with often chaotic, damaged, and addicted lives, is one of the changes I'm proud to have achieved".

His critics may question why he is leaving before the Sentencing Act 2026 is enacted in September, when more people are expected to be released early and further criminals will serve their sentences in the community.

A source in the Ministry of Justice told the BBC: "We're gutted he's going but the new person is going to have their work cut out to get their head round what's round the corner."

News.title: South East Water hosepipe ban to affect 2.4 million people
News.content:
A hosepipe ban has been expanded to cover 2.4 million people across the south of England after record-breaking temperatures.

South East Water's ban now includes parts of Sussex, Surrey, Hampshire and Berkshire - an extra 1.5m customers. A ban in parts of Kent has been in force since 3 July.

Douglas Whitfield, SEW's water supply director, said it was "deeply sorry" and "incredibly grateful to everyone helping us protect water supplies" after exceptionally hot and dry weather.

Eastbourne MP Josh Babarinde said he was "appalled", calling it "the direct result of years of underinvestment in upgrading infrastructure and building resilience".

Under the restrictions, households in the affected area will be banned from using a hosepipe in their homes for tasks including cleaning, filling ponds, or watering plants.

The ban will officially come in from 00:01 BST on Saturday, but SEW has asked its customers to abide by the restrictions immediately.

The UK record for the hottest day in June was broken for a third day in a row last month, with temperatures reaching 37.3C, the Met Office said.

News.title: Pupil not guilty of trying to murder history teacher after stabbing her in the head
News.content:
A pupil has been found not guilty of attempted murder after stabbing his teacher in the head with a kitchen knife.

The boy, 16, followed Vicki Williams into her empty classroom at Milford Haven Comprehensive School in Pembrokeshire, after asking for help with his history work on 5 February.

He pulled a knife from his bag and lunged at her. Williams told a jury at Swansea Crown Court she feared she would die.

On Monday, he was found not guilty of attempted murder but guilty of wounding with intent, and unlawful wounding. He will be sentenced on 3 September.

The boy had previously pleaded guilty to possessing a kitchen knife on the school grounds.

Judge Paul Thomas KC accepted a majority verdict on the charge of wounding with intent, which meant at least 10 jurors agreed following four hours deliberation.

During the attack, Williams grabbed the knife, pushed the boy back with her legs, and screamed.

She received injuries to her head, back and hands after the attack.

She said the look on the teenager's face was one of "pure hatred".

During a police interview, Williams said how the boy, who was 15 at the time and who cannot be named due to his age, came to her classroom "cool and collected" at the end of the school day to ask if his "work was correct".

She said that "got [her] confused" because he had "never seemed bothered before".

It was when he shut the door to the classroom, saying it was cold, that "alarm bells" began to ring in her head.

Williams said he was trying to "keep her talking" while he was "trying to find something in his bag".

"I ask him again, 'are you sure you're alright?' And then he pulls [the knife] out of the bag and lunges at me," she said.

The boy told the court Williams had seen him with the knife and "tried to grab it" from him. He said he "accidentally assaulted her" during the struggle.

She told the court she believed she was about to die, thinking: "I'm fearful that I am dying, I've seen the knife, I know I've been stabbed, all I'm thinking at that point is, 'I need help'."

Williams said the attack "came out of nowhere".

News.title: Ryanair profits drop as Iran war puts off passengers and lifts fuel costs
News.content:
Ryanair's profits have fallen sharply as war in the Middle East sent jet fuel prices soaring and customers reluctant to book flights.

The Irish airline's pre-tax profits dropped 34% to â¬593m (Â£503m) between April and June while sales were flat as the company was forced to cut fares to stimulate demand.

Ryanair also said it expects summer fares to be slightly lower than last year due to "consumer hesitancy" around air travel.

The price of fuelling a plane has jumped since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February and while Ryanair said it had "hedged" or struck deals for the most future fuel costs, those not included in these arrangements had more than doubled.

Crude oil prices hit $90 (Â£67) a barrel for the first time in a month on Monday, before falling back slightly, after a weekend of intense exchanges of fire between the US and Iran.

Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz â an essential route for global oil and gas supplies â has ground to a halt.

An interim peace deal last month brought some respite to oil and energy prices, but they spiked again as negotiations broke down and fighting resumed.

The airline warned that its results for the year will be "highly sensitive" to external factors such as conflict escalation in the Middle East and Ukraine as well as the price of unhedged jet fuel.

Fares for for the key summer period between July and September are on track to be "modestly" lower than last year, with many passengers booking closer to departure than normal.

The firm's finance chief, Neil Sorahan, said flights on its popular Mediterranean routes were still full. "People [are] as keen to get away as ever, albeit booking just a little bit later," he said.

Between April and June, Ryanair's revenue ticked up 1% to â¬4.4bn.

While passenger numbers rose 6% to 6.1 million- helped by the Easter holiday in April - fares fell by 6% as the airline reduced fares to entice flyers concerned about the Iran war.

Ryanair's share price fell 5% on Monday.

Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, said Ryanair was in a better position than many of its rivals, but nonetheless "visibility is worse than San Francisco airport when the fog sets in".

"The renewed escalation in hostilities in the Middle East is unhelpful and without a lasting resolution, challenging times for the airline and travel space look set to continue."

News.title: Drug dealer exploited 14-year-old boy into selling drugs for him
News.content:
Siddiqi met the boy in Glasgow's St Enoch Centre during the school summer holidays in 2025 and asked if he "wanted to start making money".

The boy initially refused as he believed the dealer was talking about drugs.

But the High Court in Glasgow heard Siddiqi eventually persuaded the child to team up with him by suggesting he could use the cash to help his mother.

The youngster was given Siddiqi's Instagram account and later a mobile phone.

The boy lied to his mum that he had a "summer holiday camp" to go to after Siddiqi messaged him, and in mid-July the teenager was taken to a known drug den in Glasgow.

He ended up staying there for a number of days and was shown how to "bag up" crack cocaine.

Prosecutor Jennifer Nicholson-White said: "Siddiqi would attend the flat for only a couple of hours each day due to having an electronic tag. He would give the boy Â£20 to buy food."

The child was then taken by taxi to a dirty, rubbish-strewn property in Paisley in Renfrewshire.

He was told to hand out "testers" to local addicts - small samples of cocaine.

The boy ended up staying at the flat for the rest of the week.

The prosecutor said the child handed out about 60 testers and was given the phone numbers of drug users.

She added: "He estimated Siddiqi made about Â£700 each day in sales."

News.title: Fire crews to remain at Arthur's Seat for days after blaze
News.content:
Firefighters are expected to remain at Arthur's Seat in Edinburgh "for a couple of days" following a large blaze on Sunday evening.

Small plumes of smoke could still be seen on Monday morning along Salisbury Crags and large swathes of vegetation below the cliff face had been burned black.

Six fire engines were sent to tackle the the grassfire with crews working overnight to douse the flames and dampen hotspots.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) said there were "no reported casualties" but Police Scotland said Queen's Drive, the road that encircles the Holyrood Park hills, remained closed to all vehicles.

It is the second fire in the last three months at the landmark, an ancient extinct volcano that offers panoramic views of the Scottish capital.

Edinburgh University student Mahek Jayantilial, who lives near Arthur's Seat, said she could see the fire from her window.

"I was a bit worried because I thought the fire would come this way, but thankfully there's enough concrete here to stop it," the 24-year-old said.

News.title: Parched grass reveals 'lost' 17th Century garden
News.content:
The recent high temperatures have revealed the outline of an ornate and "lost" 17th Century garden at the Chatsworth Estate.

The Great Parterre, which is beneath the south lawn at Chatsworth House in Derbyshire, was designed in 1699 for the 1st Duke of Devonshire, to complement the newly completed south facade of the house.

This is not the first time the European-style formal garden has been exposed due to the hot and dry weather - it was also revealed during dry spells in 2022 and 2018.

A spokesperson for the estate said after temperatures exceeded 30C in May, June and July, and with the "exceptionally dry" start to July, the lawn was "parched enough for history to reveal itself once again".

News.title: Residents told to pay £7,000 each to fix water pipe outside their homes
News.content:
Residents say they could face prosecution if they do not pay thousands of pounds to repair a water pipe outside their homes.

The residents of five houses in Pontycymer, Bridgend county, said they were told by Welsh Water that a leak from the shared pipe supplying their homes needs to be repaired at their own cost, which they estimate could cost more than Â£7,000 each.

The Garw Valley locals claim they have been given no evidence of where the leak is which their insurance companies need to cover the cost, causing sleepless nights.

A Welsh Water spokesperson said it does not own or manage the pipe so it's the responsibility of property owners, and residents have 11 days to fix it.

Welsh Water added that the leak needed to be repaired as it was wasting water, and it could issue a potential prosecution under Section 75 Notice under the Water Industry Act 1991, external.

The estimated cost of more than Â£7,000 would go towards replacing the rear water pipe in their back gardens with a new pipe at the front of the terraced row, they said, along with connecting it to each house individually.

Resident Nerys Walters said the dispute had brought her massive amounts of stress over the last two years.

She said they initially thought the cost of repairs could be covered through insurance, but with no evidence of the leak being provided, insurers have said they would not pay out.

Walters said: "It's been a nightmare situation for us that has really caused us all a lot of stress.

"Welsh Water have said they would pay for a new line that runs parallel to the front of the property, but we would then have to fund the cost of it coming in from the gate, and through the house to our rear stopcock.

Walters said she had spoken to "numerous contractors" who quoted the residents more than Â£1,000 a metre for the work.

"This has been going on for about a year and a half now and we've been asking for that evidence ever since but have been given nothing", she said.

"No evidence of the leak, and no reason as to why they adopted other pipes in the street but not ours. All the while the deadline they have given runs down. It's been very difficult and we just want to get it sorted."

News.title: Terrorism investigation launched after suspect hurls ‘incendiary device’ at ICE office in NYC
News.content:

The New York Joint Terrorism Task Force took a man into custody Monday morning after he allegedly ignited “an incendiary device” outside of a federal building that houses Immigration and Customs Enforcement offices.

Police apprehended the man, who has not been publicly identified, after he set off the device in front of 26 Federal Plaza in Manhattan around 8:30 a.m., according to a video posted on X by Freedom News TV. Smoke could be seen billowing from an area directly in front of the building.

Preliminary information indicates that fireworks exploded inside a garbage can, sources told CBS News. Authorities then found the suspect with airsoft rifles – which deploy pellets, helmet and carbon dioxide cartridges.

“This morning an individual deployed an incendiary device outside of 26 Federal Plaza,” The FBI’s New York field office said in a statement. “The individual has been taken into custody and the FBI New York Joint Terrorism Task Force is investigating the incident.”

The joint task force combines resources from the FBI with the New York Police Department.

open image in gallery Smoke billowed from the area in front of a federal building where a suspect set off an incendiary device Monday morning ( AP )

26 Federal Plaza is a federal building located in downtown Manhattan that houses the New York field office of ICE, immigration courts, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and other agencies.

The location has received media attention over the last year as the Trump administration has cracked down on illegal immigration and conducted operations in New York City. Protesters have taken to the streets surrounding the building to display opposition to the administration’s harsh enforcement.

The administration has faced intense scrutiny for deploying federal agents inside the building to arrest immigrants as they arrive for court hearings or check-ins.

It’s unclear what motive the suspect may have had in setting off the device.

open image in gallery Law enforcement officers tackled a suspect to the ground and arrested him moments after he allegedly set off a fire in front of the building that houses ICE field offices in New York City ( AP )

But those familiar with the matter told New York Daily News that the suspect wheeled a cart with fireworks and flammable liquid in front of the building to ignite the fire. The cart allegedly had a sign that read, “ICE off our streets.”

One person was taken to a local hospital with minor injuries, a source told NBC News.

Italy have reportedly held talks with Pep Guardiola in a bid to convince him to take over as their national team coach.

The Azzurri missed out on a third successive World Cup in March after play-off final heartbreak at the hands of Bosnia and Herzegovina, leading to the departure of Gennaro Gattuso.

And in a bid to end this dismal streak after 12 years without World Cup football, Sky in Italy are reporting that Italian Football Federation have made an ambitious approach towards decorated former Manchester City boss Guardiola.

Italy icon Paolo Maldini, who has been newly appointed the technical director of the FIGC, travelled to Barcelona alongside advisor Leonardo to speak with the Catalan, who left City after 10 glory-laden years at the end of last season.

It remains to be seen whether Guardiola is keen to take the job but the FIGC is making serious efforts to convince him, with Maldini and Leonardo speaking to Guardiola over three days.

Pep Guardiola has reportedly held talks with Italy ( Getty Images )

Italy have only ever had one foreign manager and that was 60 years ago, with Argentine Helenio Herrera taking charge of the team alongside Italian Fercuccio Valcareggi between 1966 and 1967.

If they fail in their bid to land Guardiola, the FIGC is also examining Roberto Mancini and Andrea Pirlo as potential candidates, two figures who have been at the heart of the Italy setup in the past - whether as a player or manager.

Guardiola said before his City exit that he wasn’t planning on taking a new job “for a while”, citing a lack of “energy” - just as his storied rival Jurgen Klopp said when he departed Liverpool.

"No plans for [coaching] for a while,” he said during his final press conference for the club. “Otherwise I would be here. I need to step back. I will not [coach] for a while.

"I feel I will not have the energy every day, with expectations to fight for the title. I know myself, I have that energy, but I feel like I will not have it [in the future]."

The hosts of The View have torn into Donald Trump over his appearance at Sunday’s World Cup final.

Trump was on hand to help present medals and trophies at the conclusion of the match, which saw Spain defeat Argentina 1-0 in extra time. He then forced his way into the team’s winning photo, much to the chagrin of viewers at home.

During Monday’s broadcast, the women of The View launched right into dissecting Trump’s appearance.

“I will say it did seem like some people got a very chilly — like a ‘boo’ chilly reception from the crowd,” Whoopi Goldberg said. While showing viewers a photo of Trump crashing the Spain team photo, Goldberg added: “Can I just point out he looks like somebody inserted his picture?”

Ana Navarro interjected: “He inserted himself. But I mean, it’s like, I don’t know how this guy thinks that he’s not gonna get booed in a stadium that’s full of Latin Americans and Spaniards.”

open image in gallery The hosts of 'The View' ripped into Trump crashing the Spain team photo after their victory ( PA )

open image in gallery The hosts of 'The View' tore into Donald Trump's appearance at the World Cup final ( ABC )

She continued, thinking back to the Argentina team walking across the field to accept their medals from Trump and Fifa president Gianni Infantino: “If these guys weren’t on this field, if they were standing in front of a Home Depot, Trump’s eyes would be racially profiling them.”

Navarro then launched into a laundry list of statements Trump has made in recent months about Spain, including calling them “bad people” and saying “Spain is a loser.”

She then looked into the camera and smiled: “Oh no they’re not.”

California thieves are targeting air-conditioning units to strip for copper parts, according to reports. ​

The theft of the valuable copper parts echoes the targeting of catalytic converters, from the bottom of cars, which contain precious metals. Thieves will steal the equipment, then sell the parts for the metals.

The Pasadena Police Department told KTLA 5 that at least six businesses have been targeted in recent weeks, with a pet hospital, two small businesses and a bakery all falling victim to the thieves targeting air conditioning units. Each of those four businesses has now been left without air conditioning. ​

Darlene Lopez, who works at the Pasadena Animal Hospital, told the outlet that the business was forced to bring in swamp coolers to keep their patients cool amid high temperatures in California. ​The temperatures are around mid- to high-80s in the area throughout the week.

“We have our patients in the cooler area of the hospital,” Lopez told the outlet.

open image in gallery Thieves are targeting air conditioning units in Pasadena, California, in order to take the copper parts inside, authorities said ( AFP/Getty )

Pasadena Chief Communications Officer Lisa Derderian confirmed to CBS News that Sweet Red Peach, a bakery, and the Petsadena Animal Hospital were among those targeted.

​“Both continue to conduct business, but it has had an impact financially,” Derderian said. “And with unseasonably high temperatures the past several days, it takes a toll on working conditions.”​

Both businesses have turned to using portable AC units and ice to keep their workers cool. ​

The Pasadena Police Department told NBC Los Angeles that they responded to reports of a theft at Sweet Red Peach on the evening of July 14. Earlier that day, the fiancée of business owner Daniel Griffin noticed that the building was hotter than usual. ​Eventually, a technician determined that half of the copper wiring inside the AC unit had been taken by thieves. The stolen wire was worth around $4,000.​

The damaged air conditioning unit was valued at around $11,000, but the technician noted that the entire system would need to be replaced.​

Griffin told the outlet that he believes that the thieves struck between 12.30 a.m. and 7.15 a.m., possibly using a collapsible ladder to target the units on the roof of the business.

Jeremy Melton, the CEO of Impact Service Group, told 11Alive that the copper wiring and tubing inside AC units can be cut up and taken to a recycling yard, where it is sold for money. Then, the copper parts are scrapped.

Melton continued by saying that he had called up a local scrapyard, with an official saying that they offered $4.50 per pound of copper, with copper coils being bought for $2.30 per pound. He says that an AC unit could contain as much as 100 pounds of copper, depending on the unit’s size. ​

open image in gallery The theft of the copper inside AC units echoes the targeting of catalytic converters on cars, which contain precious metals including rhodium and platinum, which can be sold ( Getty )

​The targeting of AC Units is similar to the thefts aimed at catalytic converters, a car part that contains rhodium. The precious metal is used because of its resistance to high temperatures and corrosion.

Catalytic converters are devices that transform toxic gases and pollutants into less toxic pollutants. For example, carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides can be converted into carbon dioxide, nitrogen and water vapor.

Rhodium was priced at over $12,000 per ounce in February 2026, according to Trading Economics.

Catalytic converters also contain the valuable metals platinum and palladium.

New prime minister Andy Burnham has invited US president Donald Trump to visit Manchester in one of his first calls since entering Downing Street.

While White House sources offered no details of the phone call, new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea is understood to also have been discussed.

This follows reports Mr Burnham could back new fossil fuel production, leading Mr Trump to declare on Truth Social that people in Aberdeen would be "dancing in the streets".

POLITICO has reported the former mayor used the call to invite the US president to Manchester, an offer Trump indicated he would accept.

Asked previously what he knew about Mr Burnham, the president said: “I don’t know, I think I see that he was, I guess, the mayor of a town.

“I hear he’s extremely liberal, extremely.”

open image in gallery Donald Trump posted about Burnham’s plans for North Sea oil and gas licences over the weekend ( Screenshot/ TruthSocial @realDonaldTrump )

Throughout Monday, Mr Burnham has received congratulations from world leaders. Senior figures from the European Union seized the opportunity to call for closer EU-UK relations, while Ukraine’s president said he would speak to Mr Burnham later in the day.

European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen said she looked forward to working with Mr Burnham for the “prosperity of people on both sides of the Channel”.

She said in a post on X: “Congratulations, dear Andy Burnham, on your confirmation as Prime Minister.

“I look forward to working with you to strengthen the EU-UK partnership.

“For the security of our shared continent. And the prosperity of people on both sides of the Channel.”

The president of the European Council, Antonio Costa, said: “In the last two years EU-UK relations gained a new, positive momentum. I look forward to continuing to further deepen our co-operation for the benefit of our citizens and businesses.

“The United Kingdom and the European Union are stronger together.”

open image in gallery World leaders have congratulated Andy Burnham on becoming prime minister after he officially entered Downing Street ( PA Wire )

Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky said he wished Mr Burnham “every success in addressing the challenges of today”.

He said: “Britain has always been one of the global leaders. We are ready to work together in all possible formats.

“We highly appreciate the UK’s political, defence and values-based support. The foundation of our bilateral relationship is stronger than ever, and we will continue to make each other stronger. I’m looking forward to our conversation later today.”

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said: “Congratulations Prime Minister Burnham on your appointment as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.

“Australia and the United Kingdom are longstanding friends, allies and partners, united by shared values and deep ties between our peoples.

“I look forward to working with you to strengthen our partnership and promote security, resilience and prosperity in the years ahead.”

French President Emmanuel Macron, who worked closely with Sir Keir Starmer on a coalition of the willing for Ukraine and a future mission to secure the Strait of Hormuz, said: “I extend my congratulations to Andy Burnham on his appointment as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.

“In the face of the challenges that unite us, I hope that we will deepen our relationship in service of our peoples and by giving new momentum to the partnership between the United Kingdom and the European Union.

“I also wish to commend the action of Keir Starmer, whose commitment to serving his country has helped to strengthen co-operation between the United Kingdom, France and our European partners.”

open image in gallery Donald Trump said people in Aberdeen would be ‘dancing in the streets’ in a post on his Truth Social platform following reports that Mr Burnham could back new fossil fuel production ( Getty )

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said: “Congratulations and best wishes for a successful tenure to the new Prime Minister.

“Italy and the United Kingdom are bound by a deep friendship and a collaboration that, over the years, has grown ever stronger, also thanks to our joint work on key dossiers fundamental to our nations: from managing migratory flows to the major international crises, always addressed with a great spirit of collaboration.

“I am certain that we will continue down this path, strengthening our strategic partnership in the interest of our nations and our citizens.”

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said: “Congratulations to Andy Burnham on taking office as Prime Minister. Germany and the United Kingdom are close partners. I look forward to working together.”

News.content:

Kevin Keegan, the former England footballer and manager and a legendary figure at both Liverpool and Newcastle United, has died at the age of 75.

It was announced in January that Keegan had been diagnosed with cancer, with his family revealing he was to begin treatment. Keegan said in June that he had been diagnosed with stage four cancer, adding that he wanted to attend a match at Newcastle’s St James’ Park to say “goodbye”.

A statement was published on behalf of the Keegan family by the Sky Sports journalist Pete Graves on Monday afternoon, confirming Keegan had passed away while surrounded by his wife and two daughters.

open image in gallery Kevin Keegan has died at the age of 75 following a battle with cancer ( Getty )

“It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75,” the statement said.

“The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

“Kevin, a double Ballon D’or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather. The family would like to thank Kevin’s incredible medical team for all their support.

“This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy.”

Most revered for his feats as a manager at Newcastle and as a player at Liverpool, Keegan forged a successful career that included three First Division titles, one FA Cup, one European Cup, and two Uefa Cups as well as two Bundesliga titles between the years of 1968 and 1984.

Newcastle led the tributes and said: “We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan, one of the most iconic, influential and deeply loved figures in our club’s history. Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters.”

“Liverpool FC is deeply saddened and mourning the passing of the legendary Kevin Keegan,” the Reds said. “The thoughts of everyone at the club are with Kevin's family and friends at this hugely difficult time... Our 'Mighty Mouse', his legacy at Liverpool will be forever etched in history.”

open image in gallery Keegan is one of English football’s greatest ever players ( Getty )

open image in gallery Keegan was at the heart of the start of Liverpool’s dominant era ( Getty )

Keegan’s traits as a forward was founded on his pace and ability with the ball, and he formed a formidable ‘little and large’ strike partnership with John Toshack, and was at the heart of Liverpool’s prosperous side in the 1970s under Bill Shankly and Bob Paisley.

As a manager, Keegan took Newcastle from the second tier into the Premier League and to their best-ever second finish, earning the nickname ‘King Kev’, and signed some of the club’s most iconic players, including Alan Shearer. Newcastle’s record goalscorer simply posted: “My Hero. My manager. My friend. Sleep easy Boss.”

Aside from an iconic 1970’s bubble perm, Keegan is arguably best known for his “I will love it” rant from 1996, when he took the bait and publicly criticised Sir Alex Ferguson’s comments, although Manchester United had the last laugh when they went on to win the league title, with the Magpies finishing second.

Born in 1951 in Armthorpe, Doncaster, and the son of a miner, Keegan has told the tale of using his brother’s pram as a goalpost. While his father might have been a Newcastle fan, because they had moved before Keegan’s birth, he would grow up supporting local side Doncaster Rovers.

Compared to most modern footballers, Keegan had an unorthodox journey to the top of the game. Rather than coming through an established club academy, he started his career at Scunthorpe in 1968 as an apprentice, having been spotted the previous year playing in local leagues, he made his debut against Peterborough at the age of 17, and went on to make 29 league starts in his first season.

In his autobiography, Keegan mentions the club’s low wages forcing him into summer jobs, such as plate-laying in the local area. But in 1971, Keegan had caught the eye of Liverpool’s chief scout Geoff Twentyman, and he was signed by Bill Shankly for a reported figure of £35,000, having scored 18 goals in 124 appearances in the midfield for Scunthorpe.

open image in gallery Keegan won the Ballon d’Or twice while playing for German club Hamburg ( Getty )

Shankly cultivated Keegan’s talent, reportedly telling him after just three days of training at Melwood ‘you will play for England’, something that in fact happened only the following year when Keegan made his debut against Wales at Cardiff.

Keegan joined Liverpool at a time Shankly was cultivating what would become one of the dominant forces in European football, and when he left in 1978 for Hamburg there were not many pieces of silverware the club had not lifted.

In his 230 appearances for the club and 68 goals, Keegan had three league titles, two Uefa cups, one FA Cup, and one European Cup, won in his final season, and under Shankly’s successor, Paisley.

open image in gallery Keegan was signed by legendary Liverpool manager Bill Shankly ( PA )

“Liverpool made me, not just as a footballer but as a person,” Keegan said in 2011. "The people I met – Shanks, Tommy Smith, Ian Callaghan, Ron Yeats – all these people you take something from. The fans made me. When they started singing my name… what am I, five foot seven with Cuban-heeled boots? But [because of them] I was six foot six."

But during his time at Liverpool, aside from the heroics, trophies and memorable goals, one moment also stood out: his sending off in the 1974 Charity Shield match for a fight with Leeds’ Billy Bremner became the first-ever red card in the fixture and become one of Wembley’s most iconic moments.

open image in gallery Billy Bremner and Keegan removed their shirts in protest at the red card in the Charity Shield match, in one of Wembley’s most iconic moments ( Getty Images )

Keegan joined Hamburg in 1977 for a then-German transfer record of £500,000 and went on to win two Bundesliga titles before coming back to England and playing for Southampton, then Newcastle. Hamburg said: With Kevin Keegan, world football loses one of its most defining personalities. We will always cherish an honorable memory of our former champion and two-time Ballon d'Or winner.”

During his playing career, Keegan played against a 19-year-old Diego Maradona, with whom he exchanged shirts at the end of a match, and a 38-year-old Pele. He tangled with the likes of Johan Cruyff, George Best and Michel Platini, and won the Ballon d’Or in 1978 and 1979. He is one of only four Englishman to win world football’s most prestigious individual award, and the only one to do twice.

His England career, however, was affected by the side’s inability to qualify for tournaments, and injury. Keegan earned 63 caps for the national side, scoring 21 goals and captained the team on 31 occasions until his international retirement after the 1982 World Cup, at the age of just 31. Keegan’s only World Cup appearance was limited to just 26 minutes as England were knocked out by Spain, with the forward dealing with a back injury that prevented him featuring in the group stages.

open image in gallery ( PA )

open image in gallery Keegan exchanges shirts with a teenage Diego Maradona after an International friendly match between England and Argentina on May 13, 1980 ( Getty Images )

Keegan might have only played for Newcastle for two seasons, but he was popular with the supporters, and it was there he finished his English professional career at the age of 33. But it was a relationship that prepared for him to take the managerial reigns at the club almost eight years later.

At the time Newcastle were battling relegation in the second tier of English football, and Keegan not only saved the club from slipping further down the football pyramid, but into the Premier League for the 1993-94 campaign the following year.

In 1996, the club finished second, their still-highest ever Premier League finish, and Keegan would make a key signing before his departure the following year, the return of Newcastle-born Shearer one year after he became a Premier League champion with Blackburn Rovers.

open image in gallery Kevin Keegan brought Alan Shearer back to Newcastle, who went on to become the club’s record goalscorer ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery Keegan was loved as a manager at Newcastle and was known as ‘King Kev’ ( Getty )

open image in gallery Keegan’s battle with Sir Alex Ferguson’s Manchester United is one of the great Premier League title races ( PA )

Keegan taught Newcastle how to dream. “Kevin was one of the few who connected, especially with Newcastle fans, he had in abundance, passion, he gave everything,” said the former striker Micky Quinn. “He got within a whisker of winning a Premier League. He loved the fans. A working class connection - very few ever get that connection - that love and warmth from the fans and back. They adored him."

After a short break, Keegan took charge at Fulham, but he was appointed England manager in February 1999. He memorably resigned after defeat at the hands of Germany in the last match played at the old Wembley, resigning five minutes after the match after just 20 months in charge.

Keegan’s tenure as England manager was in the latter stages of his career, he went on to manage Manchester City, before declaring his retirement from the sport in 2005.

However, one club tempted him back into the fold and he returned to St James’ Park in January 2008, but he publicly split from the board and he left in September of the same year, and Keegan’s public spat with Mike Ashley proved an irreparable difference.

Keegan took a back seat from the limelight and aside from a few dinner events, spent time with his wife, Jean, and two daughters, Laura and Sarah.

Police are searching for suspects in connection with a weekend break-in at the home of Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley.

Police in Tredyffrin Township, Pennsylvania, about 20 miles (32 kilometers) northwest of Philadelphia, were called to the home early Saturday for a report of a burglary in progress. When they arrived, they said the suspects had fled.

“Mr. Barkley and his family were not harmed during this incident,” police said in a news release. They released a photo of a white SUV, saying it may be involved in the break-in.

Police said they did not receive any other reports about break-ins in the area. Police were investigating the possibility that Barkley’s home was targeted.

The Chester County District Attorney's office is assisting in the investigation.

“We are asking the public to help us identify those responsible by checking any home security cameras for suspicious activity in the area” from early Saturday, the office said in a statement.

Police and the district attorney's office did not immediately respond to email and phone messages seeking comment Monday.

Phone messages seeking comment also were left with representatives of the Eagles and Barkley.

In May, Argentine police arrested two Chilean citizens suspected of being part of a transnational gang that orchestrated burglaries at the homes of well-known athletes, including stars from the NBA and NFL.

According to local police, the two were part of a crime ring that targeted the homes of prominent athletes in the U.S. and Argentina, including NFL stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce and former tennis player Juan Martín del Potro.

Targets also included the homes of NBA players Luka Doncic and Mike Conley Jr.

In 2024, the NFL issued a security alert to teams and the players’ union following the burglaries involving the homes of Mahomes and Kelce.

Barkley took a step back from his record-setting 2024 season when his 2,504 yards rushing in the regular season and playoffs were the most ever, as Philadelphia’s offense was less potent last season. He still managed to rush for 1,140 yards and scored nine total touchdowns.

News.title: The best bars and nightlife in Lyon
News.content:
While drinking in this gourmet city remains firmly rooted in the surrounding Rhône Valley’s ancient wine-growing heritage, new-gen addresses have embraced world cocktail culture in style. They’re using Lyon’s long-envied gastronomic know-how and rich bounty of local seasonal produce to create some sensational new drinks and food pairings as only the French can. Artisanal spirits meanwhile are increasingly fashionable: cornichon gin, Mezcal-fuelled soirées at chef Carla Kirsch’s gourmet tacos joint in Croix-Rousse, and the stunning Christian Drouin gin and pine-needle liqueur cocktail with stick of Comté cheese to stir I recently had at Hôtel Dieu’s Le Dôme bar all spring to mind.

Come the warmer days of spring and summer, the city’s fervent café-life spills onto pretty pavement terraces, while floating bars moored along Les Berges du Rhône (the landscaped river banks of the Rhône’s Rive Gauche or Left Bank) hum with after-dark dance parties and festivities. Clubbing remains fairly mainstream.

News.title: How to have the perfect holiday in France’s gastronomic capital
News.content:
Calling all bon vivants. This is your city. Within seconds of tucking into a traditional andouillette (tripe sausage) or modern vegetarian cuisine in a jam-packed bistro, admiring fine art in a Renaissance abbey, or getting delightfully lost in a traboule (secret passageway) used by 19th-century silk weavers, you’ll quickly realise that Lyon is a city that knows how to live well.

Enthralling, cinematic and richly storied, after living here for 10 years, I still find myself being surprised by a walled garden I never knew, a fresque (wall mural) suddenly popping up on a riverfront wall, a new museum or river boat route.

Street-smart Romans first spotted the city’s extraordinary topography, founding Lugdunum (Lyon’s predecessor) in 43BC on the sunny slopes of Fourvière. And to this day, this basilica-crowned hill above Lyon’s quaint Unesco-listed Old Town (Vieux Lyon) is the perfect perch for clocking the mighty Rhône and Saône rivers that wend their way so gracefully through the centre.

The city’s quays, landscaped with peaceful water gardens and floating bars, buzz night and day – while culture lovers can explore a bounty of museums. Then there’s the gastronomy: among France’s finest, thanks to the unfaltering creativity and sass of city chefs, both past and present.

News.title: The 16 best things to do in Lyon
News.content:
Few dedicated foodies make the pilgrimage to Lyon without dining once chez Paul Bocuse, be it at the late chef’s mythical, out-of-town gastronomic temple in Collonges-au-Mont d’Or (which lost one of its three stars in 2020, having held three since 1965) or at the more affordable Comptoir Paul Bocuse inside landmark covered market Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse. Across the street, admire a larger-than-life portrait of the iconic chef, frescoed onto the side of a building. Inside the market, the moules glacées (cold mussel ‘soup’) at oyster and shellfish specialist Maison Merle and a gooey round of Saint Marcellin cheese from Fromagerie La Mère Richard are other local legends. Avoid buying fruit and veg here unless you have to – weekly outdoor food markets elsewhere in the city are cheaper.

To sample future talent in the Lyonnais kitchen, mingle with students over lunch, dinner or drinks and live music at La Commune – an innovative food court that hosts chefs aspiring to open their own restaurant in Lyon. Resident chefs cook up a storm at La Commune for maximum six months, meaning an ever-changing rollcall of epicurean excitement at this unique culinary incubator.

To extend the experience further afield, consider a road trip along a section of the Vallée de la Gastronomie, stretching 620km (385 miles). In Lyon, the gourmet route delves into the secrets behind chef Joseph Viola’s award-winning duck foie gras and sweetbread pâté en croûte (think French-posh pork pie) and the city’s distinctive offal-based bouchon (Lyonnais bistro) cuisine.
