News.title: Spain win World Cup in triumph of football over Argentine thuggery
News.content:
Spain should have won far more comfortably, but the European champions lived up to the claim made by their coach Luis de la Fuente and proved they are the best team in the world, having beaten the favourites France in the last four.

Spain won this tournament for the second time, 16 years after the first. Now there is just one nation chasing a “second star”, the one beaten by Argentina in Atlanta last Wednesday.

If England ever want to win this again then here is the blueprint. This is how the game should be played. Get the ball, keep the ball, love the ball, move the ball. Try to play. Be brave and stay brave. It is not complicated, but it requires a re-education.

Maybe one day English football will grow up and cherish ball-players of their own, rather than Manchester City signing Rodri, who was magnificent here until he tired, or Arsenal with Martín Zubimendi, who successfully replaced him.

Rodri was named player of the tournament, in recognition of the football his nation played and the 30-year-old’s importance to to their system. He is their heartbeat and metronome. England do not just need to find a Rodri, but cherish whoever that is.

News.title: Hamilton takes out Russell as Antonelli stretches lead with Belgian GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix from Spa-Francorchamps. The story of yesterday and in fact the weekend was of everyone trying to dislodge Kimi Antonelli from the top of the timesheets. Spoiler alert if you did not watch qualifying: they failed.

That is not to say the fight wasn’t a half-decent one. Max Verstappen and Red Bull were the closest challengers in the end, demonstrating an element of revival during a tricky season. Whether that will continue during the race is hard to know. Verstappen certainly thought he would have been further down the field without the tremendous tow he received from Isack Hadjar, his Red Bull team-mate, in the final sector.

Lando Norris also pushed Verstappen, though was almost half a second down on Antonelli’s time in the end. Unfortunately he will not be able to take advantage of a start from third place because he takes a 10-place grid penalty. George Russell, who has managed to reduce his Mercedes team-mate’s advantage to just 25 points in the past few rounds, was fourth and will start third. He did however, have a difficult session once again, finishing more than half a second off his team-mate.

He was at a loss to explain this. Well, he knows where he lost most of the time: on the straights. But he still does not understand exactly why it is happening. The good news for him is that third place is often the most optimal starting position at this track.

Will that be the case today? Let’s see...

News.title: Ryan Fox matches father Grant’s sporting folklore with Claret Jug
News.content:
It’s the final day of the Open Championship, golf’s oldest and most-prestigious major. The leaderboard offers up hope of a seesaw day where little-known-of golfers tussle it out with big names under the north-west English sun. All in all, it should be an exciting day.

But, as with the past two days, we head into the round with talk dominated by a certain Bryson DeChambeau. It’s as frustrating and annoying as it is, in these days dominated by social media/content etc etc, painfully predictable. So let’s get the DeChambeau news out the way. Having been fairly hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on Friday, the YouTube content creator had a tantrum, threatened to withdraw, caused a delay in the release of third-round tee times, before turning up and shooting a one-under 69 to lie four behind the leader heading into today.

That’s not all, The Bryson DeChambeau Show carried on after yesterday’s round where James Corrigan takes up the script...

Bryson DeChambeau marched straight to the offices of the R&A after being heckled with a cry of “you’re a cheat” on Birkdale’s 18th green on Saturday. As the controversy over his two-shot penalty from Friday’s second round rumbled on, Telegraph Sport understands DeChambeau, who shot a third-round 69 to lie four shots off the lead of the Open, asked R&A chief executive Mark Darbon for his scorecard from Friday. It is against policy so his request was rejected. DeChambeau then went back to the recorder’s hut and asked if they had it. Again, the answer was in the negative. It is unclear why he wanted it, but a theory emerged that he wished to put it on his social media channels.

All in all it is pathetic posturing that you’d expect from a stroppy teenager. He’s only three off the lead and has the game to win at Royal Birkdale, he’d do well to forget the perceived slights (whatever they may be) and get on with trying to win the Claret Jug.

Oh, and to add another scene to the soap opera Rory McIlroy doubtless spoke for many inside and outside the rope when he called out DeChambeau saying: “Yeah, look, I won’t pretend to be up here and defend Bryson. I’m not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it’s for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.”

So, I think it’s best we focus on the golf today and not the theatrics and sorry antics of the American.

Sam Burns, his playing partner yesterday, was brilliant as he backed up his 62 of Friday with a five-under 65. He leads by two on 10 under and is the man to beat. Lurking behind with intent are a host of big names and big hitters – Ryan Fox (eight under), Si Woo Kim (eight under), Lucas Herbert (six under), Ludvig Aberg (seven under) and the man himself YouTube’s very own DeChambeau (six under).

Also in with a hint of a hope is Tommy Fleetwood, the hometown boy in search of his first major, the Englishman will start the round on five under.

Stay here for all the action, where I hope all the talk during and after the day’s round is focused on the winner’s brilliance rather than the emotions of DeChambeau.

Sports.title: Fifa launch formal investigation into Argentina World Cup final brawl as Leandro Paredes red card decision revealed
Sports.content:
FIFA have opened a formal investigation into the disgraceful scenes that marred the end of the World Cup Final.

In an unprecedented outbreak of ill-tempered violence, Argentina players and staff lined up to attack Spain as they celebrated their victory.



Video images captured assistant boss Roberto Ayala punch Spain schemer Dani Olmo in the face during a heated exchange.

Midfielder Leandro Paredes launched into two Spain players, throwing a series of punches at Eric Garcia and Gavi.



Defender Nahuel Molina squared up to Rodri and appeared to swing a leg at him while former Manchester City defender Nicolas Otamendi accused ex-Etihad team-mates Rodri and Aymeric Laporte of bad-mouthing his side in a bid to influence the officials ahead of the game.

Other skirmishes broke out across the pitch with Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni having to intervene to try to break things up.

It all came after Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez was sent off after picking up a second yellow card, for a shocking foul on Pau Cubarsi, in stoppage time at the end of normal time just eight minutes after being booked for dissent.

He later begged for forgiveness from the Argentine faithful.

Paredes, who somehow escaped being sent off after the match, was a human wrecking ball after his arrival from the bench for the second half.

It was initially thought that Paredes had been red-carded, but Fifa have now told SunSport no action was taken immediately after the final whistle.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Liverpool’s Alexis Mac Allister went unpunished for a horrible early lunge on Olmo, while even Lionel Messi joined the list of shame as he suggested Marc Cucurella should be sent off for covering his mouth as the pair passed each other.

It left Fifa with a catalogue of “crimes” to consider with a formal probe launched after they received the reports from the various match officials, including Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic.

Argentina’s shameful decision to turn their back on Spain’s trophy lift was in keeping with their behaviour through the knock-out stage, including the assaults and goading of England during their semi-final win last week.

That included substitute Valentin Barco running 60 yards across the pitch from the dug-out to celebrate Fernandez’ equaliser in the face of John Stones.



Incredibly, Scaloni backed his players, claiming: “I’m so proud of how we competed.”

Argentina face a heavy fine while Paredes is in line for a ban although there is no timescale on the investigation.

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan was the miner’s son who became a superstar on and off pitch with two Ballons d’Or and his trademark perm
Sports.content:
FOR a man of few inches, Kevin Keegan had an awful lot of nicknames.

Mighty Mouse. Wor Kevin. King Kev.

The miner’s son who dug out silverware for a living.



A serial winner as a player and a manager who got bums OFF seats, fans flocking to his messianic fervour.

A fearless “Superstar”, with a splash of Brut and a trend-setting perm, who had the courage of his own convictions but bridled at any who questioned him.



Whose infamous post-match melt-down at Leeds would have launched a thousand memes in the modern era.

And whose later managerial career included ignominiously quitting the England job in the Wembley toilets.

Yet with his death at the age of 75, a huge hole has been left in the lives of generations of supporters on Merseyside, the South Coast, North East and northern Germany.

Unlike so many of today’s pampered millionaires, Keegan was an authentic working class hero.



Proud of his North East roots, even though he grew up among the collieries of South Yorkshire and made his fledgling professional steps in Lincolnshire, with Scunthorpe.

It was the school of hard knocks, Keegan among the players who shared driving duties to away games in the club minibus and was carpeted for crashing the club groundsman’s vintage tractor.

Standing just 5ft 7in – when he wanted a trial at Doncaster he was informed he should try to be a jockey instead – Keegan made up for his lack of stature with constant commitment, in his initial role as a bustling attacking midfielder. And one who was never scared to stand up for himself.



When Bill Shankly and Liverpool came in for him in 1971, Keegan blithely insisted he was being paid £45 per week at Scunny, refusing to back down from his demands for a rise before agreeing what was a £33,000 move – a huge sum for a lower league player.

It was to prove a major moment, for Keegan and his new club, as he immediately supplanted Alun Evans as John Toshack’s strike partner.

That the pair had little in common off the pitch, it was a different story on it, an instinctive understanding that brought 189 goals between them in six seasons, with Keegan clocking up an exact century.

His combative nature never abated, most famously shown in the 1974 Charity Shield where he was sent off, shirt slung over his shoulder, for an old-fashioned brawl with Leeds skipper Billy Bremner. It was an iconic image.

While starring for Liverpool, where he won seven trophies including three championships, Keegan was among those tarred by England’s failures through the 70s.



There were moments of brilliance but also controversy, with Keegan brutally beaten by airport security guards in Belgrade when the Yugoslav FA had not prepared a welcome party and then walking out on Don Revie’s squad after being dropped for a British Championships game with Wales in 1975.

Three days later, chastened into returning to Revie’s fold by Shankly’s Liverpool successor Bob Paisley, he ran Scotland ragged at Wembley as England won 5-1.

He and Revie made up sufficiently for Keegan to be named captain the following after injury curtailed Gerry Francis’ international career at the age of just 24 but it was in Liverpool red that he truly thrived.



Which made his decision to accept the BBC offer to take part in the popular Superstars show in 1976 even more remarkable.

Can you imagine a Premier League striker being allowed to even ride a bike these days, let alone race one round a cinder track, resulting in a brutal fall that left skin scattered everywhere and an open graze? Keegan got back on his feet, demanded a re-race and finished second quickest.



The following summer, there was a greater shock. Days before the European Cup Final win over Borussia Monchengladbach, where he induced Berti Vogts into conceding the penalty that sealed the 3-1 win he had agreed a £500,000 move to Hamburg.

It saw a six-fold increase in his £22,000 a year wages – and the start of Keegan’s ascent into the stratosphere, even if he could not prevent another World Cup qualification failure.

Keegan was the inspiration of Hamburg’s unexpected Bundesliga triumph in 1979, when he won his second consecutive Ballon D’Or trophies – the only Englishman with multiple wins – and starred as they reached the European Cup Final against Nottingham Forest in 1980, won by a John Robertson strike.

He even released a pop song that made the German top 10. They were Head Over Heels for him.

That game in Madrid came three months after Southampton boss Lawrie McMenemy had announced Keegan was to return to England to play for Saints and it was in 1980 that ITV began screening his adverts for Brut, alongside Henry Cooper. Another famous partnership.



Two seasons at The Dell brought 43 goals in the build-up to the 1982 World Cup, where injury deprived Bobby Robson of both Keegan and Trevor Brooking until the final minutes of the goalless draw with Spain that saw them eliminated unbeaten.

But a fall-out with McMenemy saw him make a £100,000 move to second division Newcastle, where he became an instant legend, the key man as promotion was clinched in 1984 before he retired.

For eight years, Keegan was out of the game although he appeared on TV screens as an ITV pundit.

But in 1982, he was back – and back at Newcastle, too, replacing the sacked Ossie Ardiles as the Toon faced potential relegation to the third tier.

Once again, he was to prove an inspiration and the leader of a captivating movement, producing a swashbuckling, all or nothing style of football that brought a new generation of Tyneside disciples.



Promotion was followed by consolidation and in 1996, a team that seemed set to win the title – before his maverick approach over-gilded the lily, the signing of Faustino Asprilla disturbing the balance of the team.

Newcastle, 10 points clear of Manchester United at Christmas, had seen that lead whittled away to four when the Red Devils came to the North East on March 4, with 11 games left.

Keegan’s side dominated but could not find a way past Peter Schmeichel and Eric Cantona crashed home the only goal.

When Keegan slumped over the pitchside advertising hoarding after Stan Collymore’s stoppage-time strike clinched an astonishing 4-3 roller-coaster at Anfield a month later, he summed up the despair.

But Newcastle came again, only for Keegan’s anger at Fergie’s drip-drip of barbs bursting over when his side beat Leeds at Elland Road to stay in the contest with two games to go.



Pushed to the end of his tether, Keegan, gesticulated wildly as he went after the Scot, who had “gone down in my estimation”, infamously declaring: “You can tell him now, if you’re watching it, we’re still fighting for this title.

“He’s got to go to Middlesbrough and get something, and… and… I’ll tell you, honestly, I will love it if we beat them, love it!”

Fergie did, too, telling his players Keegan had lost control. United won their last two games, Newcastle drew theirs and finished four points adrift.

Keegan’s response was to spend a world record £15m to bring Alan Shearer back to his home town but the spark was ebbing. He attempted to quit three times before it was accepted in January 1997. The response was as if there had been a death in the Newcastle family.

By September he was at Fulham, initially as chief operating officer before replacing the axed Ray Wilkins at the helm but Glenn Hoddle’s England sacking – for comments about the disabled – brought a call for King Kev to bring the fun back.



He agreed, initially on a caretaker basis, Paul Scholes scoring a hat-trick in a Euro 2000 qualifier against Poland, but swiftly as permanent boss.

England scraped into the play-offs, Scholes scoring twice against Scotland at Hampden but then losing 1-0 at home in the second leg.

He subsequently admitted he would have quit if the Scots had gone through.

Euro 2000 was a debacle, a them and us squad, suggestions of a card school culture and a group stage elimination despite Shearer scoring England’s first competitive winner against Germany since 1966, Keegan increasingly angry at the negative media scrutiny.

Four months later, in what was the final game at the original Wembley, Keegan was jeered off after Didi Hamann scored the only goal, resigning in the dressing room toilets and explaining: “I don’t want to outstay my welcome. The fans put me in the job but they feel it’s time for me to go.”



There was still four seasons at Manchester City – the highlight a 4-3 FA Cup win at Spurs from three down at half-time with Joey Barton sent off walking to the dressing room at the interval – and a short-lived final return to Newcastle in 2008.

It was never going to last with Mike Ashley.

After that, Keegan went back to the TV studio but it was the start of him fading from public sight.

Yet for so many, those who watched him play, or watched his Newcastle side in their pomp, there can only ever be smiles.

Sports.title: Who was Kevin Keegan’s wife Jean, and how many children did couple have?
Sports.content:
KEVIN Keegan has sadly died aged 75 following a battle with stomach cancer.

The legendary England player and manager passed away surrounded by his family on July 20, 2026.



In a heart-breaking tribute, close friend Peter Graves wrote: “It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75.

“The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.



“Kevin, a double Ballon D’or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather.

“The family would like to thank Kevin’s incredible medical team for all their support.

“This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy.”

The former Newcastle manager’s family revealed he was diagnosed with stage four stomach cancer in January 2026.

A statement released by his loved ones read: “Kevin Keegan was recently admitted to the hospital for further evaluation of ongoing abdominal symptoms.

“These investigations have revealed a diagnosis of cancer, for which Kevin will undergo treatment.”



The sporting community rallied around in support, with Newcastle United also releasing a statement: “Our former player & manager, Kevin Keegan will undergo treatment after being diagnosed with cancer having been admitted to hospital for further evaluation of ongoing abdominal symptoms.

“King Kev. We’re with you every step of the way. Hoping for a full and speedy recovery.”

The club then displayed the message ‘We’re all here with you King Kev’ on the LED board ahead of their narrowly fought victory against Leeds United.

Who was Kevin Keegan?

A prominent striker for Liverpool during their dominating period under highly decorated manager Bill Shankly, he helped lead the Reds to three English league titles, the European Cup, two Uefa Cups and the FA Cup.

During his playing days, he was nicknamed “King Kev” and “Mighty Mouse”.



After leaving Liverpool, he headed to Hamburg on a British record transfer of £500,000, where he won the Bundesliga.

He received two Balloon d’Ors while at Hamburg, in 1978 and 1979 respectively.

Keegan returned to England in 1980, first joining Southampton before heading to Newcastle.

After retiring, he transitioned into management for spells in charge of Newcastle, Fulham and Manchester City.



He also took charge at international level, spending over a year as England boss between 1999 and 2000.

Who is Kevin Keegan’s wife, Jean?

Keegan met his bride-to-be Jean Woodhouse on the waltzers at Doncaster fair in September 1970.

Just a teen at the time, he approached her, but said she had a crush on Manchester United superstar George Best.



Keegan chose to lie about his job, revealing: “I said that I worked at the steelworks.

“Telling them I was a footballer would have sounded too flash, even though I was an unknown playing for a small club.”

Keegan managed to win Jean over, and the couple moved to Liverpool after his £35,000 switch to Anfield under Bill Shankly.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They became engaged and later married in September 1974.

The couple share two daughters, Sarah and Laura Keegan.

Sports.title: Premier League club announce badge change as crest blasted for ‘struggling to perform’
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE have revealed their plans to change their current badge, in order to modernise and develop as a club and a brand.

The Magpies said their current badge, designed in the 80s, “struggles to perform” in modern times.



It was reported in June 2025 that the Saudi ownership would not stick with the current crest.

At that time one option was to completely reinvent it, but that now seems to be off the table.



Today’s club statement read: “We have been transparent about a basic challenge: our current crest, designed in the late Eighties, struggles to perform in a modern setting.

“Its complexity affects how we show up. Its intricacies and irregularities make consistent, high-quality reproduction impossible – from modern digital platforms, to broadcast environments and merchandise.



“In an increasingly competitive global landscape, it constrains our ability to represent this club to the standards it truly deserves.

“But it’s not just a question of competing commercially, it’s also one of pride.

“This is not change pursued for the sake of it. Evolution is essential, ensuring our crest remains authoritative, legible, and unmistakably Newcastle.

“Not just for supporters today, but for every generation that follows.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In recent years the club met with a wide range of audiences, hosting dedicated supporter events and focus groups.

On the back of this, they have pledged “to simplify and protect what already exists”.

The castle was considered the most essential element of the crest, with the shield and the seahorses also set to remain.

The new badge will NOT be circular, with the club thinking that would be too “generic”.



In terms of what to expect next the club said: “This is your club, and your voice will continue to shape what comes next.

“In August, we will hold workshops with key fan groups to hear where we are, what you’ve told us, and what happens next.

“We will also host sessions, in person and online.”

Sports.title: Last picture of Kevin Keegan shows football icon smiling with Premier League legend ahead of England World Cup opener
Sports.content:
THE LAST picture of Kevin Keegan shows the legend smiling with his Premier League pal ahead of England’s World Cup opener.

The former Newcastle manager’s family revealed he was diagnosed with stage four stomach cancer in January.



The diagnosis came after “King Keegan” was admitted to hospital with ongoing abdominal problems.

Kevin was last pictured in good spirits on June 17 alongside pals Peter Graves and Sam Allardyce.



Graves shared a snap with Keegan ahead of the first England game of the World Cup.

He captioned the post: “Three Lions! In great company for the opening England match tonight. Big Sam and KK. Come on England”

Fans were quick to praise Kevin’s good health, adding that the former England captain was “looking well”.

Earlier this year, Keegan appeared at the Tyne Theatre and vowed to “say goodbye” properly to his beloved Newcastle at St James’ Park.



Opening up to host Graves, he said: “I want to say goodbye. I didn’t get the chance when I left (Newcastle United) last time…”

The two time Ballon d’Or winner also bravely spoke out about his diagnosis and chat with his doctor.

He added: “They said we have a top doctor with this new way of fighting what you have got. Which is stage four cancer.

“He was a Liverpool supporter so I went to meet him. I knew I wouldn’t be walking alone, if you know what I mean.”

Today, friend Peter Graves confirmed Kevin’s passing with a touching tribute.



He wrote: “It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75.”

A statement from his family in January read: “Kevin Keegan was recently admitted to hospital for further evaluation of ongoing abdominal symptoms.

“These investigations have revealed a diagnosis of cancer, for which Kevin will undergo treatment.

“Kevin is grateful to the medical team for their intervention and ongoing care.

“During this difficult time, the family are requesting privacy, and will be making no further comment.”



The football legend is widely regarded as one of the greatest England players of all time.

He has won three First Division Championships, two UEFA Cups, one FA Cup and a European Cup in his playing career at Liverpool.

As a manager, he is famous for his passionate “I would love it if we beat them” rant at Sir Alex Ferguson.



It came before his Newcastle side threw away a 13-point lead and lost the Premier League title to Man Utd in 1996.

After quitting as Newcastle manager in 2008, the adopted Geordie vowed never to return to St James’ Park while Mike Ashley remained.

The ex-England boss spent two seasons on Tyneside as a player before so nearly landing the Magpies’ first league title since 1927 as manager in 1996.

Ashley brought him back in 2008 but they went on to have a bitter falling-out over the club’s transfer policy.

Their feud came as Keegan took charge of Newcastle for a second time in 2008, but lasted only 22 games.



Keegan insisted he would only go back to St James’ Park once the unpopular Sports Direct tycoon had gone.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He had previously managed the Magpies for five years between 1992-97, in what was their most successful spell in recent history.

Keegan scored 49 goals in 85 appearances for the club as a player.

Sports.title: ‘My Hero. My manager. My friend’ – Alan Shearer leads tributes to Newcastle and England legend Kevin Keegan after death
Sports.content:
ALAN SHEARER has led tributes to Kevin Keegan following his death at the age of 75.

Keegan’s close friend Peter Graves shared the news of his passing on Monday afternoon.



He said: “It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75.

“The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.



“Kevin, a double Ballon D’or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather.

“The family would like to thank Kevin’s incredible medical team for all their support. This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy.”

Shearer was one of the first ex-players to pay tribute to the legendary player and manager, writing: “My Hero. My manager. My friend. Sleep easy Boss.”

The 55-year-old played under the management of Keegan when he first joined Newcastle ahead of the 1996/97 season.

Newcastle have also paid tribute, taking to social media to write: “We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan, one of the most iconic, influential and deeply loved figures in our club’s history.

“Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters.”



Southampton added a tribute to the two-time Ballon d’Or winner, writing: “We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan.

“Kevin signed for the club in 1980 as the holder of the Ballon d’Or and brought great joy to fans at The Dell and across the football world.

“Our thoughts are with his family and friends at this difficult time.”

Tributes for Keegan have been shared over social media by fans and former players.

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said: “RIP Kevin Keegan. One of the greatest players this country has ever produced, trophies & goals galore, double Balon d’Or winner shows he was an absolute giant of the English game.



“One of the most important men in making @LFC what it is today.”

A statement from Manchester City read: “Everyone at Manchester City is devastated to learn our former manager Kevin Keegan has passed away, aged 75.

“Kevin was a transformative manager who brought optimism and vibrancy to City during his four-year spell in charge.

“The promotion campaign in 2001/02 will never be forgotten, and Kevin then established us once again as a top Premier League side in the years that followed.

“Our thoughts are with Kevin’s family and friends at this very difficult time.”



An Everton statement added: “Everyone at Everton is saddened to hear of the passing of Kevin Keegan.

“Our thoughts are with his close family and friends at this difficult time.”

And a post from the official England account read: “We are incredibly saddened by the news that Kevin Keegan OBE has passed away.

“Kevin earned 63 international caps and scored 21 goals between 1972 and 1982, before managing the #ThreeLions from 1999 to 2000.

“Our thoughts and condolences are with Kevin’s family, friends and former clubs.”

Keegan kicked off his professional playing career in the 1960s with Scunthorpe United and went on to play for Liverpool, Hamburger, Southampton and Newcastle.

He was also capped 63 times for the England national team and scored 21 goals.

Sports.title: Belgium manager Rudi Garcia quits after famous World Cup demolition of USA in controversial Balogun clash
Sports.content:
RUDI GARCIA will leave his role as Belgium manager when his contract expires at the end of the month.

The Belgian FA confirmed it will not extend the Frenchman’s deal beyond July 31, bringing his 18-month spell in charge to an end.



Garcia took over from Domenico Tedesco in February 2025 and helped the Red Devils retain their place in League A of the Nations League.

He also guided Belgium to the 2026 World Cup, where they reached the quarter-finals before being knocked out by eventual champions Spain.



Garcia said: “After discussions with the RBFA, we have decided not to extend the excellent journey we have shared over the past 18 months.

“I leave Belgium in League A of the Uefa Nations League and among the top eight teams in the world.

“I would like to thank my outstanding group of players, Sports Director Vincent Mannaert, and the fans who supported us throughout this World Cup.

“I wish Belgium every success as they continue the generational transition that I was proud to help initiate.”

Belgium’s World Cup was shrouded in controversy after their last-16 clash against the USMNT.

US star Folarin Balogun was spared an automatic one-match suspension following US President Donald Trump’s Fifa intervention.



The rescinded suspension permitted the Monaco striker to start against Belgium and has since blown up into a Fifa v Uefa civil war.

Sports director Vincent Mannaert added: “Rudi Garcia has unquestionably played a key role in restoring the Belgian Red Devils.

“He was appointed national coach in a challenging sporting and financial context.

“Thanks in particular to his commitment and experience, team cohesion was restored and a strong result was achieved at the most recent Fifa World Cup.



“On behalf of the federation, I would like to warmly thank Rudi and his assistants for the past 18 months.

“Together with my team, I am currently preparing for a new cycle, including the appointment of a new national coach.”

Sports.title: How brave Kevin Keegan faced stage four cancer battle with cheeky sense of humour before tragic death aged 75
Sports.content:
BRAVE Keegan tragically revealed he had stage four cancer just weeks before he died – but kept up his famous sense of humour.

The Newcastle and Liverpool legend had battled stomach cancer since January but close pal Peter Graves today announced he has passed away.



Keegan, 75, was admitted to hospital earlier this year, revealing to fans that he was receiving treatment.

Following a car accident, Keegan needed to have an operation, and it was during scans conducted by doctors that his cancer was discovered.



His family also shared that Kevin had been experiencing abdominal issues, which was explained by the stomach cancer diagnosis.

Stage four cancer is the most advanced stage of cancer that means the disease has spread to other parts of the body.



A statement released at the time read: “Kevin Keegan was recently admitted to hospital for further evaluation of ongoing abdominal symptoms.

“These investigations have revealed a diagnosis of cancer, for which Kevin will undergo treatment.



“Kevin is grateful to the medical team for their intervention and ongoing care.”

In June, Kevin opened up about the terrible diagnosis for the first time, and said he wanted to say a “proper goodbye” to his beloved football club.

Speaking with Peter Graves at the Tyne Theatre, Kevin shared how he had discussed treatment with doctor at the time of the diagnosis.

He said: “They said we have a top doctor with this new way of fighting what you have got. Which is stage four cancer.



“He was a Liverpool supporter so I went to meet him. I knew I wouldn’t be walking alone, if you know what I mean.”

Speaking about a cheeky quip he made, Keegan added: “I asked the consultant what his success rate was… He said, ‘About three out of 10’.

“I said to him if he was a striker and he only scored three times out of 10 I’d drop him. But so far, whatever he did to me, it’s working.”

The two time Ballon d’Or winner also described a meeting with a doctor about his treatment.



He said: “I was in a car accident and, through that, I had to have an operation. Whilst having the scan for the operation, they found out I had cancer.

“They said they had an absolute top doctor for fighting what you have got, which is stage four cancer.

“So I went to meet him. He’s a Liverpool supporter so I knew I wouldn’t walk alone.

“He said, ‘Kevin, this new treatment, I’ve got a tremendous strike rate’. I said, ‘What’s your strike rate?’

“He said, ’33 per cent’. I thought it would be 80 per cent, 90 per cent. 33 per cent!



“I’m still here at the moment.”

During another moment at the theatre, Keegan told the audience: “I want to say goodbye. I didn’t get the chance when I left (Newcastle United) last time…”

After the event, the beloved ex-footballer received a standing ovation.

The football legend is widely regarded as one of the greatest England players of all time.

He has won three First Division Championships, two UEFA Cups, one FA Cup and a European Cup in his playing career at Liverpool.



Keegan scored 49 goals in 85 appearances for the club as a player.

And as a manager, he is famous for his “I would love it if we beat them” rant at Sir Alex Ferguson.

Following his tragic death, his close friend Peter Graves wrote a heartbreaking tribute this afternoon: “It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75.

“The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

“Kevin, a double Ballon D’or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather.

Keegan enjoyed an illustrious career as both a player and manager. His work at Newcastle United helped transform the Magpies into one of the best club's in the country and the Toon have also paid an emotional tribute.

Today, we mourn the loss of a true giant of our history, and at the appropriate moment, we will carefully consider how we shape a lasting tribute to Kevin’s remarkable life and legacy. The Reds also paid tribute to Keegan and said: "We are deeply saddened by the passing of the legendary Kevin Keegan and mourn his loss.

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher tweeted: "RIP Kevin Keegan. One of the greatest players this country has ever produced, trophies & goals galore, double Ballon d'Or winner shows he was an absolute giant of the English game.

"Above all that, Kevin forged an extraordinary bond with Newcastle, built on the roots of his father, Joe. He understood our people. He embraced the North East with a passion that was genuine and unwavering, and in return, he earned his rightful place in the hearts of millions.

"Kevin’s impact will not be measured by appearances or results. It will live on in the memories he created with club and country, the dreams he inspired wherever he went, and the generations of supporters around the world who fell in love with football because of him.

"At this profoundly sad time, we send our love and deepest sympathy to Kevin’s wife Jean, his family, friends and all who had the privilege of knowing and working alongside him.

‌



"Today, we mourn the loss of a true giant of our history, and at the appropriate moment, we will carefully consider how we shape a lasting tribute to Kevin’s remarkable life and legacy.

"Rest in peace, King Kev."

View 8 Images Kevin Keegan has died aged 75 (Image: Julian Hamilton/Daily Mirror)

Fellow Toon icon Alan Shearer simply added: "My hero. My manager. My friend. Sleep easy boss."

‌



One of the England legend's last appearances was on Tyneside in May where he told the audience: "They said we have a top doctor with this new way of fighting what you have got, which is stage-four cancer.

"He was a Liverpool supporter so I went to meet him. I knew I wouldn’t be walking alone, if you know what I mean." Keegan first revealed in January that he had cancer.

After a 'really tough time,' he felt well enough to commit to this appearance at the Tyne Theatre in Newcastle, the city that he loved and where the fans adored him.

He joked that he couldn't form a dream strike partnership with Peter Beardsley and Chris Waddle as he "wasn't very fit at the moment."

‌



Liverpool, for who Keegan made 323 appearances during the 1970s, said: "Liverpool FC is deeply saddened and mourning the passing of the legendary Kevin Keegan.

"The former Reds No.7, who appeared 323 times and scored 100 goals for the club across six seasons, died at the age of 75 on Monday after being diagnosed with cancer last year.

"The thoughts of everyone at the club are with Kevin's family and friends at this hugely difficult time.

View 8 Images Keegan and David Beckham in 1999 (Image: Toby Melville/PA Wire)

‌



"One of just four Englishmen to win the Ballon d'Or, Keegan also represented Scunthorpe United, Hamburg, Southampton and Newcastle United during a playing career in which he was regarded as a hero wherever he went.

"Keegan also received 63 caps for his country – 31 as captain – and netted 21 times.

"He then moved into management with spells at Newcastle (two), Fulham, Manchester City and the England national team.

"Keegan's association with Liverpool began when he arrived from Scunthorpe as a 20-year-old in May 1971.

‌



"He endeared himself to Kopites soon after joining, scoring on his debut in the 1971-72 league opener against Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

"A forward partnership for the ages with John Toshack would blossom, and with it came success for the second of Bill Shankly's great Liverpool teams.

"Keegan produced 41 goal involvements (22 goals, 19 assists) in year two of his Anfield career, helping deliver the First Division title and a maiden European trophy.

"In the two-legged UEFA Cup final with Borussia Monchengladbach, the bona fide superstar scored two of his side's goals and set up another in the 3-2 aggregate win.

‌



"He was the standout performer again in the 1974 FA Cup final with a double at Wembley to down Newcastle, where in the future he would be known as 'King Kev' for more terrific service.

View 8 Images Keegan signed fellow Liverpool great Robbie Fowler for Manchester City in 2003 (Image: PA/PA Wire)

"The 1975-76 Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year award came on the back of another league and UEFA Cup double for the Reds.

"Keegan had signalled his intention to move abroad ahead of 1976-77, shocking the footballing world given his status.

‌



"He signed off at Liverpool in the best way possible, though, by firing in 20 strikes en route to earning a third league winner's medal and lifting the club's first European Cup.

"He won the Ballon d'Or in two of his three seasons at Hamburg and then returned to his homeland for the remainder of his time in football.

"'Liverpool made me, not just as a footballer but as a person'," Keegan said in 2011.

"'The people I met – Shanks, Tommy Smith, Ian Callaghan, Ron Yeats – all these people you take something from.

‌



"'The fans made me. When they started singing my name… what am I, five foot seven with Cuban-heeled boots? But [because of them] I was six foot six'."

"Our 'Mighty Mouse', his legacy at Liverpool will be forever etched in history.

"Rest in peace, Kevin Keegan."

The official England account added: "We are incredibly saddened by the news that Kevin Keegan OBE has passed away. Kevin earned 63 international caps and scored 21 goals between 1972 and 1982, before managing the Three Lions from 1999 to 2000.

‌



"Our thoughts and condolences are with Kevin's family, friends and former clubs."

Another of Keegan's former clubs, Southampton, posted: "We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan.

"Kevin signed for the club in 1980 as the holder of the Ballon d’Or and brought great joy to fans at The Dell and across the football world. Our thoughts are with his family and friends at this difficult time."

View 8 Images Keegan as manager of Newcastle in January 2008 (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

‌



Fellow Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher added: "RIP Kevin Keegan. One of the greatest players this country has ever produced; trophies and goals galore. Double Ballon d'Or winner shows he was an absolute giant of the English game. One of the most important men in making LFC what it is today."

The son of a Geordie-born miner, he was a pioneer of the modern game, negotiating his own contracts, appearing in TV ads and moving abroad to further his career at the peak of his fame with Liverpool in the 1970s.

Keegan won the three League titles, two UEFA Cups, and the FA Cup, moving to Hamburg after winning the European Cup with the all-conquering Merseyside giants in 1977.

He was then twice voted European footballer of the year. In a 2013 interview, at the launch of his Soccer Circus business in Scotland, he said: "I have never been scared to do something new. I did the adverts, I did the record, I moved abroad, I have always been one of those people who say, 'Why not?' rather than 'Why?'".

‌



"I am very lucky in that I enjoy meeting people, it is a great help in life, not just business." It made him a hugely popular figure during his playing career, as England captain, and later as a manager, even as the national side struggled under his leadership.

With typical honesty, he stepped down after admitting that he did not think that he was good enough. He had stints in charge of Fulham, and Manchester City, but it was his two spells at Newcastle Utd which defined his managerial career.

In the late 90s, he managed a United side nicknamed 'The Entertainers' because of their fearless brand of attacking football.

As a player, he was equally fearless, and famous for his Brut adverts with Henry Cooper, pop singles, curly perm, and an episode of the TV show 'Superstars', filmed in Bracknell in 1976, where he fell in a bike ride but got back on again despite being injured.

‌



View 8 Images Keegan was a legendary player for Liverpool in the 1970s and 1980s (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

In his 2018 autobiography 'My Life in Football', dedicated to his wife Jean and former Liverpool boss Bill Shankly - 'two people who have given me so much' - he wrote: 'It never ceases to amaze me how many people think that my lifetime achievements consist of, in rough order: the time I crashed off my bike in television's Superstars, my perm, and my top-40 record with Head Over Heels in Love."

He met Jean in 1970 while riding the waltzers in Doncaster; he told her that he worked at the steelworks as he thought saying he was a footballer would sound 'too flash'.

They married in 1975 after his £35,000 transfer to Liverpool. Born in Armthorpe, near Doncaster, in 1951, his grandfather, Frank, was a hero who saved lives in the 1909 West Colliery mining disaster in Co Durham.

‌



His family kept a photo of the 30 survivors; Kevin bore a striking family resemblance to Frank. From humble beginnings in Yorkshire, he went on to become a sporting hero to millions of football fans.

View 8 Images Keegan during his last game as England manager in October 2000 (Image: Ross Kinnaird/Allsport/Getty Images/Hulton Archive)

His dad Joe and uncle Frank loved Newcastle Utd and told young Kevin all about their favorite players of yesteryear, Hughie Gallacher and Jackie Milburn.

Kevin was born at his aunt's house because it had electricity, making childbirth safer; his dad bought his first football boots after winning a bet on horses.

‌



At 15, he and two friends ran 50 miles from Nottingham to Doncaster, which he said prepared him for the physical demands of football.

He worked as an office clerk at Pegler Brass Works before a first professional football contract with Scunthorpe Utd as a 17-year-old.

Three years later, legendary Liverpool manager Bill Shankly spotted his undoubted talent, signed him and converted him into a striker.

Forming a lethal partnership with Welsh striker John Toshack, Keegan scored 100 goals in 323 games before a British record £500,000 transfer to Hamburg.

‌



View 8 Images Newcastle United fans hold a flag of Kevin Keegan prior to the Emirates FA Cup third-round match against Bournemouth (Image: (Annabel Lee-Ellis/Getty Images))

He was their top scorer with 17 league goals when they claimed the Bundesliga title in 1978-79. He was European Footballer of the Year in both the 1977-78 and 1978-79 campaigns during his three-year spell. Keegan moved to Southampton in 1980.

He was the PFA Player of the Year in 1981-82 before making the switch to Newcastle in 1982, retiring as a player two years later.

He scored 21 goals in 63 appearances for England and captained his national side 31 times, making a late appearance in the 1982 World Cup in Spain after struggling with a back injury.

‌



Joining Newcastle Utd as manager in 1992, he led the club to the second-tier title and promotion into the Premier League in 1993. In 1996, his side let a 12-point lead slip before he famously said, "I would love it if we beat them", in an emotional live TV outburst during the tense run-in with Alex Ferguson's Manchester United.

Keegan said friends had 'love it' as their ringtone and insisted that he was 'comfortable enough in his own skin' to see the funny side.

FIFA boss Sepp Blatter sent a fax to commend the Geordies' attacking football after the epic 4-3 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield in 1996.

"The main reason I went to Newcastle was Kevin Keegan," former England midfielder Rob Lee recalled. "He was my idol. I was a West Ham fan as a kid but Keegan was the first superstar I had pictures on my wall of."

‌



Striker Les Ferdinand told how he travelled to Birmingham to see him when he was about to sign for Aston Villa. "Just his enthusiasm and his vision for where he wanted to take the club," Ferdinand said, "he had me sold after a couple of minutes."

Keegan left United in 1997 and took over at Fulham a year later, before being appointed as England boss in February 1999. He left that role in October 2000 following a 1-0 defeat by Germany in a 2002 World Cup qualifier, the final game at the old Wembley Stadium.

View 8 Images Keegan in action for England in 1979 (Image: Peter Robinson/EMPICS Sport/PA Wire)

Keegan, though, returned to club management with a four-year spell at Manchester City prior to a short eight-month stint back at Newcastle in 2008. He left, and later successfully claimed unfair dismissal, after falling out with then club owner Mike Ashley.

‌



He told how he secretly returned to St James' Park in disguise for a fan's party.

I met him for the last time there for the unveiling of Alan Shearer's statue in 2016.

He gave a friendly hello, recognising me from our many encounters on assignments for the Daily Mirror down the years, first as England manager and then at Fulham with 1966 World Cup legend George Cohen.

He never refused an autograph request, cracking jokes about his time with Shearer at the club that they both loved with a passion.

‌



Keegan had the common touch, and that is why he remained such a hugely popular figure throughout his career, even when his stint as England boss came to an untimely end.

He said of his approach: "I buy good players and let them play." His loved ones confirmed his cancer diagnosis.

In his life story, the legend of the game told fans: "I want people to dream about their football club.

"We should all be dreamers at heart."

Sports.title: The people of Gaza watch the World Cup final amid the ruins of their homes
Sports.content:
The people of Gaza watch the World Cup final amid the ruins of their homes

Football fans, many of them children, stood amid the rubble of Gaza to support Spain as they beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time and many cheered for the Spanish team

View 4 Images Gaza refugees watching the World Cup final (Image: Getty Images)

An estimated 1.5 billion people tuned in to watch the World Cup final.

‌



But there can be few more devoted fans than the hundreds who gathered around giant screens showing the match next to the bombed-out buildings of Gaza.

‌



They stood amid the rubble of their homes to support Spain as they beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time. They cheered for the Spanish team because of the country's support for the enclave during the conflict with Israel.

‌



Giant screens, erected earlier in the tournament, have offered residents a welcome respite from daily hardships. Numan Abdullah, a Gaza resident who watched the match, said: “We came together to support Spain because it has stood by the Palestinian people for years."

View 4 Images The people of Gaza watch an earlier round of the World Cup in the US (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Argentina World Cup fate decided after calls to ban finalists from next tournament READ MORE :

FIFA launch investigation into Argentina after 'disgusting' World Cup final scenes READ MORE :

He said the gathering also carried a message of peace and solidarity with countries that stand with Palestinians. “We are a people who seek peace,” he added. Tragically, aid worker Mohammed al-Wahidi, who helped organise the screenings, died in an Israeli airstrike earlier this month.

View 4 Images The people of Gaza also watched the Egypt v Argentina game earlier this month

Al-Wahidi, 65, was an English teacher before the war but became a senior official with the Egyptian Relief Committee in Gaza. He worked for the Egypt-backed organisation that has played a prominent role in humanitarian relief efforts.

‌



Locals said that he became a familiar face in shelters across the territory because he preferred to remain in the field rather than directing operations from an office. As of late April, the UN had recorded the killing of at least 593 aid workers since the war began, including eight since Israel and Hamas agreed to a ceasefire 10 months ago.

View 4 Images The funeral of aid worker Mohammed al-Wahidi, who helped organise the screenings, and died in an Israeli airstrike. (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Aid workers set up the screenings of the World Cup games, in a bid to raise morale in the camps, especially among young children. The matches shown included the controversial 3-2 defeat of Egypt by Argentina.

Article continues below

The Israeli military launched a campaign in Gaza in response to the unprecedented Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on Oct 7, 2023. It saw 1,200 people killed and 251 taken hostage.

At least 73,118 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since then, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry. Their figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Sports.title: Argentina World Cup fate decided after calls to ban finalists from next tournament
Sports.content:
Argentina World Cup fate decided after calls to ban finalists from next tournament

Ugly scenes unfolded on the pitch after Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain

View 3 Images Argentina players conducted themselves poorly at the World Cup (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto, Getty Images)

Argentina will automatically qualify for the World Cup 2030 despite calls for the nation to be banned from the next edition of the tournament. The 2022 winners failed to retain the World Cup trophy on Sunday at MetLife Stadium after losing 1-0 to Spain, thanks to an extra-time goal from Ferran Torres.

‌



Just as had been the case throughout their dramatic semi-final victory over England, Lionel Scaloni’s side were the weaker team across the 90 minutes but used dark arts tactics to even the playing field. That was clear to see with their overly-aggressive tackling, off-the-ball confrontations and attempts to get Spain’s players sent off.

‌



Having got away with various transgressions, Argentina themselves had midfielder Enzo Fernandez sent off for a second yellow card following a reckless challenge in stoppage time. The South American nation’s players then sparked a mass brawl after the final whistle blew, with several players landing blows on their Spanish counterparts in a shocking display of unsportsmanlike behaviour and lack of grace in defeat.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The unsavoury scenes, of which there were plenty against England too, disgusted much of the football world. Sections of football fans online have even called upon FIFA to officially ban Argentina from the World Cup in four years’ time due to their string of recent controversies.

However, Argentina have already booked their place at the next tournament without having to qualify, given they are one of an unprecedented six nations hosting at least one match in the 2030 edition, along with Spain, Morocco, Portugal, Paraguay and Uruguay.

‌



Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay will each host one match to honour the centenary of the World Cup. While the rest of the tournament will continue elsewhere, they don't have to go through the arduous qualification process in a special exception to the usual procedure.

View 3 Images There have been calls by some fans for Argentina to be banned from World Cup 2030 (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport, CameraSport via Getty Images)

The 1930 World Cup, the first edition of the tournament, was played in and won by Uruguay. They beat Argentina in the final, while Paraguay have been included as the home of CONMEBOL, the first and only football confederation at that time.

‌



Argentina’s most ardent critics will be furious to learn the nation will still be involved, having taken to Reddit to call for their banning.

One user posted: "Their behaviour throughout this tournament should see Argentina banned from the 2030 World Cup. Maybe sitting a World Cup out will sort out their attitude." Another wrote: "They celebrated in English players‘ faces and then fought when they lost. Absolutely despicable… zero class."

A third chimed in with: "They should 1000% get banned for such poor behaviour," while a fourth added: "Exactly. Totally agree."

‌



Another pointed out: "Fully agreed. Show authority and ban foul behaviour. Political statements, violence and constant reckless play should be enough to earn them a disciplinary action."

With regards to Argentina and bans, midfielders Fernandez and Leandro Paredes will miss at least the next two international fixtures after being sent off. As Spain’s players ran onto the pitch to celebrate at the final whistle, Nahuel Molina appeared to throw a punch towards Spain captain Rodri's stomach too.

View 3 Images Argentina escaped punishment for holding up a controversial and political banner (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Paredes, who had already been yellow carded during the game and was lucky to escape a second booking, then seemed to punch Spain defender Eric Garcia in the throat before Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni ran over to separate the players.

Seconds later, Paredes turned his attention towards Gavi, throwing the Spain midfielder to the floor before shoving him in the face while grabbing his substitute's bib. Argentina coach Roberto Ayala also appeared to hit Dani Olmo in the throat.

After the victory over England in the penultimate round, Argentina’s players held up a controversial banner thrown onto the pitch by their supporters, which claimed the Falkland Islands belong to Argentina. Despite FIFA making it very clear that political statements had no place at the World Cup prior to the tournament, the Argentine players escaped punishment for that misconduct.

Sports.title: 'He's got to get an answer' - Russell to 'get back up' amid mystery problems
Sports.content:
George Russell says he has been "knocked down" but will "get back up" after the latest setbacks to his world championship challenge at the Belgian Grand Prix

Having cut his title deficit to Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli from 68 points to just 25 points over the previous three rounds, benefitting from two reliability problems on the Italian's car, Russell dropped 50 points behind on Sunday at Spa-Francorchamps when his race lasted just five corners before a collision with Lewis Hamilton.

But Russell's post-race frustration at his early exit, and difficult race weekend as a whole, was aimed not at his former team-mate but instead towards weekend-long power issues on his Mercedes car that he said had left him vulnerable to such an incident on the first lap.

The Briton has been searching for stronger form for several months amid a failure to match Antonelli's pace on a consistent basis but, in a social media post on Monday, he resolved to keep fighting on in the championship chase.

"Knocked down, we get back up," Russell wrote.

"No matter how many times.

"So many tough moments this year but I will not stop fighting,"

Wolff explains Russell's power problems

While Mercedes are still working to get to the bottom of the mysterious straight-line speed issues afflicting Russell's car, team principal Toto Wolff explained after Sunday's race how two separate problems contributed to the Briton's difficult weekend.

On the first deployment issue in the sessions before race day - which Russell had initially hoped would be corrected by driving style changes but was not the case - Wolff said this had compromised the Briton's speed in the final sector of the long Spa-Francorchamps lap relative to Antonelli.

"The power units are so complex, in the way you harvest, the way you deploy, the interaction from the driver," said Wolff of 2026's new engines which feature a near 50-50 split between electrical and traditional internal combustion output.

"We have a super strong package - championship-winning chassis and power unit, but we're still trying to give it our best to fix the reliability issue.

"And sometimes a new regulation (irregularity) happens. With George, over the weekend, there was definitely something on the engine that we have identified that meant he only had less energy to deploy into Turn 18 - that was the most visible.

"It's good that we spotted it here because in Budapest, which is not energy starved, it would have been more difficult to identify.

"But it still doesn't make it better for him. And that probably accounted for half the gap or a little bit more that he had to Kimi."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard with George Russell as he crashes out of the Belgian GP after contact with Lewis Hamilton.

All eight of the grid's Mercedes-powered cars were then hampered by a separate and "new" boost problem out of Turn One at the start of Sunday's race.

Andrew Shovlin, the team's trackside engineering, said Russell's had been "more extreme" and meant he was an effective sitting duck on the Kemmel Straight as the two Ferraris moved past him, with Russell eventually spinning into instant retirement in the Les Combes braking zone after contact with Hamilton, whose Ferrari understeered into the Mercedes.

Wolff added: "All Mercedes engines had a lack of energy out of Turn One, so that wasn't only George. It affected him more than Kimi, but also Kimi had that issue to a certain degree.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell pointed to an issue with the car as a reason for his collision with Lewis Hamilton during the Belgian GP.

"And that meant that he didn't come out at the end of the straight in P3, but P5. So, he lost his two positions, and then obviously the accident with Lewis."

'He's got to get an answer' - what now for Russell heading to Hungary?

Speaking during Sky Sports F1's post-race show in Belgium, Karun Chandhok suggested that Russell would want concrete engineering explanations before this weekend's race in Hungary as to what exactly was causing the confusing straight-line speed problems.

"I think he's got to go back and try to get clear answers from an engineering sense," said Chandhok.

"We've all had conversations this weekend with people from Mercedes, and the sense we're getting is that they don't have a clear answer.

"They've got to go back, they've got to look at the data, have a couple of days to digest it between now and Budapest, because he can't go on to the next race weekend with a four-tenth deficit in straight-line speed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch all of George Russell’s unlucky moments so far this 2026 Formula 1 season.

"You're taking a pencil to a sword fight, so there's no point doing that. He's got to get an answer, and if it means they have to change the power unit and take a penalty, then maybe they have to do that to try to clear away this doubt.

"Because as a racing driver, arriving at a weekend having doubt in the package or the car you've got and whether you've got a fair fight, is an awful place to be. He will be looking for clear engineering-led answers, I think."

Russell said in interviews after the race that, having also run into technical issues earlier in the season most notably in China and, when leading, in Canada, he was now "numb to the disappointment".

Asked how he could keep his driver's spirits up, Wolff said: "You have to understand that the driver is very emotional when these situations happen. But on the other side, as a Formula 1 driver, you're part of a very elite group.

"I think it's quite an honour to drive a Mercedes. Sometimes we let ourselves down. And it's just the driver, but it's also us.

"It's valuable constructor points that we lose in our fight against Ferrari. So, I hope the numb feeling goes away. We will try to help to recreate optimism and positivity."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell spins after contact with Lewis Hamilton and his race ends on the opening lap, but was the Ferrari driver's penalty fair?

Wolff, who has known the 28-year-old Russell for over a decade, added: "I think all of the drivers, at least the ones that I have worked with, when they have difficult spells, and it happens to any sports person, you need to find a way of motivating or building up.

"George has his way, and I'm definitely trying to do that. I've known him for such a long time, I understand the frustrations, and the team is 100 per cent there."

Sports.title: What does Rogers' move mean for Chelsea's squad?
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers is set to join Chelsea in a British-record £117m from Aston Villa - and his arrival is set to have a knock-on effect for Xabi Alonso's Blues.

The England international - who arrived for his medical on Monday after returning from the World Cup - had also been linked with Arsenal, but he is set to arrive in the west of London instead.

Here, Sky Sports News reporters Kaveh Solhekol and James Savundra examine why Rogers is keen on the move and what the forward's imminent arrival could mean for the rest of the Chelsea squad.

Why Rogers and Chelsea wanted each other

KS: Some people may be surprised that Rogers has decided to swap Aston Villa for Chelsea, but the player really did have his heart set on moving to Stamford Bridge and once the bid materialised, he accepted it straight away.

Playing for Chelsea next season means he will not be playing in Europe. If he had stayed at Aston Villa, he would have been playing in the Champions League, but Chelsea are still a big club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Rogers has been spotted arriving for his Chelsea medical after the Blues agreed a £117m deal with Aston Villa.

They have big ambitions and under their new manager Alonso, they are very serious about challenging for the big trophies again.

Rogers is obviously a fantastic player, we've all seen that, but he is also very physically imposing. There's been a feeling at Chelsea that one thing their side has been missing is some real physical presence and they've been trying to address that this summer. They've gone some way towards it by signing a player like Rogers.

How might Cole Palmer be impacted?

KS: I remember being at the game between Aston Villa and Chelsea last season and that was billed as being a game between Cole Palmer and Rogers - who was the better No 10? I think on the day, Aston Villa ended up winning that game and Rogers played really well.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League clash between Chelsea and Aston Villa.

So you have to ask the question - will Chelsea be able to have both Rogers and Palmer in the same side? The two players know each other well. They were together at Manchester City and Palmer's famous 'cold' goal celebration was first invented by Rogers. It'll be up to Alonso to see how he can accommodate both those players in the same side.

There are no indications that Chelsea want to sell Palmer, far from it. He's tied down to a very long contract and just before the end of the season, he gave a newspaper interview in which he said he was happy at Chelsea and was happy living in London.

There have been reports seeming to suggest that he may want to move back to the north west, that one day he wants to play for Manchester United, but I think he would cost so much that there are not many clubs who would be able to buy Palmer if Chelsea wanted to sell him.

What is the situation for Enzo Fernandez?

Image: Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez was sent off in Sunday's World Cup final (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II)

KS: Enzo Fernandez has come out on a few occasions and made it clear that he fancies a move to Real Madrid, but we had some sort of clarity on that a couple of weeks ago when the LaLiga club released a statement saying that they were not involved in any negotiations.

They had not made a move to sign Fernandez and if they did want to sign him, then they would do everything through the proper channels. Real Madrid have a very good relationship at the highest level with Chelsea, so I'm sure if they were interested in signing Fernandez, it would simply be a matter of picking up the phone.

I think what Chelsea would tell them is every player has his price and Fernandez's price is £120m. If you want him, that is what it's going to take to buy him. But as of yet, Real Madrid have not made a move for him to our understanding.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at the best goals Morgan Rogers has scored during the 2025/26 Premier League season.

JS: Fernandez's position remains largely unchanged despite the arrival of Rogers. Alonso confirmed his intention to keep the Argentine at his unveiling last week and noted to Sky Sports News that he was looking forward to working with the midfielder.

Having committed more than £100m to buy Fernandez in 2023, Chelsea would be looking to recoup at least a similar level of money to sanction a sale.

Real Madrid have ruled themselves out of the running to signing Fernandez - for now - which leaves few viable suitors.

The Argentine enjoyed success under Enzo Maresca, but is a move to Man City likely in a window in which City have spent £116m already on Elliot Anderson and given the tension between the clubs given the Maresca saga?

How might Rogers fit into Alonso's system?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol breaks down Chelsea's £117m deal for Morgan Rogers and what he could add to Xabi Alonso's side.

JS: Alonso refused to give any clues last week when it came to his playing system. His main success as a manager at Bayer Leverkusen saw Jeremie Frimpong and Alex Grimaldo dominate as wing-backs. If he adopts his preferred formation at Chelsea, Rogers is most likely to operate as a wide attacking midfielder.

Given the struggles of Alejandro Garnacho and Jamie Gittens last season and the presence of Palmer, you would expect Rogers to be favoured on the left.

There are real similarities between the positions picked up by Palmer, Rogers and to some extent Joao Pedro. Whilst the trio thrive in fluid positions rather than a strictly fixed structure, Alonso will need to lay out a clear framework with specific roles.

Are Chelsea sales required?

JS: Chelsea are Club World Cup champions. They have not always been world class on the pitch during the BlueCo era but they have been world-class sellers.

They have already ensured enough outgoings this summer to cover the £117m cost of Rogers. Chelsea raised around £130m from selling players like Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Tyrique George and the sizeable compensation from Man City for poaching Maresca certainly helped too.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After Andrey Santos' £50m move to Manchester United, here's a look at some of his best moments from last season with Chelsea

The likes of Reece James, Palmer and Joao Pedro are seen as untouchable assets, but other members of the first team squad will depart for sizeable fees - Garnacho, Nicolas Jackson and Trevoh Chalobah are likely to bring in another £100m if they go.

Despite not being in Europe this season, Chelsea will still be subjected to UEFA's stricter financial rules. Last summer, Chelsea entered into a four year settlement agreement with UEFA for breaching regulations and they'll look to demonstrate progress in showcasing financial sustainability following this window.

Chelsea brought in around £300m from player sales last summer and given the need to move on a number of defenders who are surplus to requirements and at least one striker, it could be another impressive summer of trading.

Where does this deal leave Arsenal?

KS: It's a long transfer window… but I'm not sure Arsenal would have been prepared to pay £117m for him.

Perhaps you could argue that Chelsea need him more at the moment - Arsenal are the reigning champions and they are in the Champions League as well.

A lot of these deals only happen when somebody puts their money where their mouth is. We can talk about the fact that Arsenal were potentially interested in Rogers, but it's Chelsea who made a bid and that has been accepted by Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Former England forward and manager Keegan dies aged 75
Sports.content:
Former England player and manager Kevin Keegan dies aged 75 after battle with cancer; Keegan's family announced in January he had been diagnosed with stage four cancer; legendary forward was twice named Ballon d'Or winner in 1978 and 1979

Kevin Keegan dies aged 75: Former England forward and manager passes away after battle with cancer

Sky Sports takes a look back at the incredible career of former England manager and legendary footballer Kevin Keegan, who has died at the age of 75

Kevin Keegan has died at the age of 75.

It was announced in January that the former England player and manager had been diagnosed with stage four cancer, with his family revealing he was set to begin treatment.

"It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75," a statement from Keegan's family read.

"The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

"Kevin, a double Ballon d'Or winner, was a much-loved husband, father and grandfather. The family would like to thank Kevin's incredible medical team for all their support. This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy."

Image: It was announced in January Kevin Keegan had been diagnosed with stage four cancer

Keegan was considered one of the best players of his generation and enjoyed a stellar playing career, making almost 750 club appearances, lifting the First Division trophy three times with Liverpool and winning the Ballon d'Or back-to-back in 1978 and 1979 while playing for Hamburg in the Bundesliga.

Image: Liverpool's Ian Callaghan, Kevin Keegan and Ray Clemence parade the FA Cup

Image: Liverpool striker Kevin Keegan during a match with QPR

Seven years after his retirement, he took his first coaching role as manager of a struggling Newcastle team in February 1992. The Magpies were in danger of being relegated to Division Two but Keegan kept them up and then led them to the Premier League in his first full season in charge. Then, in 1996, he took Newcastle to within touching distance of their first top-tier title since 1927.

Ballon d'Or x2

Newcastle were Premier League title favourites for most of that 1995/96 season, at one stage being 12 points clear of Manchester United. But a dramatic collapse from Keegan's side coupled with a Sir Alex Ferguson-inspired Man Utd winning 13 of their last 15, eventually saw Newcastle finish second by four points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at Kevin Keegan's iconic rant aimed at Sir Alex Ferguson in the midst of the title race between Newcastle and Manchester United

Late defeats at the hands of Liverpool and Nottingham Forest in the run-in saw United eventually haul them in. As the pressure mounted on a beleaguered Keegan, who was desperate to deliver the title to a passionate Newcastle fanbase, his infamous "I'd love it.." post-match interview after victory at Leeds, aimed at Sir Alex, among others, unfortunately characterised his time at St James' Park.
