However he will return to St James’ Park for the first time since an ill-fated spell as boss in 2008, next season, to wave to the crowd before kick-off, as long as Eddie Howe – who he backs fully – says it won’t be a distraction. That will raise the roof. 'I want to say goodbye. I didn’t get the chance when I left the club last time…' Keegan tells the audience. He means goodbye from his second managerial stint, but it was poignant given the circumstances. As Keegan continues his treatment, there could not have been any better therapy than a room full of mutual love and adulation.

Sports.title: FIFA launch investigation into Argentina's shocking World Cup final post-match behaviour... as new footage shows what really sparked final-whistle brawl
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

FIFA will investigate the behavior of Argentina's bitter players after the World Cup final descended into violence following their defeat on Sunday.

The probe into the violent final-whistle scenes in New Jersey comes just as footage reveals the exact moment that sparked the ugly brawl.

The South Americans were outplayed by Spain in a drab encounter at MetLife Stadium, with Lionel Messi and his teammates unable to disrupt their rivals with the same aggressive, physical tactics that unsettled England in the semi-final.

Barcelona star Ferran Torres bagged the winning goal in extra time to seal Spain's second World Cup triumph – after first winning the trophy in 2010 – leaving Messi, 39, in tears at the final whistle.

However, the action continued following the final whistle as a brawl broke out between the two sides, resulting in a red card for Leandro Paredes.

The Argentina midfielder was sent off for grabbing Eric Garcia by the neck and punching Gavi in the face before pushing him to the ground in appalling scenes at full time.

FIFA is now set to open disciplinary proceedings into the red card issued to Paredes, with the role of other players and officials also set to be investigated, according to The Times.

Jaja, es Molina el que empieza todo pegando a Rodri. Hay que largar a todo el clan loser este ya, que encima de macarras, perdedores e insoportables, son malísimos. pic.twitter.com/Wk6C0fwABY — The Lion (@loloutlaw) July 19, 2026

FIFA is set to launch an investigation into the violent behavior of Leandro Paredes and other Argentina players after the World Cup final descended into violent scenes

The move came after ugly scenes at the end of the game which Spain won 1-0 after extra time

New footage has revealed that a punch landed on Spain captain Rodri sparked the brawl

Some of Argentina's players lost their heads as Spain's substitutes and staff ran on to the pitch to celebrate their victory.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina hit Spain captain Rodri in the torso as he was running by, resulting in the midfielder squaring up to his rival.

That saw players from both teams pile into the melee, before Paredes threw punches.

Elsewhere, 53-year-old assistant coach Roberto Ayala was also caught landing a punch on Spain's Dani Olmo at full time.

In the aftermath of the ugly brawl, DAZN Spain claimed Argentina defender Nicolas Otamendi complained to Rodri about La Roja's pre-match comments alluding to officiating concerns ahead of the final.

The South Americans had benefitted from a series of questionable decisions heading into the showpiece event, with the Manchester City midfielder raising concerns before the final.

'You and [Spain team-mate Aymeric] Laporte. Both of you,' he said to Rodri.

'You spent the time crying and complaining about the referees, my friend. But you shouldn't have spoken before the match, you know that? Didn't you see what he said this week?'

Argentina were thuggish throughout the World Cup final, just as they had been when they beat England in the semis.

Torres's 106th-minute winner came after Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the 93rd minute following a reckless challenge on Pau Cubarsi – which summed up the South Americans' deplorable approach to the game.

por que el raton ayala le pegó una piña a dani olmo jajdjsjsjsj pic.twitter.com/ZNkBpPAcjU — Peñargrol (@CAPArgento__) July 20, 2026

Some of Argentina's players lost their heads as Spain's substitutes celebrated the win

Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni tries to intervene as Paredes clashes with Eric Garcia

Spain shared fears of roughhouse tactics from Argentina, and their concerns came to fruition with Enzo Fernandez sent off for a shocking challenge on Pau Cubarsi

Astonishingly, Fernandez complained about his dismissal for a second yellow, before attempting to get Chelsea team-mate Marc Cucurella sent off for covering his face while talking to Messi.

New laws state that footballers who cover their mouths when speaking to a player from the opposing team must be sent off, but replays showed Cucurella was simply scratching his nose as he spoke to Argentina's captain.

Paredes was also fortunate not to be sent off for a second bookable offense in regular time for a foul on the edge of the box which presented Lamine Yamal with a last-gasp free-kick before extra-time.

Following the game, the 2022 champions collected their silver medals from FIFA boss Gianni Infantino and US President Donald Trump on the stage but opted not to watch as Spain lifted the trophy – despite it being customary in finals of major tournaments.

Instead, the Argentina players, coaching team and staff walked over to the end where the majority of their fans were sat and turned their backs as their rivals celebrated.

Footage shows Spain players holding the World Cup trophy aloft as gold confetti explodes behind them, with the Argentina team facing the other way.

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, with the first one coming in the 117th minute.

There were an estimated 1.5 to 1.8 billion viewers tuning in to watch the summer tournament's showpiece finale, which saw Trump take center stage during the trophy lift.

Argentina players decided to turn their backs to Spain's World Cup trophy lift on Sunday

Donald Trump took center stage as Spain lifted the World Cup trophy on Sunday afternoon

The President refused to step aside to allow the victorious Spaniards to have their moment in the spotlight.

Trump and Infantino handed out various awards to match officials and players, before officially welcoming the team up to the stage to lift the World Cup trophy.

The President presented the prestigious title to Spain captain Rodri, who took great pleasure in raising it aloft.

Much like when he presented the Club World Cup title last summer, Trump stood awkwardly alongside the Spain squad as they lifted the trophy and celebrated wildly.

It seemed as though, when Spain were about to perform the trophy lift, Infantino had attempted to usher Trump away from the players – though the President remained where he was.

He stood to the side of the team as the confetti cannons went off at MetLife Stadium, clapping and grinning while Infantino laughed off Trump's awkward cameo.

Loud boos had come from the stands when Infantino and Trump made their way onto the pitch, as fans made their feelings on the pair undoubtedly clear.

Fans noted that one Argentina star – Tottenham defender Cristian Romero – completely ignored the President as he collected his medal from Infantino.

It appeared as though Infantino attempted to usher Trump away – but the President remained where he was

In a video which swiftly went viral on social media, the Argentinian could be seen receiving his silverware from Infantino before waltzing past Trump on stage.

Meanwhile, the President also presented a trio of awards to Spain's stars, including the Young Player of the Tournament, the Golden Glove and the Golden Ball – which were claimed by Pau Cubarsi, Unai Simon and Rodri respectively.

There was a degree of irony in regard to Trump presenting Spain with the World Cup trophy, after previously launching a stinging attack on the country at a UN summit earlier in July for not contributing enough money to NATO.

'Spain is a terrible partner in NATO. They don’t participate. They don’t pay. I don’t want anything to do with Spain. Cut off all trade with Spain, please, including visits,' he said. 'Don’t even talk to them. They’re hopeless, bad people.'

Then, on his way back to the United States on Air Force One, Trump said Spain had tried to improve its standing with him.

'I did have issues, and ​I still do. But Spain, they came back all the way today. Spain was very generous today,' he said.

'They honored a request for lots of payments, and if they didn't, we wouldn't have even ⁠talked to them.'

Earlier in the day, Trump and his wife Melania were seen taking in the action inside a packed MetLife Stadium suite – alongside FIFA president Infantino, Canada's prime minister Mark Carney and Mexico's president Claudia Sheinbaum.

Wayne Rooney savaged the 2026 World Cup final halftime show as he described the performance as 'c**p' and said the 'best part was when it ended' live on BBC

The show delivered a spectacular mix of music, nostalgia and global star power, with the likes of Madonna, Justin Bieber, Shakira and the Muppets all performing under one roof

Trump also shook hands with Spain's prime minister Pedro Sanchez as Infantino stood beside them.

Spain's Queen Letizia and King Felipe VI also greeted the President. Javier Milei, the president of Argentina, reportedly watched the game from home due to 'superstition,' The New York Times reported.

Trump also waved at the crowd from behind the glass.

Inside the private suite, Infantino posed for pictures with the President's son, Eric Trump, his wife, Lara, and their children. Barron Trump also showed up for the big game.

The World Cup final also saw a bizarre half-time show, with Madonna, Coldplay, Justin Bieber, The Muppets and Shakira performing during the 27-minute interval, which was derided by Wayne Rooney.

'To be honest, mine [his highlight] was when it finished. I like a lot of those artists but to be honest I thought it was c**p', he fumed.

'I did honestly. It just didn't get me going. I wanted the football to be back on. It was a bit flat. I like Burna Boy, I like Shakira, I like Bieber but that was too flat.'

Sports.title: Spain's World Cup heroes touch down in Madrid after enjoying £1K bottle of red wine and cigars in their New York hotel before late-night dash to airport
Sports.content:
Spain have landed in Madrid after wasting no time in jetting out of New York in the immediate aftermath of winning the World Cup with the victory over Argentina on Sunday night.

Luis de La Fuente's side secured a second star for their nation with a dogged victory against a difficult Albiceleste at the MetLife Stadium just across the river from Manhattan.

But after lifting the trophy in front of a full house of their adoring fans, La Roja opted not to ring in their victory with a night of partying in the city that never sleeps.

Instead, Golden Ball winner Rodri got the party started in transit, leading a round of singing on the team bus as the jubilant players sped back to their hotel for a team meal, before moving on to Newark Airport.

Back at the hotel, noted oenophile Marcos Llorente enjoyed a bottle of Chateau Rayas Chateauneuf-du-Pape Reserve 2014 - which costs a festive £1,009 to uncork - in his room with team-mates Ferran Torres and Marc Pubil.

The stars then boarded the Airbus A350-941 waiting for them - clad in their team's livery - and took off shortly after 2am local time.

Captain Rodri lifted the World Cup as Spain touched down in Madrid on Monday afternoon

The country's most-likely weary players will now have a little downtime before their parade

Before leaving the tarmac however, the team posed for a group photo with their manager Luis de la Fuente

Join the discussion Should Spain have celebrated more publicly in New York, or was rushing home for a trophy parade the right move?

Spain's players landed at Madrid's Barajas Airport at 2.30pm local time, and stepped out onto the tarmac with the World Cup trophy held aloft.

The reasoning behind flying out immediately after winning the World Cup is thought to be that the team will be welcomed with a trophy parade in Madrid's Plaza de Cibeles - where Real Madrid often host their own celebrations.

The players are now believed to be set for just a little downtime, before heading to the picturesque square to kick-off the party on home soil.

According to Spanish outlet La Razon, officials from Madrid have organised a secure welcome for the players that is set to attract thousands of fans as the team travels to Plaza de Cibeles in an open-top bus.

Once on board the flight, Aymeric Laporte was among the players to pose with the World Cup trophy, giving it a tender kiss in his seat as he soaked up the once-in-a-generation feeling.

Spain had previously celebrated on the pitch with their friends and family, with crossover superstars including seven-time Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz also joining in on the fun.

Players were draped in flags from their regions in the country as they posed for photos and celebrated with loved ones.

But the show was thoroughly stolen by Spain's unofficial talisman Keyne Yamal - the little brother of teen starlet Lamine.

Dressed in a replica Spain jersey with his brother's No. 19 and his own first name emblazoned on the back, Keyne darted onto the pitch at MetLife Stadium, where he then ran straight into his older brother's arms.

Lamine Yamal carried his bags - including an oversized Hermes Birkin bag - off the plane

Spain were in high spirits as they celebrated winning the World Cup on their bus home to Madrid in the early hours of Monday morning

Festivities in the hotel were limited to a bottle of £1,000 red wine drunk by Marcos Llorente, goalscorer Ferran Torres and Marc Pubill

Marc Cucurella and Gavi posed in front of the team's Airbus as they prepared to go home

The airplane arrived hours later as the city of Madrid readied a welcome home fit for heroes

Aymeric Laporte and Alex Baena both posed with the World Cup trophy onboard their plane

Rodri led a bus full of Spanish players in rounds of singing as they headed for Newark airport

Yamal had previously enjoyed a cigar in the lift as he began his journey back to Spain

The prodigal Barcelona star had celebrated earlier on the pitch with his girlfriend Ines Garcia

Yamal was all too happy to accept a hug from Keyne and quickly lifted his younger brother into the air before gently placing him back down on the field and putting a red 'Lamine' baseball hat on the toddler's head.

And that wasn't the only hat Keyne tried on while roaming around the MetLife pitch on Sunday.

A New Jersey State Trooper couldn't help but remove his cap to briefly share with Keyne, who tried it on before politely returning it to the officer.

Yamal also posed with his girlfriend Ines Garcia in a sweet photo on the pitch, with the influencer sharing it with the caption: 'You did it. Congratulations, my love - you're a world champion'.

Later, Yamal was snapped lighting a large cigar as he waited in a lift at the hotel on his journey home.

As high-spirited as Spain's celebrations were, they came in stark contrast to the ugly scenes on the pitch after the final whistle, when Argentina stars including Leandro Paredes attacked Spanish players Eric Garcia and Rodri.

Paredes throttled Garcia and pushed Barcelona star Gavi to the ground, while Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by.

Argentina defender Nicolas Otamendi later complained to DAZN Spain that rival players had been complaining to the media in the build-up to the final.

Argentina players later turned their backs on Spain's trophy lift in their last bitter act following a blue-and-white campaign as noted for its thuggishness as its strong tournament play.

Sports.title: Alan Shearer's wild World Cup party: England legend dances on the table while singing karaoke with Micah Richards as stars celebrate after Netflix confirm they WILL extend £14m deal with Gary Lineker's podcast firm
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England legend Alan Shearer could be seen dancing on a table and singing karaoke during the Rest is Football's post-World Cup party, as they celebrated the show's contract extension with Netflix.

Spain secured a second star on their crest on Sunday afternoon with a dogged 1-0 victory over defending champions Argentina at MetLife Stadium.

Shearer and Micah Richards worked the final with the BBC, with the former in the commentary booth, and the latter on punditry duty alongside Wayne Rooney and Joe Hart inside the ground.

But soon after the coverage came to an end, the pair joined Gary Lineker in the Rest is Football studio in New York to record their final episode of the tournament, before enjoying an after-party.

The 38-year-old posted videos on his Instagram story showing Shearer with a microphone in hand, enjoying some karaoke.

The former England captain was captured singing Rick Astley's 'Never Gonna Give You Up', before he could later be seen finishing off 'Mr. Brightside' by the Killers while dancing on a table.

Micah Richards posted clips of Alan Shearer singing karaoke in what appeared to be a Rest Is Football World Cup wrap party

Shearer was also captured dancing on a table while belting out the Killers' classic 'Mr. Brightside'

The Rest Is Football recorded daily shows throughout the World Cup in a Netflix deal worth a reported £14million, with Richards and Shearer balancing the podcast with their BBC duties.

In the final show, which was broadcast this morning, Lineker confirmed that the podcast will continue on the subscription-based streaming service for the 2026/27 season, starting in August.

'I've got some very exciting news,' Lineker said. 'From the start of the Premier League season, which kicks off in just 32 days, we're back on Netflix, baby!'

The former Match of the Day host then confirmed that episodes of the show will be released on a weekly basis.

It will likely see the iconic trio join forces again to discuss the biggest stories of the weekend, with guests joining on occasion.

During the World Cup, they hosted footballers and celebrities such as Harry Maguire, Patrick Vieira, Maya Jama, Michael McIntyre, and even New York mayor Zohran Mamdani was interviewed by Lineker.

It was not the only show that Lineker was a part of during the tournament, though, with the footballer-turned-presenter also appearing on ITV in a surprise guest slot during the group stage.

In a move that shocked football fans when it was first mooted, Lineker made an appearance on ITV’s coverage of Germany versus Ivory Coast. Lineker humorously introduced the show before ITV host Laura Woods interjected to remind the former England striker of his role.

'Thank you very much for joining us on ITV for this one – another day, another game, another channel,’ Lineker said as he opened the programme before jocularly apologising for slipping into 'old habits'.

Lineker then mocked the BBC, confirming ITV’s breathtaking studio overlooking the Manhattan skyline was real, while his former employers remain at Salford’s MediaCity until the knockout stages.

‘I’ve been doing a show daily for Netflix; we’re at Times Square,' Lineker later continued. 'But I desperately wanted to come and see your set because I think it’s absolutely amazing and I can confirm that it is real.'

Gary Lineker has confirmed that the Rest Is Football's deal with Netflix has been extended to cover the upcoming Premier League season

Lineker remained on the coverage for 20 minutes and jokingly asked whether he had failed the audition before departing.

'If you passed it, you would get my job, so you’ve failed,' Woods quipped.

‘I’ve got no chance of that, Laura,' Lineker replied. 'May I say what a fabulous job you do – you are very good at this.’

Lineker joined Duncan Ferguson, Gary Neville, and Ian Wright as a 'special guest' on ITV's temporarily enlarged panel.

Richards had then jokingly labelled Lineker an 'absolute traitor' on The Rest Is Football, adding '26 years of blood, sweat, and tears for the BBC, and then you go over to the rivals!'

The comment prompted Lineker to jokingly tell Richards to 'shut the f*** up.'

Sports.title: Josh Kerr slams 'appalling' prize money he receives for running the fastest mile ever
Sports.content:
Josh Kerr slams 'appalling' prize money he receives for running the fastest mile ever

Josh Kerr - the new fastest man over a mile - felt the financial reward he was given didn't reflect the magnitude of his achievement

View 2 Images Josh Kerr said he felt short-changed by the prize money he received (Image: British Athletics via Getty Images)

Josh Kerr criticised the $50,000 (£37.2k) bonus awarded to him for breaking the one-mile world record. Kerr's time of 3:42.66 was the quickest in 27 years, toppling previous holder Hicham El Guerrouj's by 0.47 seconds.

‌



The Scotsman sparked scenes of wild celebration in front of a sold-out crowd at the London Stadium. However, the financial reward didn't reflect the achievement in his eyes.

‌



He received the exact same sum from World Athletics as Moroccan El Guerrouj did in 1999. Once the dust had settled, Kerr called out the prize money situation.

‌



"It was a good day for me financially but $50,000 is a ridiculous number," he told The Times. "To get the same amount 27 years later is appalling, not to sound greedy.

Mile record-smashing Scot Kerr praised by track legend Steve Cram READ MORE :

Commonwealth Games 2026 athletes start arriving in Glasgow from around the world READ MORE :

"I know how much that took from investing in myself financially over the last eight years as a professional. I just feel like I’ve been a bit short-changed a little bit."

‌



World Athletics offer a $100k bonus (£74.5k) at flagship outdoor global championships but that sum is halved for Diamond League meetings. Kerr also admitted he had hoped to have "gone a little bit faster," although he was happy to have hit his goal.

View 2 Images Kerr smashed the 27-year world record (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

"It was just incredible, that last lap," he told the BBC. "It was just me, my shoes and the track. I was absolutely deaf in the last 110 metres. I didn't take my foot off the gas, but I started to glide and I was like, 'Oh, wow, this feels incredible.'

Article continues below

"It's incredible because I'm slowing down. So, I was like, 'I better get to the line.' So crossing the finish line, seeing 42-something - anything - was my goal, so it was great.

"I am surrounded by amazing people and was just able to stay consistent, put the work in, and I knew I had 3:42 in me. I nearly lost it there at the end, but I got over the line.

"If I'm to leave my mark on this sport as a British legend, with the legends behind me and following in their footsteps, I have to put in those performances."

Sports.title: Why we are going to see less Rory McIlroy as golf superstar changes his priorities
Sports.content:
Why we are going to see less Rory McIlroy as golf superstar changes his priorities

The two-time Masters champion is taking another long break as he admits no longer being 'fired up' by regular events on the PGA Tour schedule

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy walks onto the first tee box on day four of the The 154th Open (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Rory McIlroy was brilliant at The Open. Brilliant with the adoring crowds, brilliant with the media, brilliant with his playing partners.

‌



Even when it was clear he would not contend for the Claret Jug, McIlroy was one of the Championship’s main draw cards. Only Tommy Fleetwood, the local hero, drew as much attention.

‌



Rory is box office, wherever he goes. Scottie Scheffler is the world number one but McIlroy is the successor to Tiger Woods as golf’s poster player. Which is why his comments after his final round at Royal Birkdale will have alarmed PGA Tour executives. McIlroy is not just the most talented golfer out there, he is the most eloquent. And he gives an honest answer.

‌



Asked if he was not as ‘fired up’ by the PGA Tour as he once was, he replied: “Yeah, that is fair.” And he then elaborated, explaining his priorities have changed and that the new FedEx Cup format meant he could miss more tournaments.

Bryson DeChambeau shows true colours with response to Rory McIlroy taunts at The Open READ MORE :

Behind the scenes at Sky Sports Golf as plans for 2027 Open already put in place READ MORE :

He explained: “I think the change where it doesn’t matter where your are in the top 30 going into the Tour Championship … it’s like I just need to be in the top 30 going in there to have a chance to win a FedEx Cup.

"So why would I care about the first two?”

‌



It is a fair point. But it also shows McIlroy is becoming more and more selective when it comes to the business of competing in golf tournaments.

From the day he donned a second Green Jacket to the opening day of the 154th Open Championship, McIlroy played in five events. Five events in more than three months.

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy drew huge followings at The Open despite struggling for top form (Image: Warren Little/Getty Images)

‌



Look at the top five on the final Open leaderboard. In that same time, Ryan Fox played in nine events, Cameron Young in seven, Sam Burns and Scottie Scheffler in eight, and Tommy Fleetwood in nine.

Of those five events McIlroy played between his win at Augusta and his tied-40th place at The Open, two were majors. And the earliest McIlroy will return to the golf course will be on August 12, although judging by his comments on the FedEx Cup format, it is not an absolute guarantee he will start at the St Jude Classic on that date.

A back-to-back Masters champion and with six majors to his name - not to mention countless tournament wins worldwide and a personal fortune estimated to be around the £300million mark - McIlroy has earned the right to pick and choose when and where to play. But his performance at The Open made you wonder if his schedule could take a little away from his competitive edge.

Article continues below

McIlroy is so good that, even with a reduced schedule, he will be a prime contender for the lucrative end-of-season honours. He will be in the mix for the FedEx Cup and the Race to Dubai, that is for sure.

And when the next major comes around next April, you would not back against him making it three Masters wins on the spin.But it is clear golf is going to see less of its greatest player in the coming years, rather than more.

Sports.title: FIFA launch investigation into Argentina after 'disgusting' World Cup final scenes
Sports.content:
FIFA launch investigation into Argentina after 'disgusting' World Cup final scenes

FIFA are launching an investigation into the behaviour of the Argentina players after they were beaten 1-0 by Spain in the World Cup final on Sunday

View 2 Images FIFA is set to investigate the conduct of Argentina players after the World Cup final (Image: Getty)

FIFA is set to investigate Argentina's behaviour after the final whistle at the World Cup final. Lionel Scaloni's side sparked widespread outrage for the way they handled the 1-0 defeat to Spain at the MetLife Stadium, as players were seen getting violent and even allegedly punching some of their opponents.

‌



Leandro Paredes was shown a red card following the full-time whistle after placing his hand around Spain defender Eric Garcia's throat before kicking him to the floor. The Argentina midfielder then got into a heated confrontation with Gavi, appearing to have a swipe at his head before pushing him to the ground.

‌



Also involved in a post-match scuffle was Argentina defender Nahuel Molina, who appeared to take a swipe at Rodri as the Spain captain ran to celebrate his side's win. Molina seemed to punch Rodri's stomach which caused a furious reaction from the Manchester City star, who came rushing over to confront him.

‌



Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match READ MORE :

As well as that, a furious Nicolas Otamendi, the 38-year-old Argentina defender, then himself had a word with Rodri to speak about his and Aymeric Laporte's pre-match comments around the referee.

It came before Argentina coach Roberto Ayala, who had a glittering playing career, appeared to throw a punch at Spain attacker Dani Olmo with Garcia then forced to step in and split them apart.

But now, in response to Argentina's behaviour, FIFA have launched an investigation, according to Sky Sports.

‌



View 2 Images Leandro Paredes was sent off for an angry clash with Eric Garcia (Image: Getty Images)

It's safe to say Argentina's behaviour wasn't well received in England, with former Newcastle United forward Alan Shearer lambasting La Seleccion as "terrible" when co-commentating for the BBC.

"Paredes threw two or three haymakers into someone's face. He went for them," Shearer said. "There is no place or space for that. We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina. The reaction after the final whistle is terrible."

‌



Ex-Manchester United right-back Gary Neville, meanwhile, was clear with his verdict on ITV.

"It's a disgrace," Neville said. “I love the competitiveness of the Argentines, fighting and scrapping for their lives, Messi has propped them up, but it’s been a disgrace the last few games."

Joe Hart, the former Manchester City goalkeeper, gave a blunt assessment of Argentina's behaviour while working for the BBC. "There was one man on the pitch who did have class and that was Lionel Messi, who shook hands with every one of those Spanish players," he said. "The game's done. They could have absolutely no complaints about what happened today. Disgusting behaviour."

Article continues below

Ferran Torres was the eventual match-winner for Spain in the 106th minute after Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card and sent Argentina down to 10 men. In truth, Luis de la Fuente's men were deserved winners in the end, having had 20 shots, 12 shots on target and four big chances across normal and extra-time.

Sports.title: Commonwealth Games 2026 athletes start arriving in Glasgow from around the world
Sports.content:
Commonwealth Games 2026 athletes start arriving in Glasgow from around the world

The relaunched Commonwealth Mile will be a highlight with new world record holder Josh Kerr a clear favourite and the flying Scot joked that he could shave even more time off his brand new record

View 5 Images Athletes were greeted at Glasgow by the Games' mascot (Image: Andrew Milligan/PA Wire)

Athletes from around the world have been flying in to Glasgow for this year's Commonwealth Games.

‌



Adam Ramsay-Peaty, Georgia Hunter Bell, Katarina Johnson-Thompson, Josh Kerr, Eilish McColgan, Duncan Scott, and Jamaica's Shericka Jackson are lining up at Glasgow's Commonwealth Games.

‌



‌



The relaunched 'Commonwealth Mile,' first seen in the 1950s with athletes like Sir Roger Bannister, will be a highlight with new world record holder Kerr a clear favourite.

The flying Scot joked that he could shave even more time off his brand new record adding: "You may have to give me a couple of days because my body is feeling a little rough right now."

‌



He struggled to sleep after setting the new record 'due to the adrenaline and caffeine' in his system. "It is like a big hangover this morning," he added. "But I have to get back into it with the Commonwealth Games coming up."

Mile record-smashing Scot Kerr praised by track legend Steve Cram READ MORE :

Guide to the 2026 Commonwealth Games is on sale now READ MORE :

View 5 Images Josh Kerr is leading contender for gold in the one mile race at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

‌



Around 3,000 athletes from 74 countries are competing across ten sports for 215 gold medals, including 47 in Para sport (integrated events), with 500,000 tickets available. The first athletes from Canada, Australia and The Cook Islands arrived yesterday in time for Thursday's opening ceremony. The new format Games are seen as a blueprint for a future Olympic bid by the North of England. They were due to be held in Victoria, Australia.

But organisers unexpectedly withdrew after costs hit £3.13 bn, far more than the £1.4 bn they had expected to spend. Glasgow is delivering the scaled-back event for £114m, with the majority of funding coming from the £100m compensation paid by the Australians.

View 5 Images Welsh cycling star Emma Finucane is competing in the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

‌



Five years of event planning were completed in just one year. No public money is being used. King Charles and Queen Camilla are set to attend the opening ceremony. They will join athletes, officials, volunteers and spectators from across the Commonwealth to officially kick-off 11 days of sporting action at the OVO Hydro in Glasgow.

Sir Chris Hoy, one of Scotland's most decorated athletes, will also take part in the opening ceremony, which 5 will broadcast live. He said: "It is an absolute honour to attend the opening of Glasgow 2026 with the King and Queen.

"A home Games is always a special occasion and I have so many wonderful memories from competing in the Commonwealth Games myself.

‌



View 5 Images Adam Ramsay-Peaty is one of the biggest stars at the Commonwealth Games (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

"I have no doubt the city of Glasgow will yet again be a superb host to what promises to be an exciting event and I very much look forward to being a part of it."

Australia topped the Birmingham 2022 medal table with 179 medals, including 67 golds. Team England was just three behind on 176. Team Scotland won 51 medals with 13 golds. The other powerhouses are Canada, India and New Zealand.

‌



The Scots challenge will be led by Kerr, who set a stunning 3:42.66 world one-mile record. Jake Wightman, Neil Gourley and Jemma Reekie, also run in the mile.

Defending champions Eilish McColgan and Laura Muir as well as Paralympic gold medallists Ben Sandilands and Owen Miller further strengthen the host nation’s hopes of success. England’s Georgia Hunter-Bell (800m) and Zharnel Hughes (200m) are set to star, while Jamaican sprinter Shericka Jackson is in the Relay mix.

The Men’s 4x100m will feature Canada’s Olympic gold medal-winning quartet, headlined by their most decorated male Olympian of all-time Andre De Grasse.

‌



View 5 Images Athletes from the Cook Islands have arrived in Glasgow for the Commonwealth Games (Image: Andrew Milligan/PA Wire)

The Men’s 100m features London Diamond League winner Kanyinsola Ajayi who set a new national record of 9.84s. Among his rivals will be Kenya’s defending champion Ferdinand Omanyala. Welsh cycling legend Emma Finucane, the world, European and Olympic champion, competes after becoming the first British woman to win three medals at a single Olympic Games since 1964 when she triumphed in Paris.

She will be joined by compatriot, the swimmer Matt Richards. He said: "It is a battle of the Brits in the pool, but you have got to chuck the Aussies in there as well. It’s a pretty stacked field."

Article continues below

England’s Emily Campbell, the most successful British female weightlifter of all-time, defends her Birmingham 2022 title.

* Tickets are available at glasgow2026.com/tickets.

Sports.title: Richarlison risks wrath of teammates with reaction to Argentina losing World Cup final
Sports.content:
Richarlison risks wrath of teammates with reaction to Argentina losing World Cup final

Spain were not the only ones left celebrating on Sunday evening after their World Cup final success over Argentina with Tottenham striker Richarlison making sure he joined in with gusto

View 2 Images Richarlison slid across his lounge floor (Image: https://x.com/footballontnt)

Tottenham star Richarlison could be in for an awkward reunion with a couple of his teammates after wildly celebrating Argentina’s World Cup final heartbreak. The South American nation were aiming to become back-to-back world champions as they took on Spain in New Jersey on Sunday.

‌



But Lionel Scaloni’s men were second best throughout the game, with Ferran Torres’ goal in extra time eventually securing the title for Spain. Luis de la Fuente’s men of course celebrated their success on the pitch.

‌



But Brazil and Spurs striker Richarlison couldn’t resist getting involved from his living room after Torres' goal. His partner Amanda Araujo shared a video of the forward sliding across his lounge floor on his stomach, before he then jumped up and leapt into the air.

‌



Of course, there is a bitter footballing rivalry between Brazil and Argentina so it’s no surprise to see Richarlison toast Spain’s success. But he might now be in for an awkward chat with a few teammates.

Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match READ MORE :

The striker plays alongside Argentina defender Cristian Romero in North London, while the pair have also been joined by Marcos Senesi, who signed on a free transfer from Premier League rivals Bournemouth.

Richarlison of course also has history with Spain midfielder Rodri, who was named player of the tournament. He previously hit out at the decision to hand the Manchester City man the Ballon d’Or in 2024 instead of Brazil teammate Vinicius Jr.

‌



He wrote: “All of us who live football eagerly await the individual awards each season. Today, all Brazilians who love football woke up expecting to see another player from our country win an award for the best in the world after so long.

“Unfortunately, for reasons that no one can understand, the award did not come. And don’t get me wrong, Rodri is a great player who deserves to be among the best.

View 2 Images Richarlison was left jumping in the air after Ferran Torres' goal (Image: https://x.com/footballontnt)

‌



“But Vini not winning the Ballon d’Or was embarrassing, and the only one who lost today was football. I remember Vini saying that his dream was to see the whole of Brazil cheering for him. And that day was today!

“You are a giant and the best in the world, kid! And no trophy will change that. Keep going and never shut up! We’re together.”

Richarlison scored 12 goals in 43 appearances for Spurs last season but the 54-time capped Brazilian international was not named in his nation’s squad for the World Cup by Carlo Ancelotti. The Selecao only managed to reach the last 16, having been beaten by an Erling Haaland inspired Norway.

Sports.title: Ascot makes King George the richest race in Britain by lifting 2027 value to £2.5 million
Sports.content:
Ascot makes King George the richest race in Britain by lifting 2027 value to £2.5 million

After a successful set of financial results the track has boosted the signature middle distance prize to a value double what it was in 2024 in the week of its latest edition

View 3 Images Calandagan goes past Kalpana in the King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Image: Getty Images)

Ascot has made the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Stakes the richest race in Britain from next year.

‌



The latest edition of the track’s signature middle distance prize will be worth £2 million when it is run at the royal racecourse on Saturday. But from next year the prize-money will rise again, hitting £2.5 million, making the all-aged race more valuable than the Epsom Derby. It will mean the prize fund has doubled since 2024.

‌



With the first £2m edition of the race having attracted two runners from Japan to take on last year’s world’s best horse, Calandagan from France, plus the winner of the Irish Derby, Ascot believes the extra investment in purses has paid off.

‌



David Easterby wears lucky Sondad silks on latest leg of 326-mile charity bike ride READ MORE :

Director of Racing Nick Smith said: “In a week where the significant prize money boost to this year’s King George has resulted in two of the best horses in Japan and France being set to run as well as Irish Derby winner Benvenuto Cellini, and eight Group One winners in total, we are delighted to confirm further significant momentum for Britain’s premier all-aged race with £2.5 million on offer next year.

“In a fiercely competitive international market, it is crucial that Britain’s flagship midsummer races are appealing to connections of the world’s best horses. The Elite Races Scheme, backed by the Levy Board and BHA in 2026, has played an important part in this venture as we continue to work with our racecourse colleagues at the Jockey Club, Goodwood and York to promote the midsummer highlights of British racing, namely the July Cup, the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth Stakes, the Sussex Stakes and the International Stakes.

View 3 Images Calandagan: named best racehorse in the world in 2025 (Image: PA)

‌



“Our whole programme is important to us, of course, as demonstrated by 52% of our races this year being run for more than 2025, and a full prize money announcement for 2027 will be made in December.”

Saturday’s race has drawn a star-studded cast of ten five day acceptors headed by Calandagan and Japan’s Masquerade Ball, who finished first and second in the Japan Cup.

Calandagan’s stablemate Goliath, winner of the King George two years ago, is also included plus last year’s runner-up Kalpana. Aidan O’Brien’s quarter features Irish Derby winner Benvenuto Cellini, 2025 Derby winner Lambourn and Minnie Hauk, the triple Oaks winner who was runner-up in the Arc. Coronation Cup winner Bay City Roller needs rain to participate.

‌



View 3 Images Goliath: 2024 King George winner entered in 2026 edition (Image: PA)

Kalpana’s trainer Andrew Balding said: “She worked well on Saturday, I was very happy with her. She’s a very good horse on her day and loves Ascot – she’s not put in a bad turn there yet, so hopefully that will continue. I’m sure she’ll be there or thereabouts again.

“Calandagan is obviously a very good horse and we couldn’t match him last year, but we’ll take him on again and who knows.

Article continues below

“I think she’s a little bit fitter than she was last year and we were always sort of struggling to get weight off her last year. This year she has come to hand and stayed in a good place. It just seems to have occurred that way, but we are very happy with her.”

He added: “It’s one of the most important middle-distance races of the summer and has always been a main target for her.”

Sports.title: Argentina president makes surprising announcement immediately after ugly World Cup final
Sports.content:
Argentina president makes surprising announcement immediately after ugly World Cup final

Argentina came up short against Spain and reacted poorly at full-time as players threw punches, but the nation's president, Javier Milei, has made a surprise announcement

View 2 Images Javier Milei has announced a public holiday following Argentina's World Cup defeat (Image: Tomas Cuesta/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Argentina's president, Javier Milei, has announced that the nation will have a public holiday when Lionel Messi and co return from the World Cup. La Albiceleste fell short in their final against Spain and saw ugly scenes at the full-time whistle when members of their team threw punches at the victors.

‌



Ferran Torres' goal separated the teams in extra time but Argentina struggled to lay a glove on Spain and did not manage a shot on target. Instead, their efforts will be remembered for a number of fouls, Enzo Fernandez's red card and the unsavoury scenes upon the final whistle.

‌



Milei, nevertheless, wants to celebrate his country's achievement, having reached a second final in succession after Argentina won the tournament in 2022.

‌



"Thank you so much, players!!! "All the way to the end, with our boots on. Argentina, always on top," he said.

"WORLD CELEBRATION," Milei posted. "Given the concerns about the celebrations for the achievement of the Argentine National Team, I inform the public that, depending on what the players and coaching staff decide regarding the day to celebrate, it will be declared a national holiday."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Milei accepted it will be a difficult time for Argentina's squad but wanted to highlight the magnitude of what they had achieved. "The lessons this group has learned are enormous," the president said on Radio Mitre.

"This must be a very difficult time for the players and coaching staff, but when the initial excitement dies down, they'll realise the magnitude of what they've accomplished.

Not all of Argentina's squad are set to return to Buenos Aires, however. Many plan to head straight on holiday from the United States, or to return to their clubs immediately.

‌



View 2 Images Paredes was sent off after the game for an angry clash with Eric Garcia (Image: Getty Images)

The AFA announced in a statement: "After the final, some players from the squad will depart directly from the United States to different destinations to rejoin their clubs or begin their rest period. Meanwhile, part of the delegation, made up of players, coaching staff, and other personnel, will return to Argentina tomorrow, with an expected arrival around 5 PM."

Following the match, Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni struggled to hold back tears. His contract is set to expire at the end of the year.

‌



"I will talk to the president," he said. "I have an idea of what I would like to do. I will see out my contract and I feel the need, I don't know if something as big can be done. We need to speak this through.

"I am thankful to the president for bringing me this chance of being in this place where I am at the moment. It was a dream place for everyone. We have tried up until the very last minute to give our utmost, the staff and players. I believe it's only fair that I can take this time for myself to think this through."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
