Sports.title: Barry Hearn Sees Different Anthony Joshua Before Prenga Fight
Sports.content:
“AJ is in an amazing place at the moment. Obviously, I’ve seen him since 2012. We’ve got very close. He’s like a member of our family. “I don’t think I’ve seen him so motivated for the long term. Some of that’s been fueled by that tragic accident, but he’s now talking about the next three years in the ring. It was a year ago that we were talking about potentially two fights and then go off to a happy retirement. “He’s very motivated; he feels good about himself, but boxing is a funny sport. It takes one punch from a big lad to knock out anyone in the world. So, you’ve got to be on your toes all the time. You can’t take this for granted. And when you get your chance, you’ve got to take it. “AJ is in the mood to cause a lot of pain on Saturday. I don’t think I’ve seen him look better than this in the 14 years I’ve known him. He is in the right place, and I think on Saturday in Jeddah will be the right time,” Barry Hearn told Sky Sports.

Prenga wasn’t chosen to be a threat. He’s there to give Joshua rounds after the accident. Gym performances don’t mean much when the opponent isn’t expected to test you. Until Joshua gets back in with a heavyweight who can crack and force him to answer questions, nobody knows if the flaws from the Dubois fight remain. Barry Hearn’s comments are what you’d expect from a promoter backing one of his biggest stars.

Joshua was stopped by Daniel Dubois in 2024. AJ rebounded from that defeat last December, knocking out the YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul in a fight that was largely viewed as a celebrity-esque spectacle. Even in that victory, Joshua looked vulnerable before knocking out Paul.

AJ has always looked like a million bucks on the scale or hitting pads in the gym, but that means very little once someone real lands a clean shot on his chin.

He can look as motivated as Barry Hearn says, but gym work can’t replicate how a fighter reacts to getting hit, especially after coming back from a car accident. If Prenga manages to land something solid on Saturday, we’ll see right away if those old vulnerabilities are still there.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn: Boots Ennis Is ‘King Of The Castle’
Sports.content:
Hearn says his fighter is no longer in the position of making concessions to land the bout. Boots is now “king of the castle.”

“He was taking the smaller side of the piece last time. He was going to be the B-side. He agreed to everything that they wanted to get that opportunity. So you imagine how he feels now that he’s king of the castle,” said Hearn to the media about Ennis’ position in negotiations with Vergil Ortiz Jr. “Vergil doesn’t have anything Boots wants other than a big fight and a big payday. What does Boots want to do now? He wants to unify.” “I don’t rule out that Ortiz fight at all. One thing is for sure. He ain’t close at all at the moment.“

Hearn’s comments reflect how much Ennis’ position has changed over the past year. During earlier discussions, Ennis was still chasing the biggest opportunities and was willing to accept B-side status to secure a fight with Ortiz. Hearn says those circumstances no longer exist.

Ennis now holds two world titles and has shifted his attention toward becoming the undisputed champion. Hearn indicated that unification bouts remain the priority, but he left the door open for Ortiz if Golden Boy presents an offer that outweighs Ennis’ other options.

“Tell us what the money is. And I’ll go to Jaron, and I’ll say, ‘We got Kelly, Fundora, or Ortiz,'” said Hearn.

Unless Turki Alalshikh gets involved, it’s questionable if a fight with Ortiz Jr. is financially appealing enough for Ennis to take time off from pursuing his goal of becoming the undisputed champion at junior middleweight.

Josh Kelly and Sebastian Fundora remain among the names under consideration, with Hearn making it clear that every possibility will be evaluated before Ennis decides on his next opponent.

A fight is still available for Vergil Jr, but Hearn believes the balance of power has moved. Rather than Ennis pursuing Ortiz Jr. at any cost, Golden Boy must now convince the unified champion that the financial package is worth delaying his pursuit of the remaining 154-lb titles.

Sports.title: Vernon Forrest Silences Shane Mosley Again
Sports.content:
The rematch carried enormous significance. Forrest defended both the WBC and Ring Magazine welterweight championships after taking them from Mosley in their first meeting earlier in the year in January 2002. Many believed Mosley would make the necessary adjustments and reclaim the titles, while Forrest had the opportunity to prove the upset had not been a one-night performance.

The event attracted 15,775 fans, the largest crowd to attend a boxing card in Indiana history at the time. HBO televised the championship bout nationally, and both fighters earned career-high paydays. Forrest received $3.42 million, while Mosley collected $2.8 million. Veteran referee Laurence Cole officiated the 12-round title fight.

Mosley came out aggressively, looking to erase the disappointment of the first bout by forcing exchanges from the opening bell. Forrest refused to be drawn into a firefight. Standing three inches taller with the longer reach, he established his jab early, circled effectively and answered Mosley’s rushes with sharp counters before tying him up whenever the action moved inside.

As the rounds progressed, Forrest steadily took control. Forrest repeatedly stabbed Mosley with the jab before tying him up whenever the challenger got close, forcing Mosley to reset his offense over and over. Referee Laurence Cole was forced to separate the fighters throughout the contest as the tactical battle became increasingly physical.

The middle rounds lacked sustained action, drawing boos from portions of the crowd, but Forrest remained committed to the game plan. One report even noted that a fight in the stands during the sixth round briefly attracted as much attention as the action inside the ring.

Mosley increased the pressure during the championship rounds, finally producing several spirited exchanges in the tenth. Forrest answered with crisp counterpunching and finished strongly, landing several hard right hands late in the eleventh before boxing confidently through the final round. There were no knockdowns, but Forrest consistently landed the cleaner, more effective punches.

CompuBox statistics reflected the tactical nature of the contest. Forrest landed 120 of 446 punches, while Mosley connected on 114 of 259, with Forrest’s jab, timing and ring control outweighing Mosley’s higher connect percentage.

Judges Gary Merritt (117-111), Tony Castellano (116-112) and Jerry Roth (115-113) all favored Forrest. HBO unofficial scorer Harold Lederman and several media scorecards also had Forrest winning, confirming that his first victory had been no accident.

The rematch closed the book on one of the era’s most compelling rivalries. Forrest had defeated Mosley twice as a professional after also beating him during the 1992 U.S. Olympic Trials, establishing a rare mastery over one of boxing’s greatest fighters.

Mosley later captured world titles in higher weight classes, while Forrest continued his championship run before unifying the welterweight division. More than two decades later, the rematch remains one of the signature victories of Forrest’s Hall of Fame career, removing any doubt that his success against Mosley was built on superior technique rather than surprise.

Sports.title: Shakur: Zuffa Promised Haney And Tank Davis Fights
Sports.content:
Even under the best circumstances, it’s not a given that Zuffa will be able to hook a big fish like Gervonta Davis to fight Shakur. Despite Shakur’s elite skills and massive new Zuffa backing, he simply doesn’t move the needle the same way with the casual audience.

If Shakur demands anything close to parity or tries to dictate the terms, Tank will likely dig his heels in. Tank has shown before that he would rather sit out, pursue a lesser name, or even talk about walking away from the sport entirely than give up his leverage to an opponent he feels needs him more than he needs them.

“What really went into the decision was mainly life-changing money. Not only life-changing money, just life-changing opportunities,” Shakur said to Fighthype. “Dana [White] and Nick [Khan], they kept saying, ‘We want to get you in with the best fighters. We wanted you to fight the best.’ The guys that they mentioned was Devin and Tank. And when I heard that, I’m like, why would I go away from what I’ve been wanting to do my whole career? I think my whole career I’ve been saying the titles and all that, I done it. With all due respect to the titles, I appreciate y’all… but I want to fight the best. I want to get in there and prove myself and get under them bright lights and see who’s the best. I’m not scared of taking no risk.”

Haney hasn’t said whether he’s going to fight Shakur next or defend against his WBO mandatory, Keyshawn Davis. If Keyshawn actually upsets Haney to take the WBO welterweight title, Shakur’s biggest potential fight is effectively dead.

“I think that’s what really kind of kicked it off with me and Zuffa. Their vision is as big as mine. I ain’t never really hear promoters with big visions like me. It’s an amazing thing, and I’m happy to be the person to lead the new school and new generation,” Shakur said.

With Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn officially locked in for September 12, a Ryan loss changes everything for the 147-pound division. Ryan is arguably the sport’s biggest ticket seller and pay-per-view draw outside of Canelo. Shakur vs. Ryan is a massive financial fallback if Tank or Haney fall through. If Benn beats Ryan, that golden parachute disappears.

While a Benn victory makes Conor a massive star under the Zuffa banner, a Shakur vs. Benn fight doesn’t carry the same casual fan appeal or domestic PPV weight as a clash with Garcia. Benn doesn’t have the same popularity in the U.S as he does in the UK. American fans view Benn as the son of a famous retired ex-world champion, who has never beaten any elite-level fighters during his career.

Sports.title: Mike McCallum Stunned Donald Curry In Classic Title Fight
Sports.content:
The scheduled 15-round championship bout was televised by HBO from the Caesars Palace Sports Pavilion in Paradise, Nevada. Richard Steele served as referee, while Guy Jutras, Jerry Roth and Ove Ovesen handled the scoring. An official attendance figure was never widely reported, but the event drew major attention as one of the biggest championship fights of 1987.

McCallum was making the sixth defense of the WBA junior middleweight title he had won in 1984. Nicknamed “The Body Snatcher,” the Jamaican-born master tactician had knocked out every opponent during his title reign. Even with those accomplishments, sportsbooks installed him as a 2-1 underdog.

Curry entered as the WBA’s top contender after previously holding the WBA, WBC, IBF and Ring Magazine welterweight championships. Moving to 154 pounds offered a fresh opportunity to reestablish himself among boxing’s elite and position himself for even bigger fights.

The fight also carried significant financial rewards. McCallum earned a reported $475,000, while Curry received $425,000, excellent purses for championship fighters during that era.

For four rounds, the betting odds appeared justified. Curry’s jab repeatedly beat McCallum to the target. His hand speed, combinations and movement kept the champion from settling into his rhythm, and a sharp right hand in the second round buckled McCallum’s knees. By the end of the fourth, Curry had built a comfortable lead on all three scorecards. McCallum remained dangerous, but he looked a step behind as Curry controlled the action.

At 1:14 into Round 5, Curry stepped inside and drove a right hand toward McCallum’s body. McCallum anticipated the attack, gave a subtle body feint of his own, then unleashed a crushing left hook that landed flush on Curry’s jaw. The fight ended instantly.

Curry crashed flat onto his back, staring toward the lights as Steele began the count. He slowly regained awareness around seven but never gathered himself in time to continue. The referee completed the count, and McCallum had retained his championship with one of boxing’s most unforgettable single punches.

The knockout earned KO Magazine’s Knockout of the Year honors and remains one of the finest one-punch finishes ever shown on HBO. Ironically, Sugar Ray Leonard worked the broadcast that night after Curry had reportedly objected to his presence on the telecast, which brought an extra bit of drama to an already memorable evening.

McCallum later vacated the WBA title to pursue championships at middleweight and light heavyweight, eventually becoming a three-division world champion and earning induction into the International Boxing Hall of Fame. Although he never landed the marquee fights against Sugar Ray Leonard, Marvin Hagler, Thomas Hearns or Roberto Durán, his body of work cemented his reputation as one of boxing’s most accomplished champions.

The defeat for Curry proved far more damaging than anyone expected. He won a handful of fights afterward but never returned to the level that once made him one of the sport’s pound-for-pound stars, suffering later defeats to Michael Nunn and Terry Norris before retiring.

More than three decades later, McCallum’s left hook remains one of the greatest one-punch knockouts in championship boxing history and the defining moment of an unforgettable title fight.

Sports.title: Is Eddie Hearn Protecting Diego Pacheco?
Sports.content:
If Aleem was able to land that frequently, what happens against Osleys Iglesias, Lester Martinez or even middleweights Carlos Adames or Yoenli Hernandez if they moved up? Those fighters carry more power, are physically stronger, and wouldn’t be as forgiving once Pacheco found himself exchanging at close range.

The Kevin Lele Sadjo fight exposed flaws in Pacheco when the action became physical. He didn’t look comfortable under sustained pressure, and those issues weren’t answered against Aleem because the matchup never forced him into the same type of fight.

Pacheco’s post-fight comments focused on Canelo Alvarez and Jaime Munguia. Eddie Hearn has also floated Munguia as a possible next opponent. If Matchroom wants to prove Pacheco belongs with the division’s elite, fights against Iglesias, Lester, Adames or Hernandez would answer far more questions than a quick jump toward a lucrative name.

Hearn has the financial backing to make those fights. If Matchroom bypasses them and heads straight toward Munguia, it will be difficult to ignore the possibility that the priority is maximizing Pacheco’s value before a dangerous contender exposes the flaws that are still visible in his game.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Calls MSG Fight “Storybook” As Questions Follow Zuffa Debut
Sports.content:
Saturday’s main event is a 10-round showcase against Steven Butler, a fringe contender with five defeats who has come up short in his biggest opportunities. Berlanga also enters the fight after losing two of his last three bouts, including a knockout defeat to Hamzah Sheeraz, followed by a year away from the ring.

That leaves little margin for error in his first appearance under the Zuffa banner. An impressive win would give Dana and Zuffa a platform to match Berlanga against recognizable names at 168 or 160 pounds. A poor performance, or an upset loss, would make that job far more difficult.

Ticket demand has also become part of the conversation. The BoxingTickets account on X claimed Zuffa removed roughly half of the remaining inventory for the event before increasing prices on the seats still available, describing the move as “gimmicking the ticket sales.”

Zuffa has not commented publicly on the ticket changes. With the promotion investing heavily in Berlanga as one of its first headline attractions, Saturday’s fight carries importance well beyond the result inside the ring.

Sports.title: Mystery Title For Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn
Sports.content:
The promotion has repeatedly discussed its long-term goal of operating with one champion per weight class. If that plan begins in September, Garcia-Benn would be a logical stage for introducing a Zuffa world welterweight title.

Instead of advertising the fight as the WBC World Welterweight Championship, Zuffa chose far more general language.

Several outcomes remain possible. Ryan may simply enter the ring carrying the WBC belt as champion, with Zuffa avoiding sanctioning-body branding in its own promotional material. Another scenario is that the company reveals its own championship belt during fight week or on the night of the event, making the winner the first Zuffa welterweight champion.

A third possibility is that both titles are recognized, with Garcia entering as WBC champion while the victor also receives a Zuffa championship belt.

None of those outcomes has been confirmed. The poster itself offers no explanation beyond the phrase “World Welterweight Championship.”

For a promotion launching what it has billed as a new era in boxing, the lack of specificity is difficult to ignore. Identifying the fight as a WBC title bout would have been easy. Choosing broader language instead has shifted attention toward what Zuffa plans to place in the ring when Ryan and Benn are introduced.

Zuffa may answer that question during fight week or wait until the championship presentation on September 12. Until then, the identity of the title being contested remains one of the biggest unanswered questions surrounding the event.

Ghana News.title: Wontumi conviction ‘sad’ – Palgrave Boakye-Danquah questions political implications
Ghana News.content:
Former Government Spokesperson on Governance and Security, Dr Palgrave Boakye-Danquah, has expressed disappointment over the court's decision to convict and sentence New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, over the Samreboi illegal mining case.

His comments come after the Accra High Court sentenced the Ashanti Regional Chairman to 20 years' imprisonment over illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay, who presided over the Criminal Division of the High Court, delivered the sentence on Monday, July 20.

The court also imposed a fine of 10,000 penalty units, equivalent to GH¢120,000, with a default sentence of three years' imprisonment if the fine is not paid.

Dr Boakye-Danquah, speaking on Asempa FM's Ekosiisen show, said the outcome was unexpected because, in his view, the evidence presented by the defence team did not establish that Chairman Wontumi was personally involved in illegal mining activities.

"We did not expect this outcome because, based on the evidence we provided, it was clear that there was nothing presented in court that showed Chairman Wontumi was personally involved in illegal mining throughout the proceedings," he said.

According to Dr Boakye-Danquah, the defence had been optimistic that an application filed at the Supreme Court would influence the court's consideration of the matter before judgment was delivered.

"We were therefore very hopeful that, considering the application that was filed at the Supreme Court, Her Ladyship would take her time to consider the matter. Unfortunately, she did not agree with our position and went ahead to deliver her judgment," he stated.

The former government spokesperson described the verdict as disappointing and suggested that the case could be viewed within the context of political victimisation.

"It is very sad. It feels like a form of political victimisation of a politically exposed individual," he said.

Dr Boakye-Danquah stressed that Chairman Wontumi was not an ordinary individual but a prominent political figure whose position carries significant importance within the NPP.

"We are not talking about just any other person; we are talking about the sitting Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party, the stronghold of the party and the largest opposition party," he added.

While expressing disappointment with the judgment, Dr Boakye-Danquah questioned whether similar legal action would be taken against other individuals alleged to have links to illegal mining activities.

"If this is the direction we are taking, while we know that there are others who are actively involved in galamsey, then we will wait and see how things unfold," he said.

He called for fairness and consistency in the fight against illegal mining, adding that the country must ensure that accountability applies equally to all individuals regardless of their political affiliation or status.

"We can only hope and pray that our country can come together and find its way forward," he said.

READ ALSO: Chairman Wontumi sentenced to 20 years in prison

Dr Boakye-Danquah also defended Chairman Wontumi's conduct throughout the legal proceedings, describing him as cooperative and respectful of the judicial process.

He said the NPP chairman had consistently appeared before the court and complied with all requirements during the trial.

"Chairman Wontumi has been law-abiding throughout this case. There was not a single day that he failed to appear in court. We have been very cooperative with the court and followed due process," he said.

He revealed that he had recently met with Chairman Wontumi before the former was taken into custody following the court's decision.

"I have just parted ways with him, and he is being taken to Nsawam. How did we get to this stage in this country?" he questioned.

The party's leadership, including its flagbearer and legal team, has indicated that it is reviewing the judgment before announcing its next course of action.

Ghana News.title: AMA unveils 2 new compactor trucks to boost waste collection
Ghana News.content:
The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has unveiled two new refuse compactor trucks to boost waste collection, reduce the accumulation of refuse and improve sanitation services across the capital.

The six-wheel-drive, rear-loading trucks were acquired at a total cost of about GH¢2.4 million and commissioned by the Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Ahmed Ibrahim, at a ceremony held at the AMA headquarters in Accra.

Each truck has a carrying capacity of about 20 cubic metres, a compaction ratio of between 3:1 and 4:1, and a payload capacity of between 9,500 and 10,000 kilogrammes. They are fitted with manual, electric and wireless remote-control operating systems to improve efficiency in waste collection.

Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, Mr Ibrahim commended the Mayor, Assembly Members, directors and staff of the AMA for improving service delivery despite inheriting significant financial and legal challenges.

He said the Assembly had previously struggled with garnished accounts, judgement debts, unpaid legal fees and several court cases, but had gradually stabilised its finances and strengthened its ability to undertake development projects.

While describing the acquisition as a step in the right direction, the Minister said two trucks alone would not be enough to meet the sanitation demands of the capital.

He urged the Assembly to work towards acquiring at least five or six refuse compactors to improve waste collection across the metropolis.

Mr Ibrahim said that effective waste management requires strong collaboration between central government, metropolitan assemblies and private waste-management companies, noting that neither the public nor the private sector could tackle the challenge alone.

He also called on neighbouring municipal assemblies to invest in their own sanitation equipment instead of depending heavily on the AMA to collect waste generated within their jurisdictions.

According to him, Accra's position as the country's commercial hub means the Assembly manages refuse generated not only by residents but also by traders, commuters and visitors from across Greater Accra and other parts of the country.

The Minister assured the Assembly that the Ministry would continue exploring ways to support the AMA because of the unique sanitation burden it bears as the authority responsible for the capital's central business district.

He also appealed to residents to help keep the city clean by reporting indiscriminate dumping of refuse into drains, on roads and at unauthorised locations through the Assembly's hotline, 0544 914 628, to enable prompt enforcement action.

The Mayor of Accra, Michael Kpakpo Allotey, expressed appreciation to President John Dramani Mahama for making funds available to support the Assembly's sanitation and development programmes.

He disclosed that the AMA did not own a single refuse compactor when he assumed office and had relied largely on rented equipment and services from private waste-management companies.

According to the Mayor, the continuous rental of sanitation equipment was expensive and unsustainable, making it necessary for the Assembly to begin building its own fleet.

Mr Allotey also said that sanitation management should not be limited by administrative boundaries, saying all metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies share responsibility for keeping the capital clean.

He acknowledged public concerns over the poor maintenance of government-owned equipment and disclosed that the Assembly is taking steps to establish its own mechanical workshop to maintain its growing fleet of sanitation vehicles and equipment.

Ghana News.title: Long way to go in prosecuting those behind environmental destruction – Erastus Asare Donkor
Ghana News.content:
Investigative journalist Erastus Asare Donkor says Ghana still has a long way to go in holding accountable individuals and companies responsible for severe environmental destruction, despite the conviction of New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi.

Speaking on JoyNews' The Pulse on Monday, July 20, Mr Asare Donkor said the conviction should not be viewed as the end of the fight against illegal mining, but rather a step towards ensuring that more people who have contributed to the destruction of Ghana's natural resources face justice.

According to him, the issue is not about celebrating the imprisonment of an individual but ensuring that the rule of law prevails.

"It is not about being happy for the incarceration or the taking away of somebody's freedom, but it is about the rule of law taking its course," he said.

Mr Asare Donkor said his investigative reports on illegal mining activities in the Samreboi area and the destruction of the Tano River have highlighted the environmental damage caused by mining operations linked to Akonta Mining Limited.

He explained that since late 2021, he and his team have produced several reports, including the documentary Destruction for Gold, which captured evidence of illegal mining activities and their impact on the Tano Forest Reserve and the Tano River.

He recalled that during investigations, some Chinese nationals mining along the Tano River referred them to Akonta Mining Limited when questioned about their licences, an indication of the company's alleged involvement in activities in the area.

Mr Asare Donkor said despite the reports and evidence gathered, authorities at the time failed to take decisive action to halt the destruction.

"We kept highlighting them. Did the government pay heed to us? No. Back then, we had no response from government on the way forward," he said.

He argued that relevant state agencies could have intervened earlier by stopping the mining activities, imposing sanctions or revoking licences where necessary.

The journalist, however, stressed that the case of Akonta Mining and Chairman Wontumi is only one example of a much broader environmental crisis.

He cited the destruction of the Pamprama Forest Reserve, where he said Heritage Imperial Limited carried out mining activities before obtaining a licence, leaving the state to spend taxpayers' money on reclamation efforts.

"We have a long way to go concerning the list of people who have done extreme harm or committed nature crimes to this country, who need to answer for this before we can clamp down on the impunity that is going on," he stated.

Mr Asare Donkor called for sustained investigations and prosecution of individuals and companies whose activities have contributed to the degradation of Ghana's forests and water bodies.

His comments follow the Accra High Court's conviction and sentencing of Chairman Wontumi to 20 years' imprisonment over illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region

Ghana News.title: Your Password Could Be The Weakest Link: 5 Mistakes That Put Your Accounts at Risk
Ghana News.content:
Kennedy Bentum Jnr is a cybersecurity professional and holds a Master of Science in Forensic Accounting from the University of New Haven. (United States of America).

He is CompTIA Security+ certified and writes about cybersecurity, cybercrime, fraud prevention, and digital safety.

Imagine waking up one morning only to discover that you can no longer access your email account. Within minutes, you realise your social media accounts have also been taken over. Friends begin calling to ask why you’re asking them for money through WhatsApp. Before the day ends, your online banking profile has been locked because of suspicious login attempts.

It sounds like the plot of a movie, but for many people, this is exactly how cybercrime begins, not with sophisticated hacking, but with a compromised password.

In an age where our lives are increasingly connected to the internet, passwords have become the digital keys to our identities. They protect our bank accounts, emails, cloud storage, social media profiles, and even government services. Yet despite their importance, many people continue to underestimate the role passwords play in keeping them safe online.

The uncomfortable truth is that cybercriminals don’t always need to break into a system. Sometimes, they simply log in using a password that was easy to guess, stolen through deception, or reused across multiple accounts.

Why Passwords Still Matter

With technologies such as facial recognition and fingerprint authentication becoming common on smartphones, it’s easy to assume that passwords are becoming less important. They are not.

Biometric features often unlock your device, but behind the scenes, passwords remain the primary method of securing most online accounts. Whether you are accessing your email, online banking, work systems, or shopping platforms, your password is still one of the first barriers protecting your information.

If that barrier is weak, everything behind it becomes vulnerable.

Five Password Mistakes That Put You at Risk

Using the Same Password Everywhere

One of the biggest mistakes people make is reusing the same password across multiple accounts.

Imagine using the same key for your house, office, car, and safe. If someone gets hold of that key, they gain access to everything. The same principle applies online. If one website suffers a data breach and your password is exposed, cybercriminals may try the same password on your email, social media, and banking accounts.

Choosing Predictable Passwords

Passwords such as 123456, password, qwerty, or even your date of birth may be easy to remember, but they are also among the first combinations attackers attempt.

Many people also use the names of their children, favourite football clubs, or phone numbers. While these choices feel personal, they are often easy to discover through social media or public information.

A stronger alternative is a long passphrase made up of unrelated words that is easy for you to remember but difficult for others to guess.

Ignoring Multi-Factor Authentication

Even strong passwords can be stolen through phishing attacks or data breaches.

This is why enabling multi-factor authentication (MFA) is one of the most effective security measures available today. MFA requires a second form of verification—such as a code sent to your phone or generated by an authenticator app—before access is granted.

Think of it as adding a second lock to your front door. Even if someone has your key, they still cannot get inside without the second layer of protection.

Sharing Your Password

Sharing passwords with friends, relatives, or colleagues may seem harmless, especially when done out of convenience. However, every additional person who knows your password increases the risk that it could be exposed intentionally or accidentally.

Passwords should remain private, regardless of how much you trust the other person.

Never Changing Compromised Passwords

If a company announces that it has experienced a data breach, many users assume it has nothing to do with them. In reality, if your account was affected, your password may already be circulating among cybercriminals.

Whenever you learn that one of your online accounts has been compromised, change your password immediately, especially if you have reused it elsewhere.

How Cybercriminals Steal Passwords

Contrary to popular belief, most attackers do not spend hours trying to guess passwords one character at a time.

Instead, they rely on techniques such as phishing emails, fake login pages, malicious software that records keystrokes, and databases of passwords leaked during previous breaches. They also use credential stuffing, an automated method of testing stolen usernames and passwords across multiple websites in the hope that people have reused the same credentials.

In many cases, the attacker succeeds because the victim unknowingly made the job easier.

Protecting Yourself Starts with Simple Habits

Improving your online security does not require advanced technical knowledge. A few simple habits can significantly reduce your risk.

Create a unique password for every important account. Use long passphrases instead of short words. Enable multi-factor authentication wherever it is available. Consider using a reputable password manager to generate and store complex passwords securely. Most importantly, think twice before clicking on unexpected links or entering your login details on unfamiliar websites.

Final Thoughts

Cybersecurity often seems like a complicated subject reserved for technology experts, but it begins with everyday decisions that every internet user can make.

Your password is more than just a way to log in. It is the first line of defence protecting your identity, your finances, and your personal information.

The next time you create a password, ask yourself one simple question: If someone tried to steal my digital life today, would this password stop them?

That answer could make all the difference.

Ghana News.title: Exchange rate has remained broadly stable despite global pressures – BoG Governor Asiama
Ghana News.content:
Dr. Johnson Asiama

The Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, has said the Ghana cedi has remained broadly stable against the major international trading currencies despite persistent global economic uncertainties and external market pressures.

Opening the 131st Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting on Monday, July 20, Dr Asiama said recent economic indicators pointed to continued resilience in the foreign exchange market, adding that the committee would carefully evaluate current developments before taking its next policy decision.

"The exchange rate has remained broadly stable, supported by improving macroeconomic fundamentals and recent policy measures," Dr Asiama stated.

He added that the committee's responsibility was to ensure that its policy stance remained appropriate in the face of evolving economic conditions.

"Our task this week is not simply to assess the latest data. It is to determine whether the framework we strengthened in May remains fit for the conditions now before us, and whether the choices we made then continue to serve the medium-term objectives on which our credibility depends," he said.

Ghana News.title: “Pretty Hurts”: The unregulated war on beauty in Ghana – a sister thinking out loud
Ghana News.content:
Introduction

In Accra, Ghana, a stroll through bustling neighbourhoods like East Legon, Osu Oxford Street, Madina, Ablekuma, Spintex or a journey up north to Tamale, Kumasi, or move to the Western city of Takoradi reveals a striking trend: gleaming storefronts and social media adverts promising “perfect curves,” “pink skin,” “shiny teeth,” and “Hollywood smiles’ Flat tummies” . Beauty clinics and spas are multiplying at an unprecedented rate, offering everything from buttock and breast enhancements to flat tummies and fashion braces. Yet beneath these glossy s and seemingly glamourous appearances lies a public health crisis that experts warn is fuelling a surging rate of cancer, kidney disease, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs) across the country (Amoako et al., 2021).

Who Is Watching?

Regulatory oversight remains alarmingly weak. The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) Ghana is mandated to regulate cosmetic products, while the Health Facilities Regulatory Agency (HeFRA) licenses health facilities. However, enforcement is inconsistent, and many so-called “beauty clinics” operate under the guise of salons, exploiting legal loopholes (FDA Ghana, 2020). This regulatory gap allows untrained individuals often self-proclaimed beauticians to administer intravenous infusions, inject skin-lightening agents, and perform invasive procedures without medical training or accountability.

These practitioners frequently source skin-bleaching creams and injectables from unverified international suppliers, including online marketplaces. Many of these products contain dangerous levels of mercury, hydroquinone, and corticosteroids substances banned or strictly regulated in other countries due to their toxic effects (Nkemngong et al., 2022). Mercury, for instance, is a known nephrotoxin linked to chronic kidney disease, while prolonged hydroquinone use increases the risk of ochronosis and skin malignancies (WHO, 2020).

The “Figure 8” Body: A Dangerous Ideal

The pursuit of the so-called “figure 8” body characterized by a narrow waist and exaggerated hips has become a global obsession. Women are resorting to extreme measures: starvation, unregulated slimming teas, herbal pills, and topical creams promising rapid fat reduction or localised weight gain for specific parts of the body. Many apply unknown oils and chemical mixtures to enhance buttock size, often without understanding the ingredients or potential health consequences.

Home-based vendors, operating with little to no regulation, produce all kinds of oral and topical beauty products like soaps, hips, butts and breast enhancement creams/oils from the comfort of their kitchens and backyards and then sell openly via social media platforms. These high demand products are sold in unlabelled containers with no ingredient list, production and expiry dates, FDA certification details; talk less of dosages or instructions for use. Others are importing weight loss or gain products and openly bragging of having the most affordable and potent products while comparing themselves to each other. The rise of “okada” (motorbike) delivery services has made access easier than ever. Influencers with idealized physiques promote these products, creating a cycle of demand driven by appearance rather than safety or science. Interestingly, many of these influencers never use the products and services they advertise.

This obsession ignores biological realities: body shape is influenced by genetics, hormonal balance, metabolism, and nutrition not by miracle creams or dangerous concoctions (Addo et al., 2020). Yet, the pressure to conform to an increasingly narrow beauty standard continues to grow.

Fashion Braces: When Aesthetics Override Health

One of the most concerning trends is the rise of “fashion braces” cosmetic dental appliances marketed solely for aesthetic enhancement, not orthodontic correction. These cheap, unregulated devices are often imported from dubious online sources and installed in beauty salons and spas by unlicensed personnel.

I recently witnessed a disturbing scene: a woman reclining on a salon bench typically used for eyelash extensions receiving braces installation from a beautician who, I later learned, was national service personnel with no dental training and operates a beauty salon as a side hustle. Two other young ladies waited their turn. This normalization of medical procedures in non-clinical settings is a public health red flag.

Certified orthodontists warn that improperly fitted braces can cause irreversible damage, including tooth root resorption, periodontal disease, enamel erosion, and even tooth loss (Opoku et al., 2023). Yet, the desire for a “perfect smile” for TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram reels overrides caution. The aestheticization of health interventions turns critical medical care into a fashion accessory with potentially lifelong consequences.

Skincare as Social Currency

Skincare routines have evolved into a social status symbol. Women are bombarded with messages that not having a multi-step regimen equates to being “laid back” or irresponsible. Influencers promote complex routines involving toners, serums, exfoliants, and bleaching agents often without disclosing ingredients or risks.

More troubling is the practice of mixing multiple products sometimes from different brands and chemical compositions into custom “toning” or “brightening” blends. I once observed a vendor in a cosmetic shop advertising a “bridal glow package” promising “caramel, mulatto, and half-cast” skin tones days before weddings. These mixtures, created without regard for chemical interactions, are sold with glowing testimonials audio and video “proof” of transformation yet their long-term effects remain unknown.

Even more alarming is the bleaching of infants and toddlers. Some parents apply skin-lightening creams on newborns, believing lighter skin offers social and economic advantages (Boakye, 2022). This practice reflects deep-seated colorism rooted in colonial legacies and perpetuated by media and advertising.

Meanwhile, natural, safe, and effective alternatives like raw shea butter, cocoa butter, cold-pressed coconut oil, and olive oil ingredients foundational to many commercial products are being abandoned in favor of branded, chemically-laden alternatives. Ghanaian-owned brands like *Skin Gourmet*, which prioritize natural formulations, offer a healthier, culturally rooted alternative, a brand I have personally used for years.

Why Are Women Risking Their Lives?

Is this merely low self-esteem? The answer is more complex. Body shaming is rampant in Ghanaian society. From family gatherings where relatives comment on a woman’s flat chest or dark skin, to university campuses where skin tone dictates social inclusion, the psychological pressure is relentless. Social media amplifies this, with anonymous users dissecting women’s bodies in comment sections.

Influencers many of whom use filters, editing tools, or even undergo undisclosed procedures promote unattainable beauty standards. The advertising industry profits from this insecurity, turning women’s bodies into projects to be “fixed.” As one young woman confided, “If I don’t enhance my body, no man will want me.” This belief, though deeply personal, is structurally reinforced by cultural norms, media narratives, and economic incentives.

The Cost of “Pretty”

The human cost of this beauty war is staggering:

Skin lightening (“toning”) is linked to chronic kidney disease, mercury poisoning, and skin cancers (Nkemngong et al., 2022).

Unregulated butt injections, often using industrial silicone or unsterile fillers, have caused pulmonary embolisms, infections, and deaths (Amoako et al., 2021).

Herbal “detox” drips administered by untrained hands can lead to septic shock, air embolisms, and IV site infections.

Fashion braces and DIY teeth whitening are destroying healthy dentition.

Despite these risks, clinics continue to multiply, and customers keep coming driven by a culture that equates beauty with worth.

A Way Forward

1. Strengthen Regulation

The FDA and HeFRA must be empowered with clearer mandates, increased staffing, and greater enforcement capacity. A publicly accessible registry of licensed beauty and cosmetic practitioners should be established to enable consumer verification. Customs agencies must intensify screening of imported cosmetic products, particularly those shipped via informal channels.

2. Public Education Campaigns

The Ministry of Health, Ghana Health Service, and National Commission for Civic Education should launch nationwide campaigns on the dangers of unregulated cosmetic procedures, skin bleaching, and DIY treatments. These should include school curricula, community outreach, and media partnerships.

3. Hold Influencers Accountable

Social media influencers who promote cosmetic products must disclose whether they use them and whether they are certified by health authorities. Platforms like Instagram and TikTok could be pressured to remove content promoting dangerous practices.

4. Cultural Shift

Change must also be cultural. Family and friends must stop body-shaming. Men must learn to celebrate women as they are. Women must reclaim agency over their bodies not as projects to be perfected, but as sites of strength, identity, and pride.

My Body, My Pride

Pride is not the rejection of self-improvement. It is the rejection of shame as a marketing tool. It is the courage to ask, *“What’s in this cream?” or “Are you licensed to inject me?”. It is understanding that real beauty does not require dialysis, reconstructive surgery, or a visit to the oncology ward.

Pretty hurts. But it doesn’t have to kill you. Your health is not a trend.

References

Addo, P. C., Osei, K., & Boateng, A. (2020). Body image perception and its determinants among young women in urban Ghana. *Ghana Medical Journal, 54*(3), 167–174. https://doi.org/10.4314/gmj.v54i3.5

Amoako, A. A., Asamoah, B. O., & Frimpong, J. B. (2021). The rising trend of cosmetic surgery and its implications for public health in Ghana. *BMC Public Health, 21*(1), 1–9. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-021-10945-4

Boakye, Y. (2022). *Colourism and skin bleaching in Ghana: Historical roots and contemporary realities*. African Studies Quarterly, 21(2), 45–60.

Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) Ghana. (2020). *Guidelines for the regulation of cosmetic products in Ghana*. FDA Ghana.

Nkemngong, M. A., Umoh, A. S., & Ajoke, C. A. (2022). Mercury and hydroquinone levels in skin-lightening creams marketed in Ghana and Nigeria: Public health implications. *Journal of Environmental and Public Health, 2022*, 1–8. https://doi.org/10.1155/2022/9786543

Opoku, M. P., Nyako, E. A., & Ofori-Asenso, R. (2023). Orthodontic tourism and the rise of “fashion braces” in urban Ghana: A call for regulation. *BMC Oral Health, 23*(1), 1–7. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12903-023-03058-5

World Health Organization (WHO). (2020). *Mercury in skin lightening products: A global review of legislation and enforcement*. WHO Press. https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240014748

Note: All names and specific locations used in personal observations are based on the author’s lived experience and are not intended to identify individuals or businesses for legal action.

Ghana News.title: BoG opens 131st MPC meeting amid global economic uncertainties, energy price pressures
Ghana News.content:
The Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, has opened the 131st Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting with a call for careful, evidence-based policy decisions as Ghana navigates global economic uncertainty and rising energy prices.

Addressing the opening session on Monday, July 20, Dr Asiama said the Committee would assess recent inflation trends, the impact of the Bank's May monetary policy reforms, domestic liquidity conditions and external risks facing the economy.

He noted that although Ghana's economy has continued to demonstrate resilience, policymakers must remain vigilant in responding to evolving global and domestic developments.

"Our task this week is not simply to assess the latest data. It is to determine whether the framework we strengthened in May remains fit for the conditions now before us, and whether the choices we made then continue to serve the medium-term objectives on which our credibility depends," the Governor stated.

Dr Asiama also launched the inaugural Monetary Policy Committee Educational Observership Programme (MPC-EOP), welcoming students from the University of Ghana to observe aspects of the MPC process.

He said the initiative reflects the Bank's commitment to transparency, public engagement and developing the next generation of economists and policymakers.

Ghana News.title: Police arrest 5 suspected robbers in Accra, retrieve firearms and ammunition
Ghana News.content:
The Accra Regional Police Command has arrested five people suspected of being members of a criminal group involved in armed robbery and landguard activities following an intelligence-led operation at Sapeiman Faase in the Greater Accra Region.

The operation, carried out jointly by the Accra Regional Police Command and the National Police Intelligence Directorate (NPID), led to the recovery of firearms, ammunition and other offensive items believed to have been used to terrorise residents in the area.

According to a statement issued by the Head of Public Affairs of the Accra Regional Police Command, Chief Superintendent Juliana Obeng, the suspects were arrested on July 17, 2026.

The suspects have been identified as Torgbui Agah Semaglo, 50; Shadrach Agah Semaglo, 22; William Kweku Sedanu, 21; Cyril Kassenu, 26; and Kingsford Agah Semaglo, 18.

Police said a search of the suspects' premises resulted in the recovery of several items, including a pump-action shotgun, a Stoeger ST-R9 pistol, a dummy Austria pistol, a jackknife, a face mask, 12 BB cartridges, three rounds of 9mm ammunition, one round of AK-47 ammunition, a talisman and two kitchen knives.

The statement said all the retrieved items have been retained as exhibits for investigations.

Preliminary investigations, according to the Police, indicate that the suspects are believed to be members of a criminal syndicate engaged in armed robbery and landguard activities.

"Preliminary investigations indicate that the suspects are believed to be members of a criminal group involved in armed robbery and landguard activities and are alleged to have used the recovered weapons to terrorise residents within the Sapeiman area and its environs," the statement said.

The Police said the suspects remain in custody and are assisting with investigations while efforts continue to determine whether they are linked to other robbery cases and criminal activities.

"The suspects are currently in Police custody assisting with investigations, while efforts are underway to establish their involvement in other criminal activities and to apprehend any additional accomplices," the statement added.

The Accra Regional Police Command commended members of the public for providing credible information that supports police operations and appealed for continued cooperation in the fight against crime.

"The Accra Regional Police Command commends members of the public who continue to support the Police with credible information and urges residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious persons or activities to the nearest Police Station or through the Police emergency numbers," the statement said.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Ebola death toll in DRC surges to at least 930 as outbreak gathers pace
World.content:
Ebola is spreading faster than any previous outbreak in DRC, with 37 new deaths recorded over just 24 hours at the weekend.

The death toll from the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen to at least 930 and the virus appears to be spreading faster.

The health ministry said on Monday that the number of confirmed cases had reached at least 2,344. That is total confirmed total as of Saturday with 37 deaths recorded in just 24 hours from Friday – one of the highest daily increases recorded since the Ebola outbreak was first declared in the DRC on May 15.

The World Health Organization (WHO) warned last week that Ebola is spreading in the DRC faster than in any previous outbreak.

WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told reporters that the Ebola outbreak in the DRC in 2018-2020 “took more than 10 months to reach 2,000 confirmed cases”. This time, it took only two months to reach 2,000 confirmed cases, and the ⁠⁠WHO said the ⁠⁠true tally could be at least double that.

“It is now the third-largest Ebola outbreak on record,” Tedros said. “In the past month, it has expanded faster than any previous outbreak.”

The DRC’s 17th Ebola outbreak was first detected after several deaths in Ituri, the mineral-rich northeastern province patrolled by several armed groups.

Cases of Ebola, which spreads through close contact and infected bodily fluids, have so far been found in five DRC provinces and in neighbouring Uganda. But while Uganda is now close to being “virus-free”, Tedros said, Ebola is spreading at an unprecedented rate in the DRC.

To compound problems in Ituri, where the death toll is growing fastest, healthcare workers began a strike last week and blocked the entrance to Bunia General Hospital. Staff complained of not receiving any compensation for their work since the outbreak began, despite treating patients in difficult and dangerous conditions.



Tedros highlighted that more than 80 percent of new cases were being detected “outside known contact lists, showing that transmission chains are still being missed”.

The health ministry said in its latest update that 724 patients are currently in isolation in hospitals and it is intensifying response efforts in affected areas.

“Patient care and support capacities are consolidating, with 22 new recoveries recorded in 24 hours,” the ministry said.

World.title: Andy Burnham pledges end to political instability as he becomes UK PM
World.content:
Britain’s seventh PM in a decade pledged major changes in bid to see off populist forces that are making large gains.

Andy Burnham has set out his vision for Britain as he took over as prime minister.

Burnham’s appointment was confirmed on Monday as he met King Charles III at Buckingham Palace. Becoming the United Kingdom’s seventh premier in a decade, he pledged to end the political instability that has plagued the country and promised to instigate major change.

Burnham replaces Keir Starmer, who was ousted just two years after winning a landslide election victory amid ongoing gains by populist forces.

“Britain needs to show the world that we can regain our stability once ‌‌again,” Burnham said after arriving at his official home, 10 Downing Street in London, to rapturous applause. “We have not been good enough and we need to be better,” he said.

The former mayor of Greater Manchester said he was “fed up” with the country’s ⁠⁠revolving door of leadership, which should invite “a moment for reflection and new resolution” for British politics.

Starmer was ousted by his peers about a month ago. On leaving office, he labelled his work as prime minister “the privilege of my life” and said that Burnham has his “full support”.

Burnham did not refer to Starmer in his speech, instead focusing on how he will implement change.

“We will make this moment a circuit-breaker for Britain, bringing forward the biggest changes in the last 40 years. A new political model and a new economic model,” Burnham declared.

Promising Britons “some breathing space now”, he promised to announce ⁠⁠measures this week to help tackle the cost of living.



The first instruction he will issue is “to end rough sleeping in our country”.

A 10-year plan for the country would come later in 2026, he added.

Regarding foreign policy, Burnham said Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will be one of the first foreign leaders he will speak with to assure him that British support will remain “resolute” under his premiership.

“I will be with him [Zelenskyy] 100 percent, as Keir Starmer has been, and Keir has done quite an incredible job in not just backing Ukraine but being there in a personal way,” Burnham said. “And I will be absolutely there for him in the same way.”

The new PM also indicated he would have an early call with United States President Donald Trump.

Burnham is likely to announce his senior cabinet appointments shortly, with focus on who will replace Rachel Reeves as finance minister.

The “King of the North”, as Burnham has been nicknamed due to his time leading Manchester and supporting working class issues, has been backed by the Labour Party as the party’s best chance of reining in Nigel Farage’s populist, anti-immigration party Reform UK.

Just two years after centre-left Labour won a landslide in elections, Reform leads in the polls, with the next national vote due in 2029.

World.title: What are ‘civilian’ sites in international law and where have US, Iran hit?
World.content:
The United States has escalated attacks on Iranian roads, bridges and power plants, and Iran too, has responded.

The United States and Iran are locked in an increasingly escalatory cycle of strikes that they each claim is aimed at preventing the other from securing military dominance over the Strait of Hormuz.

As the US pounds southern Iran and, in recent days, other parts of the country, Tehran too has hit back, striking US military bases in neighbouring nations in the Gulf and Jordan.

But projectiles fired by both the US and Iran have also hit civilian infrastructure, raising questions over potential violations of international law, even as the fragile memorandum of understanding (MoU) towards peace that the two countries had signed in June has collapsed.

“We’re going to knock out all their power plants. We’re going to knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate,” US President Donald Trump threatened in a Fox News interview last week. He made similar threats on civilian infrastructure earlier in April.

At least 50 people have died in Iran since the resumption of hostilities, and 500 have been wounded since July 15, according to Iranian authorities. Dozens of locations in southern and northwestern Iran have been hit in the past week, ranging from military command centres to railways and airports.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has hit back on neighbouring Gulf countries hosting US military assets, resulting in the deaths of at least two US military personnel.

International humanitarian law explicitly forbids the targeting of civilian infrastructure in armed conflict. The US and Israel hit several civilian sites in the first phase of the war that they launched against Iran on February 28, including a girls’ school in Minab where at least 170 people were killed.



A spokesperson for United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said on Friday that he was “particularly concerned about attacks on civilian infrastructure in Iran and across the region”, adding that “such attacks are unacceptable”.

So what counts as civilian infrastructure, and what places have been hit so far in the second wave of the US-Israel war on Iran? Here’s what we know:

What does the law say?

The 1949 Geneva Conventions and their Additional Protocols of 1977 forbid armed attacks or reprisals on civilian infrastructure or “objects” during a conflict.

Civilian infrastructure includes “all objects which are not military objectives”, the law says, and which are “normally dedicated to civilian purposes, such as a place of worship, a house, or other dwelling or a school”.

These also include any facilities that support the day-to-day lives of civilians and that are crucial to how a society functions: roads, bridges, railways, airports, electrical plants, sewage systems, hospitals, and phone and internet systems, for example.

The treaty states that drinking water installations and supplies, irrigation works, foodstuffs, crops, livestock as well as dams, dikes, and nuclear power generation plants also cannot be targeted.

When in doubt about whether an object is serving a military or civilian purpose, parties must assume it is civilian and thus cannot attack it, the law states.

Can civilian infrastructure be targeted?

Yes, under specific and carefully determined circumstances.

Civilian infrastructure becomes a legitimate target only when it can be proven that it was “used for military purposes at the time of the attack and that its destruction provides a definite military advantage”, according to the treaty.

Even so, the law mandates that such attacks ensure that necessary attacks on civilian infrastructure remain “proportionate to the military advantage”.

In short, attacks on suspected civilian objects are prohibited if the risks to civilians – deaths, injury, and the proper functioning of civilian life – outweigh military gains.
