World.title: Japan Tops Global Waste Index 2025; U.S., Israel, and Chile Rank as Worst Polluters
World.content:
Japan has emerged as the world leader in waste management, while Israel, Chile, and the United States rank among the worst-performing countries, according to the Global Waste Index 2025 released by Slovak-based waste technology company Sensoneo.

The report, which ranks all 38 OECD member states based on their waste generation and disposal practices, highlights significant disparities in global waste management. Sensoneoâs index evaluates countries on per capita waste generation, recycling, incineration, and landfill use.

Israel and Chile ranked last and second-to-last, respectively, primarily due to their heavy reliance on environmentally damaging landfilling practices. Israel sends 524 of the 650 kilograms of waste it generates per person each year directly to landfills. Chile recycles just 1% of its waste and sends more than 95% to landfill.

The United States, which increased its per capita waste generation from 811 to 951 kilograms since 2022, remains the highest generator of municipal solid waste globally. The U.S. disposes of nearly half of that â 447 kilograms â in landfills annually. Neighboring Canada also performed poorly, landfilling 67% of its annual 694 kg per capita waste.

At the other end of the spectrum, Japan ranked No. 1, followed by South Korea and Estonia, all of which combine relatively low waste generation with efficient disposal methods. Japan sends only 3 kilograms per capita to landfill, relying heavily on incineration (245 kg) and maintaining a controlled recycling rate.

European countries dominated the top 10 rankings, with Austria, Germany, Finland, Belgium, Sweden, Norway, and Switzerland all demonstrating strong waste management systems. Austria topped the recycling chart with 334 kilograms of municipal waste recycled per person annually â accounting for 42% of its total waste.

Meanwhile, Spain fell four places to 27th despite minor improvements. The country reduced its landfill and incineration rates slightly while increasing recycling by 10 kilograms per capita. However, its overall waste generation rose by 10 kg compared to the 2022 index.

The index revealed that in 12 of the 38 countries, over half of all waste is still landfilled â including in developed nations like Australia, New Zealand, and Canada. By contrast, Switzerland was the only country to report zero landfill disposal, while Belgium, Finland, Estonia, and Japan landfilled less than 3 kg per person.

Other key findings include:

New Zealand , Finland , and Iceland posted the largest reductions in waste generation per capita.

, , and posted the largest reductions in waste generation per capita. From an environmental standpoint, incineration is considered preferable to landfilling, but excessive reliance on either suggests a need for stronger waste reduction and recycling strategies.

About the Index and Sensoneo

First launched in 2019, the Global Waste Index is published every three years by Sensoneo, a company specializing in digital transformation for waste management systems. The 2025 edition is based on the latest available national data.

Sensoneo operates in 87 countries and provides waste monitoring solutions to cities, industries, and governments. It is the only company to have successfully implemented deposit return systems (DRS) IT infrastructure in nine countries, achieving recycling rates above 90%.

In Madrid, Sensoneo is deploying 11,100 smart sensors, marking the worldâs largest smart waste monitoring installation to date.

World.title: South Korean Model and Actor Kim Jong Suk Dies at 29, Family Urges Respect Amid Speculation
World.content:
South Korean model and television personality Kim Jong Suk has died at the age of 29, his family confirmed on June 6. The news has shocked fans and colleagues across the countryâs entertainment industry, where Kim rose to prominence following his appearance on tvNâs 2022 reality dating show Skip Dating.

Kim, who began his career in modeling before transitioning to television, had been steadily gaining popularity in recent years. His sudden death has prompted an outpouring of grief and speculation online.

While the exact cause of death remains unconfirmed, some media reports have linked Kimâs passing to an incident in Hanam involving a violent altercation between a young man and his girlfriend. According to the reports, law enforcement responded to the scene, after which the man allegedly died by suicide after jumping from a high-rise building.

Amid widespread online discussion and conjecture, Kimâs family issued a public plea for restraint, asking the public and media to refrain from spreading misinformation or making disrespectful assumptions.

Kimâs older sister posted on social media, expressing the family’s devastation and emotional exhaustion. âWe ask for privacy and understanding during this difficult time,â she wrote, emphasizing the familyâs wish to grieve in peace.

Details regarding funeral arrangements have not been made public.

World.title: Spain crowned world champions with 1-0 extra-time win over Argentina in the final
World.content:
Spain crowned world champions with 1-0 extra-time win over Argentina in the final

20th Monday, July 2026 - 00:47 UTC Full article

Photo: EPA/EFE/RONALD WITTEK

Spain were crowned world champions for the second time in their history by beating Argentina 1-0 in extra time in the final played on Sunday at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. The winning goal came in the 106th minute, after a cross from Pedro Porro that Nico Williams headed on and that, according to the match report, Ferran Torres finished to settle a game clearly dominated by the Spanish side.

The run of play reflected Spain's superiority, with 68% possession and twenty shots, eleven of them on target, against Argentina's three attempts, none on goal. The defending champions, who had reached the final hoping to repeat their Qatar 2022 triumph, barely troubled goalkeeper Unai Simón and sat back for much of the match.

The game had two decisive incidents. In the second half, the referee disallowed a Spanish goal for a foul flagged earlier in the move, with the score at 0-0. Near the end of regulation time, Argentina's Enzo Fernández was sent off for a second bookable offense after a hard challenge on Spanish defender Pau Cubarsí, leaving Argentina with ten players for extra time. The South American side finished the match with five bookings and one dismissal.

With this result, Spain claim their second World Cup, sixteen years after the one won in South Africa in 2010, when they beat the Netherlands, also in extra time, through a goal by Andrés Iniesta. The title adds to Euro 2024 and cements the generation led by coach Luis de la Fuente, who called for the achievement to be “valued.” Midfielder Rodri was named the tournament's best player.

“Destiny was written. Every final is difficult, we had Messi in front of us, but we have always relied on ourselves, playing our game,” Ferran Torres said after the match. For Argentina, the defeat dashed their bid to become the first national team to win two consecutive World Cups since Brazil, champions in 1958 and 1962.

The final closed a World Cup hosted by the United States, Mexico, and Canada, whose decisive stages were played on US soil. The tournament was marked, in its closing stretch, by the controversy surrounding Argentina, after its players displayed a banner about the Falklands following the semifinal against England, an episode FIFA is assessing for a possible breach of rules barring political messages. Argentina played the final while awaiting that decision.

World.title: Trump takes center stage at the World Cup final, presenting Spain's trophy and holding it beforehand
World.content:
Trump takes center stage at the World Cup final, presenting Spain's trophy and holding it beforehand

19th Sunday, July 2026 - 23:05 UTC Full article

The episode fits into the close relationship between Trump and Infantino, which has run through much of the tournament

US President Donald Trump was one of the central figures off the pitch at the 2026 World Cup final, co-hosting alongside FIFA President Gianni Infantino the trophy presentation to Spain, champions after beating Argentina 1-0 in extra time at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Trump, who watched the match from the VIP box with his wife, Melania, also held the original trophy before kickoff, in images that circulated widely on social media.

Trump's role in the ceremony marked a change from the tournament's two previous editions. At Russia 2018 and Qatar 2022, Infantino presented the trophy alone. FIFA had announced before the final that the two would do so jointly. The handover by the host country's head of state is, however, a practice with historical precedent at the World Cup: Queen Elizabeth II presented the trophy to England captain Bobby Moore in 1966, and King Juan Carlos I did so with Italy's Dino Zoff in 1982.

Trump entregando la Copa del Mundial de Futbol del 2026 a la selección española. pic.twitter.com/u0IoU3LK6a — Orlando Avendaño (@OrlvndoA) July 19, 2026

Before the match, the trophy was brought up to the presidential box, where Trump took it and patted it before returning it to the area set aside for the ceremony. The scene drew attention for taking place outside the official on-field act, in which the cup is usually kept under guard until its presentation to the champions. While players from both teams walked past the trophy without touching it, following a football tradition, the president approached it.

The episode fits into the close relationship between Trump and Infantino, which has run through much of the tournament. During an earlier White House visit, Infantino had already let Trump hold the cup and told him the trophy is “for winners.” FIFA also opened an office in Trump Tower in New York, and at the 2025 Club World Cup final, played at the same stadium, Trump remained at the center of champions Chelsea's photograph.

The final closed a World Cup hosted by the United States, Mexico, and Canada, whose decisive stages were played on US soil and in which Trump's role was a recurring feature, from the build-up to the closing ceremony. The tournament also introduced other US-inspired novelties, such as a halftime show and the award of championship rings to the winning team. Spain won their second world title, sixteen years after the one achieved in South Africa in 2010.

World.title: ICE kills a Colombian and a Mexican in operations where they weren't the target, officials say
World.content:
ICE kills a Colombian and a Mexican in operations where they weren't the target, officials say

19th Sunday, July 2026 - 23:00 UTC Full article

Mexican national Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52, who had lived in Houston for three decades, had died on July 7, at a traffic stop in that city

Two Latin American migrants were shot dead by agents of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) within a week, in operations in which, as federal authorities and lawmakers acknowledged, neither was the intended target. The deaths revived protests and calls for accountability over President Donald Trump's immigration policy.

Colombian national Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, 26, died on July 13 in Biddeford, Maine, when an agent fired at the vehicle he was driving. Mexican national Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52, who had lived in Houston for three decades, had died six days earlier, on July 7, at a traffic stop in that city. Migrant-rights groups said Durán Guerrero was authorized to work in the country; the embassies of Colombia and Mexico are providing consular assistance to the families.

The circumstances of the Maine death are the subject of conflicting accounts. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said the driver tried to flee and that, “fearing for public safety,” the agent fired. Senator Angus King, after speaking with DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, gave shifting accounts of whether the man was the target of the operation, and noted that the agents were not wearing body cameras. In Houston, the Harris County District Attorney's Office opened its own investigation and issued nearly twenty subpoenas, saying the federal government was not sharing evidence.

Following the two shootings, Mullin suspended most ICE traffic stops, at the request of Republican Senator Susan Collins, who said the Biddeford case raised “critical questions.” The pause, however, lasted hours: border czar Tom Homan played it down, and the measure was reversed by government decision.

The deaths come amid a sharp increase in immigration arrests. Democratic lawmakers and former officials linked the incidents to pressure to meet arrest quotas. “When there is that relentless pressure to do more, more and more, agents make mistakes,” Deborah Fleischaker, a former ICE deputy policy director, told CNN. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer criticized the administration for deploying thousands of agents “without making sure they were trained.”

DHS has repeatedly defended its agents' conduct. Mullin said in May that agents “sacrifice” themselves for the country's safety and that ICE had been “demonized.” Approval of Trump's immigration policy has fallen: about 60% of Americans disapprove of it, according to an Ipsos and Washington Post poll. Various media tallies, in the absence of official figures, put at several dozen the number of people who have died in ICE shootings or in custody since the start of Trump's second term.

World.title: Lula asks Trump to explain 25% tariffs on Brazil, speaks of a "war of truth"
World.content:
Lula asks Trump to explain 25% tariffs on Brazil, speaks of a “war of truth”

19th Sunday, July 2026 - 17:43 UTC Full article

“The war I want to wage with him is a war of narrative, a war of truth. I want to show the world who is telling the truth in this tariff war between Brazil and the United States,” Lula said

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva publicly called on his US counterpart, Donald Trump, to explain the reasons behind the 25% tariffs he imposed on most Brazilian products, a measure Brasília attributes to political rather than commercial motives. The levies, announced on July 15 by the Office of the US Trade Representative, will take effect on July 22.

“The war I want to wage with him is a war of narrative, a war of truth. I want to show the world who is telling the truth in this tariff war between Brazil and the United States,” Lula said on Friday during a visit in Rio de Janeiro. The president, who is seeking reelection in the October 4 vote, said his country was “a peaceful people” and that Washington would not manage to deceive Brazilian society.

The tariffs are applied under Section 301 of US trade law, following a yearlong investigation that concluded Brazil engaged in unfair trade practices. Washington cited the treatment of US technology companies, barriers to ethanol, intellectual-property protection, the PIX payment system, and illegal deforestation linked to agribusiness. The measure includes broad exemptions, among them coffee, beef, oranges, some energy products, and aerospace parts. A parallel investigation into forced labor, concluding next week, could add a further 12.5%.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio blamed Lula for the outcome of the negotiations and said he had not negotiated “in good faith,” arguing that the president had put his “ego” ahead of a deal. Lula rejected Washington's arguments: he said his government has reduced deforestation, that 76% of the US products Brazil imports pay no duties, and defended his country's right to regulate digital platforms and to keep PIX, which he described as “a heritage” of the Brazilian people.

The dispute moved to the center of the election campaign. Lula's main rival, right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, rejected the government's accusations that his family had promoted the levies in Washington and attributed the measure to Lula's own handling of the matter. He and his brother, former congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro, met with Trump at the White House in May.

The tariffs come on top of the 50% ones Trump had imposed in 2025, explicitly tied to the trial of former president Jair Bolsonaro — a Trump ally — sentenced to 27 years in prison for attempting to overturn his 2022 election defeat. Brazil's government estimates the new levies could affect 18% of its exports to the United States, some $7.4 billion, and is weighing reciprocity measures and support for affected sectors.

World.title: Andy Burnham is the Labour leader, third time lucky for the UK’s prime ministerinwaiting
World.content:
Andy Burnham is the Labour leader, third time lucky for the UK’s prime minister in waiting

19th Sunday, July 2026 - 01:35 UTC Full article

Andy Burnham sworn is as MP fom Makerfield

By Eric Shaw, Honorary Research Fellow in Politics, University of Stirling. Mr. Shaw is alzo a member of the Labour Party - A brief introduction, Andy Burnham officially becomes UK Prime Minister next Monday and can be expected to announce plans for new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea, as reported by BBC.

However the Labour Party's 2024 manifesto - which the new leader said he would follow - had pledged to not issue new licenses but to honor existing ones.

At the heart of the debate are two oil and gas fields in Scotland - Rosebank and Jackdaw - which regulators approved in 2022 and 2023 under the then Conservative government, but were overturned in 2025 after a legal challenge..

The announcement will form part of a flurry of measures from Burnham including plans to take water and energy companies under public control and a new council house-building program.

He is also expected to outline new measures that will give “people breathing space on the cost of living” and intends to make a “dynamic start... focused on delivering tangible change to people's lives as soon as possible”.

However on oil and gas, BBC reports that a source close to the incoming PM said no final decisions in the area had yet been made and would be unveiled at a later date instead.

Andy Burnham has won on his third attempt to be Labor’s leader. In a wide-ranging speech to Labour MPs at a special conference in London, a jubilant Burnham pledged to “bring back hope” and promised to be a leader for all nations of the UK. But it has taken him well over a decade to get here. In 2010, as a rising star associated with the Blairite wing, he made his first bid for the leadership.

In truth, back then he had little prospect of success: he was merely placing a marker. Five years later, he stood again but could do little to derail the Jeremy Corbyn bandwagon. Yet fast-forward 11 years and his ascent seemed unstoppable. Next Monday, he will become the UK’s 59th prime minister.

To understand why and how this happened, the circumstances that created this opportunity for Burnham are key. In 2024 Labour returned to power with a thumping majority, but with little more than a third of the total vote. Within months the new government was lurching from crisis to crisis; its standing in the polls collapsed and Keir Starmer became the most unpopular Prime Minister since modern records began.

At the same time, the party faced powerful challenges from opposite ends of the political spectrum – the radical-right Reform UK and the left-wing Greens. Labor’s electorate was visibly disintegrating, its plight made stark by the disastrous local and devolved parliamentary elections of May 2026 when it shed huge numbers of local councillorsand los Wales for the first time in over a century. The message for the parliamentary Labour Party (PLP) was stark: virtually all of them were at risk of losing their seats.

In these circumstances speculation around a challenge to Starmer mounted. But why should a man twice rejected by the party so rapidly emerge as the sole contender for the crown? The key (though not sole) factors are Labor’s system for electing its leader, the balance of internal party alignments, the structure of competition and the personal factor.

In terms of the election procedures, in 2010 Labor’s leader was selected by an electoral college divided into three sections: MPs, party members and trade union political levy-payers.

This was replaced in 2013 by direct membership voting, with three categories of members – ordinary members, affiliated (trade union) members and registered supporters. (This is discussed in detail in my book, Order and Rebellion: Labor’s Managerial Politics from Miliband to Starmer, co-authored with Emmanuelle Avril.) This was the system in 2015 when Corbyn swept the board across all three categories.

But by 2026 there had been two significant changes. First, the class of registered supporters had been abolished. Second, the nominations threshold for leadership contenders had been raised from 12.5% to 20% of the PLP. It is unlikely the former had much effect but the latter certainly did, by effectively blocking anyone from the hard left from entering. This benefited the soft left, where Burnham positions himself.

Soft-left membership

There are no really reliable estimates of the shifting balance of alignments within Labor’s membership. Gauging this is difficult because of massive turnovers in membership between 2010 and 2026. Most observers would agree that membership shifted after 2015 and then to the right after 2020.

Paradoxically, the center of gravity among the rank and file did not change dramatically. Close observers of the party agreed that the mean party members tended to be soft left. This is why Starmer contested the 2020 race on a soft left platform (soon abandoned). If Burnham had done likewise in 2015, he might have won.

The structure of competition in Burnham’s three contests differed considerably. In 2010 he was not a serious contender, with the race effectively between the Miliband brothers Ed and David Ed and David. In 2015 there were four contestants: Burnham, Corbyn from the hard left, and Liz Kendall and Yvette Cooper from the right.

As a member of the shadow cabinet under Ed Miliband, Burnham had shifted to the left and was initially seen as the frontrunner. However, he made a fatal miscalculation in assuming that in response to the 2015 election defeat the party would move to the right and so he did so himself.

In fact, the party swung left and Corbyn was able to sweep up the leftwing vote – including those broadly on the soft left.

Burnham learned his lesson. After quitting parliament and winning the newly created post of mayor of Greater Manchester, he increasingly adopted a soft left posture. In the race to succeed Starmer, there were only three other plausible candidates: Angela Rayner and Ed Miliband from the soft left, and Wes Streeting from the right.

Here, chance intervened on Burnham’s side. The popular Rayner was forced to resign as deputy prime minister and deputy leader over a tax issue. Otherwise, she would probably have been in pole position. Like Rayner, Miliband, who worked closely with Burnham, was unwilling to stand against him since both shared his soft left stance. This left Streeting. His problem was simple: even if he mustered the 81 nominations he required, as a right-winger he had no chance of beating Burnham in a leadership contest. Streeting new this, so opted not to stand.

Finally, among Burnham’s personal qualities, two are worth noting. The first is his undoubted popularity among those who know him best – his Greater Manchester constituents. More broadly, he normally receives a better net rating than any other Labor politician.

The second is his willingness to take a major risk by standing for a constituency, Makerfield, that he could easily have lost. Every one of its wards were won bt Reform in the local elections and its demographics rendered it a top target for the party.

But Burnham’s unexpectedly decisive victory in the by-election demonstrated his mass appeal. For hundreds of beleaguered Labour MPs fearful of losing their seats, he was seen as their one and only lifeline. Burnham had staked his career on Makerfield and won.

World.title: Argentina-England match drove a surge in online Falklands talk, consultancy Ad Hoc says
World.content:
Argentina-England match drove a surge in online Falklands talk, consultancy Ad Hoc says

18th Saturday, July 2026 - 00:38 UTC Full article

The day of the match saw some 660,000 mentions, nearly double the volume recorded on the most recent April 2 — the date on which Argentina commemorates those killed in the 1982 war

Argentina's victory over England in the World Cup semifinal was not confined to the sporting arena on social media. According to an analysis by the Argentine consultancy Ad Hoc, digital conversation about the Falklands surpassed two million mentions over five days around the match, in an episode that revived the sovereignty claim following the banner displayed by the Argentine players.

According to the measurement, the day of the match saw some 660,000 mentions, nearly double the volume recorded on the most recent April 2 — the date on which Argentina commemorates those killed in the 1982 war — when about 373,000 were logged. The consultancy identified several peaks in the conversation between July 10 and 16: the moment Argentina's opponent became known, statements by Security Minister Alejandra Monteoliva, the day of the match itself, and the subsequent remarks by President Javier Milei, which drew reaction in the United Kingdom.

The figure the consultancy highlighted was the marked predominance of the Spanish-language term. According to Ad Hoc, “the Argentine framing prevailed in the conversation,” as “Falklands” — the British name for the islands — accounted for just 9% of mentions over the past five days, against “Malvinas,” which reached a volume roughly ten times higher: around two million mentions versus 210,000.

El encuadre argentino predominó en la conversación, ya que el término “Falklands” (la denominación que los británicos le dan a las islas) representó apenas el 9% de las menciones registradas en los últimos 5 días, frente a “Malvinas” que alcanzó un volumen 10 veces superior. pic.twitter.com/HjrYejj915 — Ad Hoc (@AdHocOK) July 17, 2026

The analysis also measured the sentiment in the digital conversation toward Milei in relation to the islands and to the figure of Margaret Thatcher, on July 15 and 16. According to the consultancy, 66.7% of those mentions carried a negative charge, against 19.9% positive and 13.4% neutral, a result it attributed to the president's statements after the win and to the government's position on the issue. This is a measurement of social-media conversation, not a representative public-opinion poll.

The data offer a quantitative dimension of the episode that dominated the agenda between Argentina and the United Kingdom during the week. After the match, Argentine players posed with a banner reading “Las Malvinas son argentinas” (“The Falklands are Argentine”), which prompted a protest from the British government and FIFA's assessment of possible sanctions. Milei called the gesture “valid and lawful,” though he asked that football not be mixed with the diplomatic dispute.

The Falklands, a British overseas territory in the South Atlantic, remain the subject of a sovereignty dispute with Argentina. Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni had asked before the match not to confuse the two spheres: “It's a football match,” he said. The final will be played on Sunday against Spain.

World.title: “The Falklands cannot remain British for ever,” a Guardian column argues
World.content:
“The Falklands cannot remain British for ever,” a Guardian column argues

17th Friday, July 2026 - 23:08 UTC Full article

The columnist reviewed the negotiations that preceded the 1982 war

In an opinion column published in the British newspaper The Guardian, writer Simon Jenkins argued that the Falklands “cannot remain British for ever” and called for London to eventually reopen sovereignty negotiations with Argentina. The piece is the columnist's personal opinion and does not represent the newspaper's editorial position.

Jenkins took as his starting point two recent developments: the agreement reached this week between the United Kingdom and Spain to dismantle the Gibraltar border, and the “Las Malvinas son Argentinas” banner that Argentine players displayed after knocking England out of the World Cup semifinal. Drawing on that contrast, the author argued that none of Britain's imperial-era territories has an eternal right to remain as it is, and noted that defending the islands costs the British taxpayer more than £60 million a year.

The columnist reviewed the negotiations that preceded the 1982 war. In 1980, then-minister Nicholas Ridley presented islanders with a “leaseback” formula, under which the United Kingdom would cede sovereignty to Argentina and then lease the islands back for a lengthy period while retaining administration. The historical record confirms that the proposal was rejected by the islanders themselves, hostile to ceding sovereignty to a country then ruled by a military junta, and that the British government had pledged not to proceed without their consent. Jenkins argued that Argentina's invasion in April 1982, while talks were under way, collapsed that path and froze any discussion of the islands' future for more than four decades.

In one of the most contentious passages, the author held that Britain's staunch defense of the archipelago is partly explained by the fact that the islanders were, in his words, white and British, unlike other populations of territories London relinquished. This is the columnist's personal thesis, not an established fact, and it contrasts with the official British position, which grounds its sovereignty in the principle of the inhabitants' self-determination.

That position rests on the 2013 referendum, cited in the column itself, in which 99.8% of 1,517 voters chose to remain a British overseas territory. There has been no resumption of sovereignty negotiations since, and successive British governments maintain that the question cannot be discussed without the islanders' consent. Argentina, for its part, maintains its claim and has on various occasions asked to reopen talks.

Jenkins concluded that, sooner or later, a British government will find the courage to reopen negotiations, though he was skeptical that a banner unfurled at a US stadium could drive such a change. The Falklands, a British overseas territory in the South Atlantic, remain the subject of a sovereignty dispute with Argentina. The 74-day war of 1982, begun with the invasion by General Leopoldo Galtieri's military junta, left 649 Argentine servicemen, 255 British servicemen, and three islanders dead.

World.title: Venezuela raises official death toll from June double earthquake above 5,000
World.content:
Venezuela raises official death toll from June double earthquake above 5,000

17th Friday, July 2026 - 22:25 UTC Full article

The true scale of the disaster remains surrounded by uncertainty

The official death toll from the double earthquake that struck northern Venezuela on June 24 rose on Friday to 5,069, after 139 new fatalities were added, according to the president of Parliament, Jorge Rodríguez. The tally, released via Telegram, keeps the number of injured at 16,740 and of people left homeless at 17,907. Authorities present these figures as provisional, more than three weeks after the disaster.

The two quakes, of magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5, struck barely 39 seconds apart, with epicenters in the country's northwest. The larger one was the most powerful recorded in Venezuela in more than a century. La Guaira state, on the central coast, was the hardest hit, with numerous buildings collapsing; damage was also reported in Caracas and other parts of the north.

The true scale of the disaster remains surrounded by uncertainty. The US Geological Survey had estimated a high probability that the death toll would exceed 10,000, and international organizations and media have warned that the figure could be considerably higher than the official one, with tens of thousands of people still missing. Efforts to verify the disaster's magnitude have been hampered by information restrictions in the country, where numerous websites remain blocked; the UN urged authorities to fully restore access to media and social networks.

According to the official report, authorities have assisted 128,324 affected families, while 21,235 people remain in 107 temporary camps. Since June 24, some 1,331 aftershocks have been recorded; the most recent sizeable one, a week ago, caused panic and precautionary building evacuations in La Guaira.

The government launched a biometric census to determine the number of homes needed, which it estimates at around 25,000. On Tuesday, the National Assembly approved on first reading a reform of the Law against Real Estate Fraud to speed up reconstruction. The first vice-president of Parliament, Pedro Infante, said the amendment — pending a second debate — seeks to provide legal certainty and financing so the private sector can begin an accelerated home-building process.

The disaster strikes a country going through a prolonged institutional crisis. The government is led by acting President Delcy Rodríguez — sister of Jorge Rodríguez — following the capture in January of President Nicolás Maduro, currently held in New York awaiting trial on drug-trafficking charges. Rebuilding La Guaira and the affected areas is shaping up as one of the administration's main challenges in the months ahead.

World.title: Costa Rica Nature Hotel Earns Tripadvisor Travelers’ Choice Award
World.content:
A hotel and private nature reserve in Costa Rica’s northern lowlands has received a 2026 Tripadvisor Travelers’ Choice Award, placing it among the top 10% of listings on the global travel platform. El Lugar Costa Rica in Puerto Viejo de Sarapiquí in Heredia province, earned the recognition based on the quality and quantity of ratings and reviews posted by travelers during a 12-month evaluation period.

Unlike awards decided by a judging panel, Travelers’ Choice winners are chosen using feedback submitted by Tripadvisor users. Eligible businesses must have been listed on the platform for at least one year, receive a minimum number of reviews and maintain the required rating.

The award should not be confused with Tripadvisor’s Travelers’ Choice Best of the Best designation, which is reserved for the top 1% of listings. The regular Travelers’ Choice award recognizes places, restaurants and attractions that consistently receive strong reviews and places winners in the platform’s top 10%.

El Lugar combines a small luxury hotel with a private rainforest reserve covering about 486 hectares (1,200 acres). The property is within the North Atlantic Biological Corridor and alongside Braulio Carrillo National Park, one of Costa Rica’s largest protected areas. The hotel is approximately two hours northeast of Juan Santamaría International Airport, giving travelers access to the Sarapiquí region without requiring a domestic flight or a full day on the road.

Anyone staying there can explore private nature trails, take guided birdwatching trips, ride horses through forest and reforestation areas, swim in rivers and visit El Encanto, the property’s agroecological farm. Spa services and private casitas are also available. More than 130 bird species have been recorded on the property, according to the hotel. Recent sightings have included great green macaws, scarlet macaws and keel-billed toucans, while the reserve has also been registered as a birdwatching hotspot on eBird.

Hotel Manager Indalecio López said the award reflects both the work of the staff and the connection visitors develop with the property. “This award means so much to our team because it reflects what guests feel when they arrive here,” López said. He said the land was being protected long before the hotel opened and that conservation remains central to how the property operates.

El Lugar says its buildings were constructed using systems intended to reduce disruption to the surrounding terrain. These include raised foundations, gravity-based water distribution, thermodynamic water heating and natural septic systems designed to protect water movement through the property.

The hotel’s Tripadvisor listing ranked it first among hotels in Puerto Viejo de Sarapiquí when the award was announced. Its rating has remained between 4.8 and 4.9 out of five as new reviews have been added. The recognition also brings attention to Sarapiquí, a ara known for rainforest reserves, birdwatching, river activities and scientific research but often overlooked by visitors traveling between San José, the Caribbean coast and northern Costa Rica.

For independently operated nature lodges like this one, Tripadvisor reviews can carry a lot of weight. The Travelers’ Choice badge gives future guests a measure based largely on the experiences of previous visitors rather than advertising campaigns or evaluations commissioned by the tourism industry

World.title: A White-Knuckle Taxi Trip Through the Mountains of Costa Rica
World.content:
With my car doing what it does best– sitting idly in the carport awaiting a part– I walked twenty minutes in the dark down the long incline of the main street of the barrio to line up for the 5 am bus to Quepos. A red taxi pulled up. The driver stepped out and said, “Quepos! Dominical!” The going rate from Perez Zeledon to Quepos is 25 to 30 thousand colones. Not worth it as after 35 years here, I live happily on Tico time. Then he quoted his price. Mil to Dominical, mil quinientos to Quepos. Me and 2 other guys stepped forward. He loaded our gear in the trunk and off we went.

You pay your money and you take your chances. The first thing I noticed about my driver was that he liked to drive fast. The radio was tuned to a local station. Between latin dance songs,I heard an ad for a Tico restaurant in New Jersey. We crossed the Rio Pacuar bridge, recently expanded to two lanes, and began the ascent toward the 1,200 meter (3,900 feet) El Alto.

My back seat partner wore a head and neck cover and dark glasses. He reeked of garlic. I assumed he was a construction worker and not a terrorist. We passed a meat truck going up the mountain. The early morning hour meant fewer slow vehicles and we made good time. At the top of the mountain, a small pack of young men on motorcycles passed us in a swarm.

The downhill descent takes 16km (10 miles) to reach sea level. My driver wanted to cover this distance in record time. He tailgated slower traffic. Every curve felt like a carnival ride. I grabbed the overhead handle. It was broken, hanging by a screw. On a short straightaway, he breezed past a couple trucks and flew through the curve. I thought about Buddy Holly, Richie Valens and the Big Bopper, skipping the slow bus ride to catch a plane to their next destination.

We were also a trio who decided to skip the bus and save time. Death comes in threes. A long time ago, a guy I knew drove off the side of this same mountain in the fog. The smell of burning brakes lingered in the air. I was about to tell our driver that I wanted to arrive in Quepos, but not in a body bag. Then we hit the village of Platanillo, where I lived over thirty years before. We got behind a solid line of cars that descended the final mountain at a steady, unpassable pace.

We reached the costanera and were soon flying along at 120 kph. This is 75mph, the average speed on an interstate highway in the states. If I am in a car going this speed, I prefer to be in the driver’s seat. But my driver was a robust middle aged man and who knows how many tens of thousands of kilometers he had sped over the challenging roads of Costa Rica. I relaxed and went back to word games on my phone.

Twenty minutes outside Quepos our driver decided there was room for one more. An elderly woman at the bus stop climbed in. We were barely back to top speed when she began talking of her beliefs. In a loud slow voice the words streamed out. Yehova, Jesucristo, Gloria a Dios, gracias al señor. The car windows were down and a rush of wind through the car muffled a lot of what she said, which was fine with me. At one point the guy in the dark glasses said something about servidores de Satanas. I couldn’t hear enough to know if he was pro or anti Satan.

We got to Quepos and I paid the driver and found out he had an appointment in Quepos. He had covered the 80 kilometers in an hour fifteen. The money he collected went into his gas tank. A bargain is a bargain, and It’s not often you find a bargain while waiting for a bus at five in the morning.

Read more of Don Mateo’s writing from his newly published ebook.

World.title: Panama Bill Would Require Influencers to Disclose Paid Posts
World.content:
Panama’s National Assembly is considering a bill that would require social media influencers and content creators to clearly identify when their posts are paid advertising rather than independent recommendations. Deputy Walkiria Chandler D’Orcy, a member of the Vamos coalition, presented the proposal to the Assembly plenary on July 13, 2026. The measure aims to stop what she described as hidden advertising that takes advantage of the trust followers place in creators.

“What the user does not know is that many times behind that recommendation there is advertising, there is a contract, there is a payment, there is some product that has been given to that influencer or a commission for each sale… it seems to be an opinion, it is really advertising that was not identified as such,” Chandler said during the presentation.

She linked the bill to Panama’s existing consumer protection rules under Law 45 of 2007. That law already requires advertising to be presented clearly so consumers are not misled. Chandler argued that sponsored content on digital platforms often fails this standard and that stronger rules are needed, especially for younger audiences.

The proposal would require creators to make commercial content identifiable. Chandler stressed that the rules would cover promotions involving cash, contracts, free products, or commissions. She said the measure would not create new state registries or add budget costs. Chandler highlighted stronger protections for minors. She noted that many social media users are young and may have greater difficulty distinguishing genuine opinions from paid promotions.

The bill remains at an early stage. As of now, it has been presented to the full Assembly but has not advanced through committee debate or further votes. Details on specific labeling requirements, penalty amounts, the exact number of articles, or an implementation timeline have not been confirmed in official records or public statements beyond the presentation.

Influencer marketing has grown across Latin America as brands use creators to reach audiences on platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. Panama’s consumer authority has previously reminded businesses that online advertising must still comply with Law 45 rules on truthful claims and clear presentation. Chandler’s proposal seeks to apply those principles more directly to the influencer model.

If the Assembly moves the bill forward, it would join other regional efforts to address transparency in digital advertising. For now, the proposal stands as an attempt to give Panamanian consumers clearer signals about when content is commercial.

World.title: Costa Rica Bridge to Manuel Antonio Faces “Imminent Failure” Warning
World.content:
A bridge on the main car route toward one of Costa Rica’s most-visited places has been flagged as at risk of collapse, according to a special inspection carried out by the Laboratorio Nacional de Materiales y Modelos Estructurales (Lanamme) at the University of Costa Rica.

The structure spans the Boca Vieja estuary at kilometer 2.17 of Route 235, the secondary road that links central Quepos with the community of La Managua and the corridor leading to Manuel Antonio, home to the national park of the same name and a cornerstone of the central Pacific tourism economy.

Lanamme engineers assigned the bridge a rating of “imminent failure,” the most severe classification in the laboratory’s system, after finding severe corrosion running the full length of the superstructure’s main girders. The deterioration is most acute along roughly 12 meters (39 feet) at each end of the span, a pattern the report warns could lead to a collapse of the superstructure in the short term.

The bridge is not an aging relic. It opened in December 2016, built by the Ministerio de Obras Públicas y Transportes (MOPT) and the Consejo Nacional de Vialidad (Conavi) at a cost the ministry put at ₡1.56 billion (roughly US$3 million), and was promoted at the time as a modern two-lane concrete replacement that would improve access to a region the government itself described as having high tourism potential. Less than a decade later, the same authorities are being told the structure may not be safe to carry the traffic it was designed for.

Lanamme recommended an immediate detailed inspection and a load-capacity analysis to establish the maximum weight the bridge can safely bear, followed by inclusion of the structure in a short-term program of major rehabilitation or reconstruction. The report frames the corrosion as a known and worsening problem rather than a sudden discovery, pointing to a documented decline in the bridge’s condition over time.

As of yet, neither the MOPT nor Conavi had announced traffic restrictions, load limits, or emergency repairs in response to the warning. That leaves drivers, tour operators, and shuttle services heading to and from Manuel Antonio using a bridge that engineers have rated one step from failure, with no posted guidance on whether it should still carry heavy vehicles.

For an area whose economy depends heavily on visitor access, an unplanned closure of the Boca Vieja crossing — whether ordered by authorities or forced by further deterioration — would sever a primary route into the tourism zone with no obvious substitute.

World.title: Route 27 Goes One-Way at 2 p.m. and the Weather Turns with It
World.content:
If you spent the mid-year break at the beach, today is the day most people head home — and two things will shape your afternoon drive. Route 27 turns all its lanes toward San José for four hours, and the weather turns wet and windy from the middle of the day. Plan around both and you’ll skip the worst of it.

Between 2 p.m. and 6 p.m., every lane on Route 27 runs one way, toward the capital. The highway does this on the busiest return days to clear the flood of cars coming off the coast at once, so traffic keeps moving instead of stacking up at the tolls. Crews start closing and setting up the road at 1 p.m., and normal two-way traffic is back by 7 p.m.

The part to watch is speed and direction. While the lanes are flipped, the limit drops to 60 km/h (37 mph), and traffic officers will be checking — the lower speed is what keeps a road full of redirected lanes safe. And if you need to go the other way, toward Caldera or the coast, you can’t use Route 27 at all during those hours. Take an alternate instead: Route 3 through Atenas, Aguacate and Orotina; Route 1 over Cambronero; or Route 239 through Ciudad Colón, Puriscal, San Pablo, Turrubares and Orotina.

The weather gives you a reason to leave earlier rather than later. Rain and wind both build through the afternoon and into the night — exactly when the road will be busiest.

Mornings are the calmer window. Expect scattered showers over the Caribbean and the Northern Zone and some drizzle across the eastern and northern edges of the Central Valley, but nothing that should slow a drive. By afternoon, rain picks up over the Central and South Pacific — the coast most people are driving home from — and spreads to Limón and its lowlands by evening.

Wind is the part to respect. Gusts will reach 40 to 65 km/h (25 to 40 mph) in the lowlands and 70 to 95 km/h (43 to 59 mph) in the mountains, so the climb over the hills between the coast and the Central Valley will be blustery. Ease off on exposed stretches, leave more room behind the car ahead on wet pavement, and watch for standing water where the afternoon downpours pool.

In San José, look for 19 to 24 °C (66 to 76 °F) with wind from early morning. Out on the Nicoya Peninsula, Nicoya swings from about 22 to nearly 36 °C (72 to 96 °F). You can check conditions for your own route on our regional weather forecast before you set off.

The wet stretch doesn’t end today. Forecasters expect next week to open with another round of Caribbean rain as a new tropical wave moves through, so if your drive slips to Monday, the same advice holds.

In short: if you can, be on the road before the lanes flip at 2 p.m. and before the afternoon rain sets in. If you’re leaving later, hold to 60 km/h on Route 27, give yourself extra time, and take it slow through the wind and water on the way up.

World.title: International News: WestJet expands Belize service with new non-stop Winnipeg route
World.content:
International News: WestJet expands Belize service with new non-stop Winnipeg route

By Zoila Palma: WestJet has announced a major expansion of its winter 2026 schedule, including the launch of a new non-stop flight between Winnipeg, Manitoba, and Belize City, Belize, providing Canadian travelers with another direct gateway to the Jewel.

The weekly service will begin on December 14, 2026, further strengthening Belize’s air connectivity with Canada during the peak winter travel season.

The airline said the new route is part of its strategy to meet growing demand for warm-weather destinations across Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean.

The Winnipeg-Belize City service complements WestJet’s existing flights from Toronto and Calgary, giving Canadian visitors even greater access to Belize’s beaches, barrier reef, rainforests, and cultural attractions.

The new Belize route is one of five destinations being added to WestJet’s winter network, alongside new non-stop services between Calgary and Mérida, Mexico; Winnipeg and Punta Cana, Dominican Republic; Regina and San José del Cabo, Mexico; and Ottawa and Liberia, Costa Rica.

WestJet also reaffirmed its position as the leading Canadian carrier serving Belize this winter. The airline said it plans to increase capacity on several of its most popular routes, with additional announcements expected in the coming weeks.

World.title: International News: Canada to temporarily bar foreign travelers recently in Congo over Ebola concerns
World.content:
International News: Canada to temporarily bar foreign travelers recently in Congo over Ebola concerns

By Zoila Palma: The Canadian government announced Sunday that it will temporarily deny entry to foreign nationals who have been in the Democratic Republic of Congo within the previous 21 days as part of new border measures aimed at reducing the risk of Ebola entering the country.

The restrictions, which take effect on July 20 at 11:59 p.m. EDT, come despite the World Health Organization’s recommendation against imposing travel or trade restrictions on Congo, where officials continue to battle a major Ebola outbreak, Reuters report.

Canada’s Public Health Agency said the temporary measure is intended to protect public health, although it acknowledged that the risk of Ebola spreading to Canadians remains low.

The World Health Organization has repeatedly warned that travel restrictions can stigmatize affected communities and complicate efforts to control outbreaks.

The agency maintains that Ebola is spread primarily through direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person and estimates the risk of international transmission from Congo remains low. As of July 15, Congo had recorded more than 2,100 Ebola cases, including 828 deaths.

World.title: International News: Spanish Aid vessel delivers medical supplies to Cuba as humanitarian crisis deepens
World.content:
International News: Spanish Aid vessel delivers medical supplies to Cuba as humanitarian crisis deepens

By Zoila Palma: The Spanish humanitarian organization Open Arms has delivered seven tons of humanitarian aid to Cuba after its sailing vessel, Astral, arrived at the Port of Havana on Sunday.

The shipment, destined for the Juan Manuel Márquez Pediatric Hospital, includes solar panels, replacement batteries, and medical supplies aimed at strengthening critical healthcare services amid Cuba’s worsening economic and energy crisis, telesur reports.

The aid is part of the “Heading to Cuba” campaign, launched by Open Arms alongside more than 150 political and social organizations.

The vessel completed a 6,200-mile journey after departing Barcelona in May.

According to Open Arms, the mission was financed through donations from more than 4,000 supporters, raising over €160,000 (US$182,816).

The equipment will provide energy autonomy for the hospital’s intensive care unit, intermediate care unit, and clinical laboratory, helping to ensure essential medical services remain operational during frequent power outages.

World.title: Government of Belize expresses solidarity following ferry tragedy in Guyana
World.content:
Government of Belize expresses solidarity following ferry tragedy in Guyana

By Zoila Palma: On July 18, 2026, a ferry which departed from Georgetown, Guyana, carrying 116 passengers and 17 crew members, capsized in rough waves.

The latest reports indicate that 67 persons have been rescued, and a massive search-and-rescue effort is currently underway for those who remain missing.

“On behalf of the people of Belize, Hon. John Briceño and the Government of Belize extend prayers of hope for the safe rescue of those still missing off the coast of Guyana and offer comfort to the families awaiting the return of their loved ones,” a statement from the Government of Belize expressed.

The thoughts of the people of Belize are with the people of Guyana as they grapple with this tragedy.

World.title: Ministry of Education hosts STEAM Festival in San Ignacio, Cayo
World.content:
Ministry of Education hosts STEAM Festival in San Ignacio, Cayo

By Zoila Palma: On July 18, 2026, the Ministry of Education, Culture, Science and Technology held the first of its kind STEAM Festival in San Ignacio, Cayo.

The event showcased the potential of the Women in 4iR Component of the Skills for the Future Program as students presented their innovative solutions to community challenges using fundamental lessons in science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics (STEAM).

The Ministry says that this initiative creates targeted opportunities for young women to develop the critical knowledge, confidence, and technical skills necessary to thrive in the rapidly evolving landscape of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4iR).

Supported by the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) and the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), and developed in collaboration with the Education Development Center (EDC), the program aims to reach approximately 1,000 primary and secondary female students across Belize, actively encouraging them to pursue higher studies and sustainable career paths in STEAM.

World.title: Museum of Belize invites children to Maya Immersive Summer Camp 2026
World.content:
Museum of Belize invites children to Maya Immersive Summer Camp 2026

By Zoila Palma: The Museum of Belize and Houses of Culture is inviting parents to register their children for its Maya Immersive Summer Camp 2026, a week-long educational program designed to inspire Belize’s next generation of archaeologists.

Scheduled for July 20-24, 2026, the camp will give participants the opportunity to explore the museum’s Maya Creating Civilization Exhibit while taking part in interactive, hands-on learning experiences centered on Belize’s rich Maya heritage.

Campers will engage in a variety of activities, including Geology Meets Archaeology, Maya Mathematics and Trade, Ceramic Identification and 3D Models, a Maya Calendar lesson and craft, as well as games and other educational activities.

The program will run Monday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at the Museum of Belize, #8 Gabourel Lane, Belize City, and costs $15 per participant.

Those interested in learning more or registering their child can contact the Museum of Belize by calling 223-4524 or sending a WhatsApp message to 672-4264.

The camp is being organized in collaboration with the National Institute of Culture and History (NICH), the Institute of Archaeology, the Ministry of Natural Resources, and ITZAT STEAM Academy.

World.title: International News: Messi and Lamine Yamal share emotional moment after World Cup final
World.content:
International News: Messi and Lamine Yamal share emotional moment after World Cup final

By Zoila Palma: An emotional exchange between Lionel Messi and Spain’s teenage star Lamine Yamal has captured the attention of football fans worldwide following Sunday’s FIFA World Cup 2026 final.

Moments after Spain’s 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina in New York, Yamal approached Messi on the pitch, where the two shared a warm embrace and a few quiet words in a scene many described as a symbolic passing of the torch from one generation to the next.

The touching moment came after Spain secured its second World Cup title, with 19-year-old Yamal playing a key role throughout the tournament.

Messi, an eight-time Ballon d’Or winner, started the final for Argentina in what many believe could be his final appearance on football’s biggest international stage. The 39-year-old was visibly emotional after the defeat, lingering on the field as Spain celebrated its historic triumph.

The Argentine legend finishes his career with six World Cup appearances and 21 tournament goals, while Yamal’s rise continues to signal the arrival of a new era in world football.
