World.title: Scars of war linger on Syria’s Saint Simeon monastery
World.content:
Dayr Sim’ān – Near the base of a column atop which Saint Simeon Stylites once perched, scattered stones lay bare the damage inflicted on the surrounding Byzantine monastery in northern Syria by war, looting and rampant illegal excavations.

AFP accompanied a French archaeological delegation to inspect the site after more than a decade of conflict and assess what could be restored.

The fifth-century monastery and its church are, alongside hundreds of abandoned ancient villages in northern Syria known as the “dead” or “forgotten cities”, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Holding her camera and notebook, archaeologist Micheline Kurdi walked through the ruins to document the site’s state and plan the first “quick interventions” to restore it, she told AFP.

“There is irreparable damage in the monastery in the southeastern section, but on the other hand the church is standing firm and in good condition,” the 42-year-old French-Syrian said.

Inside the monastery, AFP journalists saw cracked arches and partially collapsed stone walls, while the monks’ living quarters remained intact.

– ‘Rebuild it’ –

Syria was once an archaeologist’s paradise, home to some of the oldest and best-preserved jewels of ancient civilisations.

Following the start of the civil war in 2011, archaeological sites across the country were damaged, museums looted and historic city centres levelled.

One of the most famous cases was Palmyra, the Roman-era city in Syria’s desert with an imposing kilometre-long colonnade, where the Islamic State jihadist group launched a campaign of destruction and looting after capturing the site in 2015.

The Saint Simeon monastery itself was subjected to “looting, illegal excavation, military use and neglect”, according to site director Abdel Jalil Arabi.

It was controlled by various armed groups throughout the war, he said.

An airstrike hit the monastery in 2016, which UNESCO condemned without naming the party responsible, while it was further damaged by a major earthquake in 2023.

Arabi estimated that 30 to 40 percent of the site has been damaged, pointing to the collapse of the western arch and its columns.

As for Saint Simeon’s column, Arabi said “the base is there, but the remains of the column are scattered, and we will try to rebuild it”.

The monastery, which includes one of the oldest major churches in Christianity, was built around a column that Saint Simeon sat on for years, dedicating his life to prayer.

Kurdi, who dedicated her doctoral thesis to the monastery complex, said they needed to “review old plans” to reinstall the base of the main column “and the part that remained of it”.

– Past and future –

Jean-Baptiste Faivre, French charge d’affaires in Syria, said “this heritage is extremely important, not only for Syria’s past but also for its future”.

“There will be cooperation between the Syrian Directorate-General of Antiquities and Museums and French cultural institutions to help restore and develop this site.”

Vincent Gelot from the French Catholic organisation Oeuvre d’Orient, who was also at the site, said the restoration would be carried out “with the support of donors and our partners, such as the French Embassy and the Aliph Foundation, which works to protect heritage in war-affected countries”.

“We hope that tourists and pilgrims will one day return to this place, because it still carries a message and speaks to us even today,” he added.

World.title: Plane carrying Spain’s World Cup winning team lands in Madrid
World.content:
Madrid – A plane carrying Spain’s newly crowned World Cup champions landed in Madrid on Monday, a day after their 1-0 victory over Argentina in the final in the United States.

A Spanish flag fluttered from the cockpit window as the Iberia aircraft carrying the squad taxied to the terminal at Madrid-Barajas airport at 14:30 local time (12:30 GMT) under clear blue skies.

Coach Luis de la Fuente was the first to step off the plane, followed by player of the tournament Rodri, who held the World Cup trophy aloft at the top of the stairs.

The squad were due to meet King Felipe VI at Zarzuela Palace outside Madrid before heading to the government headquarters at Moncloa Palace for a reception with Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.

The players and coaching staff will then parade through central Madrid on an open-top bus before arriving at the Cibeles square where a ceremony will be held.

Around one million people are expected to flood the streets of the Spanish capital to salute the players.

World.title: Iraqi forces destroy six ISIS hideouts in Kirkuk
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi military announced on Monday that Iraqi security forces had identified and destroyed six suspected hideouts belonging to ISIS in the northern province of Kirkuk during an air operation.

Iraq’s Joint Operations Command said in a statement that an airborne group of Special Forces carried out a rapid security operation early on Monday.

The hideouts were destroyed in precise airstrikes after field operations identified them in the Zghitun Valley area in Kirkuk, according to the statement.

The Kurdistan Region Security Agency (Asayish) also announced the arrest of two suspected ISIS militants in separate operations coordinated with Iraq’s Counter-Terrorism Service (CTS) in Sulaymaniyah province earlier in July.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: Economist: Dollar return is out of reach for restricted Iraqi banks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prominent economic expert Ziad Al-Hashemi issued a sobering analysis on Monday, July 20, 2026, regarding the recent joint understanding between the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) and the U.S. Department of the Treasury.

Al-Hashemi cautioned that the official statements do not imply an imminent return to U.S. dollar transactions for the restricted Iraqi financial institutions, describing full dollar integration as currently “out of reach” due to stringent compliance benchmarks.

The critique follows an announcement by the Central Bank of Iraq and a welcoming statement from Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi regarding a framework to qualify seven restricted Iraqi banks for a return to international correspondent banking channels.

While the government celebrated the milestone as a major leap forward for global financial integration, Al-Hashemi emphasized that the U.S. Treasury has explicitly conditioned the lifting of restrictions on a series of rigorous structural reforms that remain far from complete.

According to Al-Hashemi’s assessment of the official U.S. Treasury declaration, the transition for these restricted institutions will be heavily phased and contingent on challenging corporate governance overhauls:

Alternative Currencies Only: The initial phase of the agreement only explores re-integrating select banks into global correspondent networks using non-dollar currencies, such as the Euro, UAE Dirham, and Chinese Yuan.

Lack of American Correspondent Partners: To date, no restricted Iraqi bank has regained the ability to conduct foreign currency transactions, primarily because major U.S. banking institutions refuse to establish correspondent relationships with them.

The Structural Phase One: The first phase of the CBI-led banking reform initiative is scheduled to conclude this summer, but eligibility for alternative currencies remains strictly tied to meeting baseline governance and compliance standards.

The Stringent Path to the Dollar: To eventually handle U.S. dollars, banks must successfully complete all subsequent reform phases, pass a satisfactory third-party audit of their compliance functions, attract a qualified institutional investor, and meet international standards regarding professional competence, integrity, and fitness.

Ownership Restructuring Barriers: Domestic banks view these extensive conditions as exceptionally difficult to implement, with the U.S. Treasury’s strict mandates regarding bank ownership percentages posing the most significant structural hurdle.

Citing the formal documentation, Al-Hashemi highlighted the explicit security guardrails embedded within Washington’s fiscal policy toward Baghdad: “The United States will not tolerate the abuse of Iraqi banks by armed groups allied with Iran, and will take independent action, when necessary, to target such activities.”

Al-Hashemi noted that the primary misconception in the local market stems from confusing the allowance of alternative currency clearing with the lifting of the actual U.S. dollar ban. He asserted that it is highly improbable for these seven banks to enter the U.S. dollar transfer system over the short or medium term.

Beyond the lack of acceptance from institutional U.S. correspondent banks, the restricted Iraqi financial firms have failed to fully implement the comprehensive restructuring requirements mandated by the global consulting firm Oliver Wyman. The Oliver Wyman plan serves as the core technical benchmark for the Central Bank of Iraq’s broader strategy to modernize the domestic financial sector, increase corporate transparency, and combat money laundering and illicit financial flows.

Until these foundational auditing and ownership criteria are completely satisfied, Al-Hashemi concludes that the financial integration celebrated during the Washington summit will remain an idealized roadmap rather than an immediate commercial reality.

World.title: Ryanair quarterly profit slides on Mideast war impact
World.content:
London – Irish no-frills airline Ryanair on Monday said net profit slumped 34 percent in its first quarter as the Middle East conflict sent jet-fuel prices soaring and impacted ticket sales.

Profit after tax dropped to 538 million euros ($616 million) in the three months to the end of June, from 820 million euros one year earlier, the Dublin-based carrier said in a statement.

Ryanair, which is Europe’s biggest airline by passenger numbers and flies mainly across the continent, said the cost of fuel not subject to advance purchase agreements had soared owing to the US-Iran war.

“Operating costs rose 11 percent to 3.81 billion euros as the price of our 20-percent unhedged jet-fuel more than doubled” in the first quarter, chief executive Michael O’Leary said in the earnings statement.

While passenger traffic grew six percent, fares dropped six percent.

Fares “required stimulation as the Middle East conflict led to consumer hesitancy, concerns about EU jet-fuel shortages, economic uncertainty and later bookings”, O’Leary said.

He added that Ryanair’s net profit for the remainder of its financial year “remains highly sensitive to… conflict escalation in the Middle East and Ukraine, the price of unhedged jet-fuel, macro-economic shocks” and European air traffic control strikes.

Ryanair’s share price slid nearly six percent in Dublin midday trading after investors reacted to the bigger-than-expected drop in profits.

The airline’s “results show just how quickly nervousness surrounding the war has seeped into booking patterns and operational costs”, noted Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.

“It’s a sign that consumers are once again tightening their belts and delaying discretionary spending, leaving airlines exposed not just to soaring jet fuel costs but also the prospect of softer demand.”

World.title: Iraq leads Gulf oil exports growth despite Hormuz crisis
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq was one of the main drivers of the increase in crude oil exports from the Gulf region during the first half of July, according to shipping firms Kpler and Vortexa.

This development comes at a time when oil export levels from the region were at their peak since the outbreak of the US-Iran war in late February, despite reduced tankers’ movements in the Strait of Hormuz due to increased military operations.

Oil exports from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Iraq, Kuwait, and Iran increased by roughly 16 percent compared to June, hitting approximately 12 million barrels per day, according to Kpler, while Vortexa estimated the figure at 13.06 million barrels per day.

Iraq experienced the largest increase in oil shipments among the Gulf countries during that period, contributing significantly to the overall growth in crude exports alongside Saudi Arabia and Iran, according to Vortexa.

Despite this improvement, Reuters noted that oil shipments from the Gulf region are still approximately 32 percent below their pre-war level of 17.6 million barrels per day in February.

The number of oil tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz plummeted to three on a single day, the lowest level since May, raising fears about growing tensions and potential threats to Red Sea commerce, which might affect global oil flows.

World.title: Burnham becomes new UK PM after meeting king
World.content:
London – Andy Burnham became British prime minister Monday after meeting King Charles III at Buckingham Palace and was set to set out his vision for the country after taking over from Keir Starmer.

Starmer departed Downing Street on Monday morning, insisting in a farewell speech his two years in office had made Britain a better place.

The monarch met Starmer to accept his resignation and Burnham arrived next for the formal procedure in which the king asked him to form the next government and he accepted.

The 56-year-old is the sixth prime minister to enter Downing Street in the last 10 years.

“I am confident that Britain is now stronger and fairer than it was two years ago,” Starmer told reporters in his farewell speech outside his central London office.

“I go with good grace, I go with a smile, and I go proud of everything that we have achieved,” he added.

Burnham will face an in-tray overflowing with challenges with little time to make his mark.

In an interview with The Times published late Sunday, Burnham said he wanted to draw a line under a decade of political turmoil.

“What we’ve been doing hasn’t been working. That’s the way I see it,” he said.

“I am going to try and do things in a different way.”

In his first speech, Burnham will set out “priorities for restoring confidence in government and giving Britain more breathing room” amid the cost-of-living crisis, his team said.

Delivering growth and devolving power to regional communities are also expected to feature.

Also on Monday he is likely to announce his senior cabinet appointments, with all eyes on who will replace Rachel Reeves as finance minister.

The former mayor of Greater Manchester, nicknamed the “King of the North”, has been parachuted in by the Labour Party, after Starmer resigned last month, with MPs viewing him as the party’s best chance of reining in Nigel Farage’s anti-immigration Reform UK party.

– ‘Bigger, bolder’ –

Among Burnham’s most urgent challenges will be a tepid economy, high government borrowing costs, a ballooning welfare bill and irregular migrants arriving in small boats that have fuelled support for Reform.

Unpredictable energy prices due to the US-Iran war and a volatile American president in Donald Trump also threaten to buffet his premiership.

Burnham told The Times he would take a “different approach to public spending, and to running the economy — more focused on early investment, early intervention, setting people up for success, and much less paying for failure.”

He promised “early moves to help” with the cost of living, saying that while campaigning he heard the “pressure people feel around their finances”.

Starmer led Labour to power in July 2024 in a landslide election victory after 14 years of Conservative rule.

He announced that he would resign as prime minister and Labour Party leader in late June after a string of scandals, missteps and policy U-turns blighted his leadership.

But Burnham, who only returned as a member of parliament four weeks ago, has little room to manoeuvre amid sluggish economic growth, high public debt and strict financial rules requiring him to balance government spending against tax revenue.

– ‘Last chance’ –

Burnham was an MP between 2001 and 2017, serving as a minister in the governments of Tony Blair and Gordon Brown.

He has since reinvented himself as a man of the people, melding a relaxed, folksy style with slick social media videos.

But he has only three years to turn things around, with Reform leading in polls ahead of the next general election expected in 2029.

Burnham told supporters on Friday his Labour takeover was the “last chance” for the party to get things right.

Critics have accused Starmer’s government of being under-prepared for power when he was elected in July 2024.

Burnham has insisted he has a “plan”.

But his swift “coronation” as Labour leader has raised questions on how he will achieve his aims.

His first policy announcement came on Saturday when he scrapped Starmer’s flagship nationwide digital ID scheme, estimated to cost £1.8 billion over three years.

A spokesperson said the time and resources would be diverted “to where it’s most needed, such as helping with the cost of living”.

World.title: Boeing gets order for 100 737 MAX jets from leasing company SMBC
World.content:
Farnborough – US aircraft maker Boeing said Monday that it has received an order for 100 of its 737 MAX jets from leasing company SMBC Aviation Capital.

In the first major order to be announced at the Farnborough Air Show that opened in the UK on Monday.

The head of Boeing’s Commercial Airplanes division, Stephanie Pope, said that the order “reflects the strong demand we are seeing for the 737 MAX family’s efficiency, reliability and versatility”.

Following production quality issues, lawsuits, and an overhaul of its governance, the US company plans to stage a major comeback at Farnborough, just outside London.

The green light from the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) in October 2025 to lift the cap on production of the single-aisle 737 MAX, its best-selling aircraft, is seen as an important milestone.

It is also awaiting the certification — after several years of delays — of its three new aircraft.

SMBC’s order, the value of which has not been disclosed, covers 60 737-10 aircraft and 40 737-8 aircraft.

“Our partnership with Boeing goes back more than two decades, and this order reflects market momentum, as our airline and investor customers look to increase capacity with the 737-10,” said SMBC chief executive Peter Barrett.

“This order will support their growth ambitions well into the next decade and reflects our strong confidence in the Boeing 737 MAX and sustained demand for fuel-efficient, technologically advanced narrowbody aircraft,” he said.

The company, based in Dublin, Ireland, and described as the world’s leading aviation finance platform, manages a fleet of 1,700 aircraft for more than 170 airlines worldwide.

Boeing also announced Monday that Saudi carrier Riyadh Air is exercising options for 28 787 Dreamliners from an order placed in 2023, and will convert 20 options to the largest variant of this aircraft.

Riyadh Air has also “confirmed an order for six additional Airbus A350-1000s, bringing its firm commitment for this type of aircraft to 31,” said the European aircraft manufacturer, Boeing’s rival, in a separate statement.

World.title: 4 Indians killed, 1 critically injured after cargo ship attacked off Ukraine's Odesa coast
World.content:
.

NEW DELHI: At least four Indian nationals were killed and one was critically injured after the commercial vessel MV Golden Leo came under attack while departing Ukraine's port of Odesa on the evening of July 19, the ministry of external affairs said on Monday.In a statement, the MEA said there were 17 crew members on board the vessel, including five Indian nationals, when the attack took place."As per information available, four Indian nationals have tragically lost their lives, while one is hospitalized in a critical condition. Our Mission in Ukraine is closely monitoring the situation and is making every effort to extend all possible assistance to those affected," the ministry said.The MEA expressed its condolences to the families of those killed and wished the injured Indian national a speedy recovery."We extend our deepest condolences to the families of the deceased Indian nationals and wish the injured Indian national a speedy and full recovery," it said.The ministry condemned the attack, saying commercial shipping and civilian crew members should not be targeted."India condemns such attacks and reiterates that targeting commercial shipping and endangering innocent civilian crew members, or otherwise impeding freedom of navigation and commerce, is deplorable and should be avoided," the ministry said.

World.title: Who will ask if you’re home? The economy growing around urban loneliness
World.content:
From joint family to flat



The silver economy



The business of being heard



The small economies of a lonely weekend



Who will pay for connection?



India is the second-loneliest country in the world, according to a study by JB.com. The ranking offers a stark lens through which to view a country that is also aging rapidly, urbanising quickly and watching its traditional social structures thin out.In 2011, India had about 100 million people aged 60 and above. Projections by the Technical Group on Population Projections, cited in the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementationâs report Elderly in India 2021, show that this figure will more than double to roughly 230 million by 2036, around 15 per cent of the population. By 2050, UNFPAâs India Ageing Report 2023 estimates, nearly one in five Indians will be 60 or older.But loneliness is not waiting for old age.It is already present in the rented flats of young migrants, in the quiet of a single-person home, in weekends spent scrolling through other people's lives and in the small, almost invisible moments when there is no one to ask, âAre you home?âFor Minal, from Bihar and living alone in Pune, loneliness is âfeeling I donât belong anywhere and nobody cares about me.â She calls herself âpretty socialâ, but in her current city âhas only few people I know so I have phases when I go out alone.âA typical weekend is split between âone day I go out to eat somewhere nice and one day I stay in, cook something and journal or watch a movie.âAt home, she spends â8â10 hoursâ on screens. After closing Instagram and seeing peers travelling or getting engaged, she says she feels âempty and restless and also shit about myselfâ.Swadha, who spent years living alone in Noida for college and work, remembers the strange contradiction of returning home.âThere is a sense of reliefâ¦ but then there is also a sense of silence and nobody is there to ask are you homeâ¦ nobody cares whether you entered with the shoe on or have you left the shoe outside.âShe placed a mirror at the entrance of her home. âSomebody has to look at me, right? I used to do that for myself.âLiving alone, she says, âmeans you have absolutely no one to talk to about your dayâ¦ that will hit you so hard that it will push you away from your loved ones whom you actually speak to on the calls.âFor Neha, from West Bengal and working in Delhi, loneliness is even simpler: âno person to go back to when you feel heavyâ¦ no one to ask where you areâ¦ how have you been.âShe says she has âno social lifeâ. Her weekends are spent âgrocery shoppingâ¦ cooking and cleaningâ¦â. When she returns home, her first thought is, âwhat should I eat now.â She estimates her screen time at 4â5 hours a day at home and says that after closing social apps, she feels, âIâm wasting my timeâ¦ I should do something productive.âTheir lives may seem far removed from the concerns of India's elderly. But the emotional patterns are strikingly similar.A LASI-based study on later life reports that about 13.4 per cent of older Indians experience frequent loneliness. The odds are higher among those not in a marital union, those with more than two chronic conditions and those with small social networks or limited leisure activities. UNFPAâs 2023 report identifies social isolation and loneliness as key stressors on elderly mental health, aggravated by migration, urbanisation and weakening family support.The country is aging into this crisis.India's elderly population is not evenly distributed. Kerala's elderly share is projected to rise from about 13 per cent in 2011 to nearly 23 per cent by 2036, while Uttar Pradesh moves from roughly 7 per cent to 12 per cent. Southern states, Himachal Pradesh and Punjab already have above-average elderly proportions, creating pockets where ageing, and the risk of isolation, are much more intense than the national average.The profile is also sharply gendered.Using LASI data, government summaries note a sex ratio of roughly 1,065 females per 1,000 males among Indiaâs elderly, with women making up about 58 per cent of older persons. More than half of elderly women are widows. UNFPAâs ageing reports underline that older women are more likely to be widowed, have little personal income and live alone, increasing their vulnerability to economic insecurity and social isolation.This is the demographic stage on which India's loneliness economy is emerging.For generations, the family was India's first social safety net. That safety net has not disappeared, but it has changed shape.Migration, urbanisation, nuclear families and precarious work have moved millions away from the people and communities that once filled everyday life. A home that once had several generations may now have one person, one phone and a delivery app.The coping mechanisms are increasingly mediated by markets. Food delivery replaces the shared meal. OTT platforms fill the evening. Social media offers constant contact without necessarily providing companionship.For younger Indians, these services are conveniences. For an ageing population, they are becoming part of a much larger ecosystem of care.Policy has increasingly framed this demographic transition as an economic opportunity. NITI Aayogâs report Senior Care Reforms in India and the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowermentâs schemes speak of a âsilver economyâ built around the needs of older adults.Government estimates linked to the Senior Care Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE) initiative put the value of Indiaâs silver economy at around Rs 73,000 crore in 2024, with scope for multi-fold expansion as the elderly population grows.The first pillar is financial security.Atal Pension Yojana subscriptions rose from about 1.54 crore in March 2019 to 8.27 crore by October 2025, according to Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority data quoted in government briefs. Assets under management crossed Rs 49,000 crore.The Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme reaches around 2.21 crore beneficiaries, offering Rs 200 a month to those aged 60â79 and Rs 500 to those 80 and above. The amounts are modest, but they establish an income floor that can help with food, healthcare and basic services.The second pillar is health protection.Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY offers Rs 5 lakh a year in hospitalisation cover to vulnerable households. In October 2024, the government announced free treatment benefits of up to Rs 5 lakh annually for about 6 crore senior citizens aged 70 and above from 4.5 crore families, irrespective of socio-economic status. More than 40 lakh seniors had enrolled by January 2025.The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly, meanwhile, now covers all 713 health districts, with geriatric OPDs, wards and physiotherapy services, according to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.The third pillar is care.The SAGE portal invites start-ups to develop solutions in healthcare, housing, technology and social engagement, offering equity support of up to Rs 1 crore per project, with government equity capped at 49 per cent. The Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens grants fund 696 senior citizen homes across 29 States and UTs, with 84 more selected for 2025â26.A geriatric caregiver training scheme, run through 32 empanelled institutes, trained 36,785 caregivers in 2023â24.None of these programmes is explicitly called a loneliness programme. Yet they address many of the conditions that make loneliness more likely: widowhood, frailty, financial insecurity and living alone.Technology is becoming another layer of this support system.The government's e-Sanjeevani telemedicine platform has delivered nearly 14 crore tele-consultations nationwide, including more than 1 crore consultations involving senior citizens, according to a 2023 Press Information Bureau update and a national telemedicine assessment.For an older person who cannot easily travel, a consultation through a screen can be a lifeline. But the broader shift is significant too: an increasing number of needs, including emotional ones, are now being addressed through digital interfaces.Elderline 14567 offers senior citizens a telephone channel for grievances, abuse and emotional support, connecting callers to local services and authorities.The legal framework, meanwhile, continues to place responsibility on families. The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, and its 2019 amendment bill expand the definition of âchildrenâ and âparentsâ, remove the Rs 10,000 cap on maintenance, mandate that seniors should live a âlife of dignityâ and require dedicated police units and geriatric facilities in hospitals.The amendment widens âmaintenanceâ to include healthcare, safety and housing. It is an acknowledgement that neglect, isolation and abuse are not merely private tragedies.But loneliness is not always about being physically alone.Anandeshwar, a civil services aspirant from Uttar Pradesh now living in Delhi, describes it as ânot being understood or connected to the people around me, even when I am surrounded by others.âHe has âa big enough circle of friendsâ but meets them rarely. Deeper conversations happen âpine ke baadâ (after drinking). His ideal weekend is full: âwrite some good things, spend time with friends, participate in debating eventsâ. Reality is often different. He stays home, âwatch YT, Twitter, or just lay on the bed smoking,â joking that âevery day is weakened for an unemployed.âThe problem, then, is not simply the absence of people. It is the absence of meaningful connection.Loneliness often reveals itself through small choices.Cook or order in? Call someone or scroll? Go out or stay in bed?Minal divides her weekend between eating out and cooking at home. Neha's ideal weekend is âreading, writing and cleaning the flatâ, even if reality is often errands and rest.Yukta, a psychology student from Bengaluru living in Jaipur, describes a more connected version of the same urban life. When she is not overwhelmed by work, weekends with her roommate mean âsleep, cooking and eating good food together, watching something fun on an OTT platform, orâ¦ a movie and cafe date! And shopping or just strolling through a bazaar for fun.ââNow, it feels like âI am finally homeâ,â she says. âI can do whatever Iâd like, be whatever Iâd like and just exist in a space with only comfort to offer.âLASI-based studies identify regular social contact, leisure activities, yoga or meditation and even moderate television or computer use as factors associated with better wellbeing among older adults.The difference is that in cities such as Delhi, Pune, Hyderabad and Jaipur, these activities are increasingly curated through markets: OTT subscriptions, cafes, delivery services and paid experiences.At the other end is Srabastee from West Bengal, living in Delhi for work.âItâs feeling like no one really knows whatâs going on in your head, even when youâre surrounded by peopleâ¦ when you have something exciting or heartbreaking to share and canât think of anyone to call.âShe speaks to family and âtexts a few friends once in a whileâ, mostly sharing memes and reacting to stories. Weeks can pass before they meet.After scrolling, she often feels âdrainedâ, comparing her routine weekends of laundry, shows and ordered food with peers who seem to be âgetting promoted, buying homes, getting married, travelling the world.âThe same platforms that offer entertainment and convenience also fuel comparison. The same screens that connect people can deepen the feeling of being left behind.NITI Aayog argues that senior care needs to be recognised as a distinct sector, with regulations, standards, public-private partnerships and dedicated financing. Its vision combines public programmes such as pensions, NPHCE, telehealth and senior homes with private start-ups and NGOs.That is where the silver economy begins to overlap with the loneliness economy.The forces making Minal, Neha and Srabastee feel alone, migration, nuclear families, precarious jobs and digital overload, are also creating demand for therapy platforms, senior-living communities, companion-care services and digital communities.Some of these services may offer genuine support. Others may simply monetise a need that was once met by family, neighbours and community.The question becomes sharper when viewed against India's place near the top of the global loneliness index. A country ranked number two by JB.com is also preparing for a dramatic rise in its elderly population. By 2036, roughly 230 million Indians will be 60 or older. By 2050, nearly one in five will be.The challenge is not only how to feed, house or medically care for this population. It is also how to ensure that people have someone to talk to, someone who notices when they do not come home, someone who asks how their day was.India's loneliness economy is already taking shape, from pensions and senior homes to helplines, telehealth, therapy platforms, cafes, OTT subscriptions and delivery apps.The question is whether connection will ultimately be treated as a public responsibility or sold as another subscription.Because the people who today spend their Sundays between grocery stores and glowing screens will one day grow old. And the way India responds to their loneliness will reveal whether it sees the need to be seen, heard and remembered as a basic human need, or simply another market waiting to be tapped.

World.title: 'Hopefully govt will fix accountability': Sonam Wangchuk to continue his hunger strike
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Climate activist

on Monday said that that he has decided to continue his hunger strike after seeing the brutality on peaceful protestors marching to the Parliament.

In a handwritten note, Wangchuk said that the his hunger strike will continue until Cockroach Janata Party leaders are allowed to meet MPs at the Parliament or he is allowed to meet them at Safdarjung Hospital.

"Seeing the brutality with which peacefully protesting Youth are being dealt with, I have decided to continue my fast until the youth leaders are allowed to meet the Parliamentarians at the Sansad Bhawan or I am allowed to meet them here at the Hospital," Wangchuk said.

"Hopefully government will fix accountability of Education minister before that," he added.

He also appealed to the government and Delhi Police to allow the protesting students to present their grievances before the Parliament.

"I am touched & moved by how the youth have held on to peace despite provocation and I appeal to the Govt & Police force to resolve the issue by simply allowing the students to present their grievances before the Parliament today or tomorrow," Wangchuk said.

"I'm sure the young protesters will show the same patience and tolerance tomorrow as they did today," he added.

This comes hours after a delegation of CJP met Union minister JP Nadda and submitted its petition demanding accountability from the government over the NEET-UG paper leak case.





According to CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka, the meeting with Nadda was under way, with the Union minister seeking time to consult the government leadership on the party's demands.

The demands include the immediate release of activist Sonam Wangchuk, the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, and Rs 1 crore compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide.

This comes as thousands tried to march to Parliament as part of the Cockroach Janta Party's protest call to demand the former's resignation over alleged examination irregularities.

Outside Parliament, police used tear gas and mild force after demonstrators allegedly attempted to breach barricades and march towards the Parliament complex. Several protesters were detained.

Security was tightened across central Delhi, with Rapid Action Force personnel deployed at key locations to prevent any breach. As a precautionary measure, several gates at Metro stations in the area were temporarily closed, affecting commuters.

At least seven CJP protesters, including Abhijeet Dipke, were detained near the Reserve Bank of India, close to Parliament, during the party's 'Sansad Chalo' march, PTI reported.

World.title: DS Group launches Pallu Protection PPE to shield women farmers from pesticide exposure
World.content:
.

DS Group has launched an initiative to reduce occupational health risks faced by women farmers from exposure to agricultural pesticides and chemicals, rolling out awareness activities and a culturally tailored protective solution in seven villages of Baghpat district.The programme, part of the companyâs FarmHER initiative, is currently being implemented in Pali, Katha, Bandpur, Sunehra, Basi, Mavikala and Sankrodh. It combines community education, preventive health services and distribution of a practical protective product designed for women who commonly use saree pallus or dupattas while working in the fields.As part of the campaign, DS Group introduced a washable nano-fibre filter â marketed as the Pallu Protection Equipment (PPE) filter â that can be stitched into a saree pallu or dupatta to act as a barrier against pesticide particles, dust, harmful chemicals and PM2.5 pollutants. The filters will be made available free of charge through selected tailor shops, pesticide outlets and chemist stores across the seven villages.The company said the intervention was informed by field research which found many women already use pallus or dupattas as informal protection, despite their limited effectiveness. A male version of the product, designed to be integrated into the traditional gamcha, has also been developed.DS Groupâs outreach in the villages includes mobile awareness vans, traditional puppet shows, nukkad nataks (street plays), door-to-door education and free health camps. The health camps provide blood pressure and blood sugar screening, basic counselling and distribution of PPE masks. Women participating in the programme also receive mirrors and calendars bearing messages about safer farming practices.âWomen farmers play a vital role in Indiaâs agricultural economy, yet awareness of the occupational health risks they face remains limited,â said Rajeev Jain, Senior Vice President, Corporate Marketing, DS Group. âOur field research revealed that the saree pallu and dupatta are often used as informal protective coverings during pesticide-intensive agricultural work, despite offering inadequate protection. This highlights the urgent need for simple, practical and culturally appropriate solutions that women farmers can seamlessly adopt.âDS Group said the initiative aims to bridge the gap between awareness and action by providing accessible, culturally relevant interventions to protect womenâs health and encourage safer, more sustainable farming practices as part of its broader FarmHER programme.

World.title: Trainee IPS officer, accused of sexual harassment by colleague, hospitalised after suspected suicide attempt
World.content:
Representative image

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: A trainee IPS officer, who was booked for allegedly stalking and sexually harassing a fellow trainee at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy (SVPNPA) in Hyderabad, was hospitalised on Monday following a suspected suicide attempt, police said.According to a doctor who treated him, the trainee officer was brought to a private hospital in an unconscious state by his brother and friends, who suspected that he had consumed a harmful substance.The doctor added that a stomach wash was performed, but no "abnormal" substance was found.The trainee officer's blood and urine samples have been sent for tests, while his vital parameters remain stable.Although he was unconscious when brought to the hospital, he is now drowsy. The doctor added that further details would emerge after he regains full consciousness and the test reports are received.An alcohol bottle and a sanitizer bottle were found near his bed, according to the doctor, who cited the trainee officer's brother.The case stems from a complaint filed by a 30-year-old woman trainee IPS officer, who accused her fellow trainee of stalking and sexually harassing her. She alleged that he had been sending sexually abusive messages through an instant messaging app since June 23 and making derogatory remarks about her in front of her colleagues.The complainant claimed that the officer falsely accused her of having a relationship with another trainee and pressured her to admit to it, while using abusive language.She further alleged that on July 9, he restrained her, took her to his room by force, pulled her hair, attempted to strangle her, and held a knife to her neck, preventing her from leaving. She also accused him of assaulting her the following day.The woman alleged that the officer recorded a private video of her without consent and sent it to her husband in an attempt to blackmail her.Based on the complaint, a case was registered at Attapur police station on July 18 under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including charges related to assault or criminal force against a woman, sexual harassment, stalking, and insulting the modesty of a woman, along with provisions of the Information Technology Act, police said.The trainee IPS officer denied the allegations in a social media post, calling the complaint and rumours against him "baseless and untrue.""I fully trust the legal process and believe justice will prevail," he wrote.A police official said investigators would issue a notice asking him to appear in connection with the case.Following the registration of the case, the trainee officer left the academy, according to sources. He had earlier served as a constable in Andhra Pradesh.

World.title: 'Disgusting what government is doing': Rahul Gandhi slams police action against protesters; shares video
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress MP and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha

on Monday called Prime Minister

the 'most youth-hostile Prime Minister in India's history'.

He also criticised the use of tear gas and lathi charge against students protesting the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, saying they were only demanding a fair education system.

In a video statement shared on X, Rahul alleged that students protesting for a fair education system were being treated like criminals instead of being heard.

"This country has a majority of young people. Prime Minister Modi is the most anti-youth Prime Minister India has ever had. The boys and girls who are walking the streets of Delhi are not criminals. They are demanding their rights. Their rights are to have an education system that respects them, an education system that is fair and an education system that is working," Rahul said.

He criticised the police action against protesters, saying, "There is absolutely nothing wrong in what they are doing. It is disgusting what the government is doing and what the police is doing. Tear-gassing students and lathi-charging students is not democratic. It is not India's way and it is not the way this should be done."

Rahul said the protesters' demands were legitimate and urged the Prime Minister to act on them.





"The Prime Minister should accept these demands and do something about it. Everybody is sick and tired of the way our education system is running. Everybody is sick and tired of how the RSS has captured our education system and how all our institutions are being run by one organisation," he said.

Claiming that the Congress had been raising concerns over the education system for years, Rahul added, "This is a natural response that the young people of India are making and it should be respected.

We've been raising this issue not for weeks or months. We've been raising it for years. There's a fundamental problem and Modi disrespects all the young people of this country. All they believe in is Asatya and Hinsa, which are anti-Indian principles.

"

In a separate post on X, Congress MP alleged that PM Modi had failed to act against Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan despite repeated examination controversies.

"Prime Minister Modi is the most youth-hostile Prime Minister in India's historyâso youth-hostile that he can't even demand the resignation of a failed Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan," Gandhi wrote.

He further claimed, "152 paper leaks. 7.5 crore students victimised. And not a single guilty person punished. Who got the punishment? The hardworking youth."

Referring to the police action, Lok Sabha LoP said, "When these children raised legitimate questions about education, they were met with batons and detention.

The criminals who leaked the papers roam free, while the students raising valid issues are dragged around and beaten. This government isn't just failing the youthâit is pouncing on them."

His remarks came as the protests intensified outside Parliament, where members of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) attempted to march towards Parliament demanding accountability over the alleged paper leak and the resignation of Pradhan.

Delhi Police used mild force to disperse protesters after they attempted to breach barricades. Police said several personnel were injured during the clashes after stones were allegedly thrown at security personnel.

Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also criticised the police action, questioning why students protesting over issues related to the education system were being met with tear gas and baton charges.

Delhi Police, meanwhile, denied claims by the CJP that its founder Abhijeet Dipke had been detained during the protest, saying he was 'available on stage' and dismissing reports of his detention as 'entirely false.'

Security remained tightened across New Delhi as prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) continued to remain in force.

World.title: Fresh landslide kills seven in rain-ravaged Poonch, J&K toll rises to 17
World.content:
NEW DELHI: At least seven people were killed after a landslide struck a mud house in Jammu and Kashmir's rain-hit Poonch district on Monday, officials said.

The latest incident occurred in the higher reaches of Loran village, where a mud house was buried under debris following the landslide.

Among those killed were four women, officials said.

Rescue operations are under way at the site.

Officials said Poonch has been battered by torrential rain since Saturday evening. With the latest incident, 17 people have lost their lives in the district, while six others remain missing.

In a separate operation, a joint team of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and the Indian Army carried out a rescue and recovery operation to retrieve a body from the Munawar River in the Nowshera area of Rajouri district.

The fresh tragedy comes a day after torrential rain triggered flash floods and landslides across the Pir Panjal region, killing at least 14 people and leaving several others trapped under debris.

Chief minister Omar Abdullah cut short his visit to New Delhi and flew to Jammu on Sunday to oversee relief and rescue operations. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha also reviewed the situation and directed officials to provide immediate assistance to affected families.





The heavy rain also disrupted traffic on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway and led to the temporary suspension of the annual Amarnath Yatra and pilgrimages to the Vaishno Devi shrine and Shiv Khori after the India Meteorological Department forecast more adverse weather.

Rescue operations involving the Army, police, SDRF, NDRF, civil administration and local volunteers are continuing in the worst-affected areas of Poonch and Rajouri as authorities search for the missing and assess the damage.

World.title: Evening news wrap: CJP delegation meets JP Nadda as protest intensifies, Andy Burnham becomes UK's new PM & more
World.content:
.

CJP leaders met Union minister JP Nadda, demanding Sonam Wangchuk's release, Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and compensation for families of NEET aspirants, while the minister assured them he would discuss the demands with the government.

, forcing multiple adjournments in both Houses. The Delhi high court sought Sonam Wangchuk's complete medical records and directed doctors to appear before it before deciding on his plea to shift to a private hospital.

World.title: Krishna Byre Gowda targets ‘paper plantation’ in Bengaluru
World.content:
As a mandatory exercise, the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) took up the planting of one lakh trees every year, with a budget earmarked for the initiative.

However, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said that the implementation has remained only on paper over the years. He said on Monday during a meeting with officials of the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), “Every year, when the public questions the civic body, it says that it is planting trees in the city, but we cannot see them at all.”

According to the tree census data, Bengaluru has over 20 lakh trees, many of which are age-old. “If the civic body is planting one lakh trees every year, then where have those trees gone? There should have been lakhs of trees by now,” he argued.

According to the Minister, the civic body has not been carrying out the exercise in full but has been showing on paper that it is being done, owing to a lack of accountability and improper documentation. “Tenders don’t happen on time or adequately, which means only a few saplings are planted every year while the records show that the works have been completed,” he said.

Mr. Gowda directed that before any tree is felled for development works undertaken by the corporation, metro, or any other government department, the agency concerned must pay the Forest Department the cost of planting ten saplings for every tree that is removed.

According to GBA data available with The Hindu, 8,689 trees have been felled by the civic body over the last three financial years for development projects, while 86 have been felled in the last three months. In addition, 1,032 trees have been removed for other reasons.

According to GBA officials, the recommendations of the Tree Expert Committee have been taken wherever necessary before felling, and compensatory plantation has been carried out. But Mr. Gowda said, “Citizens are unable to see where the trees are being planted.”

He also acknowledged that poor-quality tree species have been planted in the past, which would be corrected this time, and that only high-quality saplings would be planted this year. He said hardwood species would be prioritised.

Following the massive uprooting of trees across the city during the recent rains, The Hindu had reported on the need for hardwood tree species in Bengaluru, highlighting that softwood species accounted for more than 95% of the uprooted trees.

Mr. Gowda stressed that the tree plantation drive is essential for the survival and future of Bengaluru, as it helps regulate temperature and improve the Air Quality Index. The plantation drive must go beyond paperwork and be implemented in its true spirit, he said, adding that the civic body must take responsibility for nurturing the saplings.

World.title: Bhatti Vikramarka inaugurates Integrated Oil Palm Complex, calls oil palm an assured source of income even during drought
World.content:
Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka on Monday said oil palm cultivation offers farmers assured income even during adverse conditions such as El Nino and drought, reaffirming the government’s continued support to promote the crop.

He was speaking after inaugurating Godrej Agrovet Limited’s ₹300-crore Integrated Oil Palm Complex, claimed to be India’s first-of-its-kind facility, at Anjanapuram village in Konijerla mandal of Khammam district.

Agriculture Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao, Godrej Industries Group Chairperson Nadir Godrej and others were present.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Vikramarka said Khammam district is synonymous with agriculture and farming is the backbone of the local economy. He urged farmers to take oil palm cultivation for higher productivity and better returns.

He noted that India produces only 12 lakh metric tonnes of palm oil against an annual requirement of around 25 lakh metric tonnes, resulting in heavy imports and foreign exchange outflow.

Stating that oil palm cultivation has expanded to nearly three lakh acres since its introduction in 1991-92, he said the price of Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFBs) has increased from around ₹12,500 per tonne in 2023 to nearly ₹23,000 per tonne today, reflecting the growing economic value of the crop.

He said the integrated facility spread over 113 acres, houses R&D, seed genetics, nurseries, milling and refining units, and will boost oil palm cultivation besides transforming Khammam into a major agro-based industrial hub.

World.title: Graduation ceremony in TVMCH; 250 students receive degrees
World.content:
A total 250 students of Tirunelveli Medical College received their degrees from District Collector Anand Mohan in the 56th graduation ceremony held on Saturday night.

Fifteen students, who bagged university ranks, were honoured with medals.

Former Deans of TVMCH Sithi Athiya Munavara, M. Ravichandran, S.M. Kannan, Dean of Thoothukudi Government Medical College Hospital Ebenezer Joel Kumar and others participated.

World.title: Current politics will not allow a Kapu leader to become CM of A.P., says MLC Somu Veerraju
World.content:
Member of Legislative Council (MLC) Somu Veerraju has said the current political environment does not allow any leader from the Kapu community to become the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.

Speaking at an event held here on Monday to pay tributes to Kapu leaders Mudragada Padmanabham and G.S. Rao, Mr. Veerraju, a former president of the Bharatiya Janata Party State unit, said, “We, the Kapu community, need to deeply understand today’s politics in Andhra Pradesh that will not let any Kapu leader become the Chief Minister. Everybody needs to introspect why towering personalities from the community are not being allowed to join the parties, including the BJP.'’

The Kapu community unit in the city organised the event in memory of former MP, four-time MLA and former Minister Mudragada Padmanabham, who passed away on July 14, and Kovvuru-based former president of Kapu Nadu and AP Congress Committee G.S. Rao, who died on July 11.

Remembering his association with Padmanabham, Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Council and YSRCP leader Botcha Satyanarayana said the duo had witnessed many struggles during their political journey.

Referring to the movement led by Padmanabham for the cause of Kapu community, Mr. Satyanarayana said the community needed to continue its struggle for rights. “In today’s democracy, nothing comes by begging and whatever is needed should be taken,” he said.

MLC Thota Trimurthulu, a close aide of Padmanabham, appealed to the Kapu community to draw inspiration from the struggles of Padmanabham to achieve reservation for the community. “The real tribute to Padmanabham is to revive his movement for the reservation. In Vijayawada, a high-level meeting should be held with Kapu leaders from across the State to decide a plan of action to take forward the social movement of Padmanabham,” said Mr. Trimurthulu.

YSRCP leader Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy hailed the honesty and uncompromising attitude of Padmanabham.

Kapu leaders Jakkampudi Raja, Jakkampudi Ganesh, Ambati Rambabu, Kurasala Kannababu, and senior YSRCP leaders offered floral tributes to the portraits of Padmanabham and G.S. Rao.

World.title: Five arrested in Guntur for murders linked to missing persons cases
World.content:
Tadikonda police arrested five persons for murder allegedly committed in connection with a robbery linked to a missing person case. During interrogation, the accused also allegedly confessed to their involvement in another murder linked to a separate missing person case, police said on Monday.

According to Guntur Superintendent of Police (SP) Vakul Jindal, the investigation was conducted using scientific and technical evidence. Police said that the prime accused, Devarakonda Nageswara Rao alias Omkar, along with Gujjarlapudi Samuel alias Simon, Kanaparthi Manikanta, Gattamaneni Pushpa and Devalla Padmala, allegedly conspired to rob real estate businessman Madugula Sankara Rao of Phanidharam village after learning about his financial status.

The accused allegedly lured the victim under the pretext of purchasing land at Yadlapadu, procured SIM cards from other States, hired a car and purchased ropes and binding wire in advance. On July 7, they allegedly strangled Sankara Rao near Vankayalapadu village, robbed him of four gold rings, a gold chain and ₹72,000 in cash, and dumped his body in a quarry pit near Pothuru after tying it to a cement fencing pole. They later used the victim's mobile phone to mislead his family before destroying the SIM card.

During interrogation, the accused also allegedly confessed to another murder involving Nagaraju of Vengalayapalem. Police said Omkar, Bannu and Manikanta reportedly admitted to taking Nagaraju in a car, killing him en route and disposing of his body in the Sagar Right Canal near Macherla.

Following a complaint from Nagaraju's parents, police had earlier registered a missing person case at the Nallapadu police station. Police said that further investigation into both the cases was in progress after the seizure of the car, mobile phones, cash and other incriminating material.

World.title: NEET-UG: Submitting fake OMR sheets for scrutiny will invite legal action, says NTA
World.content:
In the wake of many Optical Mark Recognition (OMR) sheets submitted for scrutiny turning out to be fake or AI-generated, students and parents are advised to submit only original OMRs for scrutiny, the National Testing Agency (NTA) stated on Monday (July 20, 2026).

“Any fake or AI-generated OMR may invite legal action against the complainant. NTA is closely scrutinising and monitoring all complaints,” the agency has further said.

It has come to the notice of the National Testing Agency that images of OMR answer sheets said to be the “correct” record of certain candidates who appeared in NEET(UG) 2026 are being circulated on social media, in support of claims that the results declared against those candidates are wrong, NTA further said.

NTA has stated that the agency verifies records in all such cases — the genuine OMR sheet of every candidate bearing the correct roll number, test booklet number, answer sheet barcode and serial, test booklet code and the candidate’s own name and parentage in the candidate’s own hand, together with signature and thumb impression of the candidate and the two invigilators, is held on record with NTA. “It was made available to the candidate at the registered e-mail address and on the candidates portal,” NTA claimed in the statement.

In case of claims made by a candidate Arya Singh, NTA stated that the genuine OMR sheet of the candidate is with NTA. “It was also emailed to her at the registered e-mail address during the OMR Response Key Challenge window. The image being circulated is a digitally altered version of that same sheet. The recorded time of signature of one of the invigilators has been changed from 3.45 p.m. on the genuine sheet to 2.45 p.m. on the altered image. There are several other markings of digital alteration on the forged OMR sheet,” NTA stated on X. “The score of 167 marks is verified and stands as declared.”

In another case of a claim by a candidate Lakshya Singh, the Central agency has stated that the image being circulated shows response markings that are not present on the genuine sheet. Additional bubbles have been shaded in digital means to create a forged OMR sheet. Of 180 questions, the candidate attempted 54 (34 correct, 20 incorrect) and left 126 unattempted. The score of 116 marks is verified and stands as declared.

Meanwhile, Lakshya Singh’s relative claimed that NTA had not given any OMR sheet over the mail previously, and that there was no download option on the login portal. “Now we have to fight a legal case with NTA, as in it is our kid who has forged things or it is NTA’s mismanagement or loophole deliberate or indeliberate,” Mr. Singh’s aunt Purva Bhargava stated on X.

In the case of a candidate named Avaneesh Srivastava, NTA has stated that the image being circulated is not an OMR sheet issued by NTA. The identity inserted into that image (Ajeet Singh, son of Lakhan Singh and Smt. Reena Singh) does not correspond to any candidate registered with NEET(UG) 2026. No candidate by that name and parentage exists in the NEET(UG)2026 database.

The image is a digitally regenerated version of the candidate’s own genuine OMR sheet. The identity fields have been overwritten, and the printed portion of the sheet has been regenerated by AI or OCR-based tools, producing visible errors on portions of the genuine OMR sheet and cannot be altered by any candidate with a pen. The candidates own OMR sheet on record has been evaluated and score of 337 marks is verified and stands declared, NTA stated on X.

The score declared against all such candidates is fully consistent with that OMR answer sheet, the official answer key notified for NEET(UG) 2023 and the calculation sheet on file, there is no evaluation error, the agency mentioned.

The images being circulated as the correct OMR are not documents issued by NTA. They are digitally manipulated versions of the candidates own genuine OMR answer sheets. The alterations observed in the cases examined range from the introduction of additional response markings to the alteration of names and of the authenticated signature time of an invigilator amount others.

The creation submission or circulation of a fabricated digitally altered or otherwise forged OMR answer sheet is a cognisable offence under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means)Act 2024 and separately attracts liability under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and the IT Act, 2000, NTA has further said in an official statement.

Candidates with genuine grievances are advised to follow the process set out in NTA’s public notice dated July 20, 2026 available on NTA website.

World.title: Southwest monsoon failure strangulates farming in Tirunelveli, tourism in Tenkasi districts
World.content:
The belied southwest monsoon this year has smothered farming operations in Tirunelveli district while landing excruciating punch on neighbouring Tenkasi district’s tourism industry, which would usually be bustling with activities during this season every year.

Since the southwest monsoon would bring in copious influx of water into the dams of Tirunelveli and Tenkasi districts, it would be deciding the fate of ‘kar’ paddy season every year. After this monsoon played truant this year, the precarious storage level in the dams, especially in Manimuthar and Papanasam dams, has discouraged the agriculturists from going in for ‘kar’ paddy cultivation.

The farmers have so far raised agricultural crops, including paddy on only 5,676.98 hectares and the horticultural crops on 663.86 hectare, mostly in Vickramasingapuram, Ambasamudram, Kallidaikurichi and Cheranmahadevi areas as the farmers having their holdings in Tirunelveli or Palayamkottai are sceptical about their fortune due to poor rainfall.

Even though water has been released from the Papanasam and Manimuthar Dams, paddy or banana has been raised only in the areas closer to the reservoirs like Vickramasingapuram, Ambasamudram, Kallidaikurichi and Cheranmahadevi areas. And, paddy procurement centres have been opened only in these areas – Paappaakudi, Therkku Kallidaikurichi, Ayansingampatti, Therkku Paappaankulam, Therkku Veeravanallur, Poongudaiyarkulam, Vadamalaisamudhram, Thediyoor and Sengulam.

“The farmers, who have already been hit hard by the skyrocketing prices of chemical fertilizers and the pesticides, cannot take chances with poor storage in the dams. So, I’ve decided to wait for the next season – ‘pisanam’ paddy season between November and February in the northeast monsoon,” says farmer Maharajan of Palayamkottai.

As most of the agriculturists are very much confident that there would be no rainfall during this season, vast tracts of lands in Tirunelveli and beyond are barren now.

The southwest monsoon, which would usually bring heavy flow of water in all waterfalls of Courtallam and thereby ensure huge earnings from thousands of tourists from various parts of southern India towards this tiny town, has let down the business completely this year.

“It is unprecedentedly hot here in Courtallam this year. Even the tourists, who would usually stay here at least for 2 days to enjoy bath in the waterfalls of Courtallam and the Paalaruvi in neighbouring Kerala, and electrifying weather here, wind-up their tour prematurely within a day due to poor flow of water in the Main Falls, Five Falls and the Old Courtallam Falls. Cancellations of rooms are hitting hard everyday the hotels, resorts and those who rent out 2 or 3 BHK houses to the tourists. There is no need to explain about the business loss to the eateries, teashops, autorickshaws and other small businesses in Courtallam,” says R. Selva Murugan, a cab driver from Tenkasi.

Barring the bowl-like Gundar Dam, the smallest of the 5 reservoirs of Tenkasi district with the storage level of just 36 feet, all other dams have lesser water which will not be sufficient for irrigation of the paddy raised in the district during this ‘kar’ season.

“This is very much disappointing... While tourism has suffered huge blow, the farmers are not prepared to gamble. Even the district administration has decided to organise the ‘Saaral Vizhaa 2026’ only for 5 days which would usually be an 8-day affair. So, the southwest monsoon this year has become a disastrous experience for us,” said a senior official attached to the Department of Agriculture.

World.title: CJP protest in Delhi LIVE: Jantar Mantar stage dismantled after Parliament march; protesters to stay put, as Wangchuk vows to continue fast
World.content:
Activist Sonam Wangchuk announced on Monday (July 20, 2026) that he would continue his indefinite hunger strike, saying the police action against protesters during the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) “ Sansad Chalo” march has prompted him to extend the fast until youth leaders are allowed to meet parliamentarians or he is permitted to do so from the hospital.
